🦆 LPCC Duck Report — 13-19 August 2026 🥇

9 ducks
Week 18 · 13 Aug 2026 – 19 Aug 2026
A properly productive week for the exclusive zero club: nine ducks laid across eight fixtures, seven of them on Saturday alone. Let's tour the grounds. Saturday 15 August 1st XI v Mersham Sports CC (h) Jordan Austin opened both the innings and the day's misery, ct Katie Jordan b Ashley Cook for his 3rd of the season and 53rd career duck — 14th on the all-time list, with Duck of the Year 2021 and Diamond Duck honours already banked. On this very day in 1964, John Thirkell (1943-1977, 90 ducks, five-time Duck of the Year) was also dismissed for nought, so Jordan keeps fine calendar company. Will Hughes (b Anurag Mhatre) brought up his 7th career duck, drawing level with current campaigner Daniel Baker on the same tally. A paid-up Debutante Duck club member from his actual debut, long since filed away. Thomas Beeney (b James Rand) notched a 9th duck of the season — 58th career, 10th all-time — and with a Duck of the Year 2026 board entry already secured, he isn't just topping this season's charts, he's defending the crown in real time. 2nd XI v Tonbridge CC (a) Aaron Hughes, ct Prendergast b Batley off just 3 balls, opens his season account and moves to 21 career ducks, level with Dave Todd (1978-2014). Tidy symmetry: his kin Will Hughes was also walking back for nought the very same Saturday, one XI over. 3rd XI v Rodmersham CC (a) Nolan Wilde, ct Linder b Thompson, takes his 4th of the season and 25th career, drawing level with Dave Charlton (1988-2018). 4th XI v New Ash Green CC (h) Mohamed Safeer Ibra Lebbe (lbw b Mick Sumner) already has 3 ducks this season from just 3 career innings — an early and thorough education in the art of not scoring. Gene Smith (b Daryl Horton) reaches 4 for the season and 4 for his career, level with Matthew Ward (2011-2012). Sunday 16 August 1st XI v Grenfell CC (h) Jude Brooks, b Daiwik Singh off 4 balls, records his 2nd of the season and career, joining Alan Probert (2008-2009) — himself a rare double member of the Debutante and Retirement Duck boards. Jacob Landman survived 13 balls before falling ct Patel b Singireddy, his 2nd of the season and 3rd career. On this day in 1953, John Ames (1952-1978, 49 ducks) also departed for nought, against Mote A. Week in summary Nine ducks, eight matches, and Saturday doing the heavy lifting with seven of them spread across four different XIs — consistency of a very particular kind. Thomas Beeney remains the club's chief tormentor-in-chief this season. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 🍩 1. Thomas Beeney — 9 ducks, 32 inns (28.1%) 2. Spencer Gray — 5 ducks, 22 inns (22.7%) 3. Brandon Eloff — 5 ducks, 24 inns (20.8%) 4. Anthony Karassellos — 5 ducks, 31 inns (16.1%) 5. Theo Clements — 5 ducks, 34 inns (14.7%) See you all next weekend — the honours board never sleeps, and there's always room for one more nought. 0️⃣🏏

🦆 DUCK REPORT — 5 to 12 August 2026

8 ducks
Week 17 · 5 Aug 2026 – 12 Aug 2026
Seven matches, eight ducks, and the exclusive zero club opened its gates once more to the unlucky, the unfortunate, and — twice this week — the entirely golden. A tidy week's harvest. 🏏 1st XI — Borstal CC (away, 8 Aug) A brace for the visitors. Darrell Houghton-Judge fell to Mohammed Azhar after five balls of stern resistance, his 1st duck of the season and 37th of a fine career (277 innings, 34th all-time) — level with Joshua Knowler, who played 2008–2025. Darrell remains a Full House nearly-man, one position shy of ducking right through the order. Last man Matthew Carter joined him moments later, bowled Sam Pepper, his own season-opener and 39th career duck from 316 innings (29th all-time) — level with Chris Newman (2002–2017). Carter is a paid-up Debutante Duck club member and a former Duck of the Year, class of 2004. 🏏 3rd XI — Bredgar CC (home, 8 Aug) Another double, this time at home. Trevor Back edged behind for his 2nd duck of the season and a mighty 95th career nought — 797 innings deep and 3rd on the all-time roll, a regular of the Ducks on the Road, Homebody and Lone Duck top tens. On this very day in 1998, Richard Piper (96 ducks, 2nd all-time) was doing much the same against Bearsted. Curtis Etherington kept him company, bowled Sophie Hogben for his maiden career duck in only his 3rd innings — level with the mysterious - Howard, whose entire Linton career back in 2006 amounted to exactly one. 🏏 Midweek XI — The Mote CC (away, 11 Aug) Theo Clements, bowled Ronak Patel, notched his 5th duck of the season and 15th career (109 innings) — level with Richard Knowler, 2004–2026. 🌞 Sunday 1st XI — Stone-in-Oxney CC (home, 9 Aug) Praveen Tunga went first ball to Toby Withers Green — a golden duck, the purest form of the art — his 4th of the season and 10th career, from the Only Two Quacks board alongside Brandon Eloff. On this day in 1964, John Thirkell (90 ducks, 5th all-time) fell for nought against Harrietsham. 🌞 Sunday 2nd XI — Westerham CC (away, 9 Aug) Two more out at Westerham. Reuben Mundell was caught off Arhum Khan for his 1st duck of the season and 5th career — level with Alex Holt (2022–2026) — and comes from proper duck-collecting stock, sibling Thomas Mundell sat on 8 career noughts and a parent-child pairing with Blair Mundell on 3. Then Alexander Nunn, first ball, bowled Ishtiaq Azram — a second golden duck for the week — his 3rd of the season and 10th career, another to share Thirkell's 1964 date with Harrietsham. 📋 Week in Summary 8 ducks from 7 matches, and a curious symmetry: three fixtures — Borstal, Bredgar and Westerham — each produced a matching pair, and two victims never got off the mark at all. Consistency of a very particular kind. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 1. Thomas Beeney — 8 ducks/30 inn (26.67%) 2. Spencer Gray — 5/21 (23.81%) 3. Brandon Eloff — 5/23 (21.74%) 4. Anthony Karassellos — 5/29 (17.24%) 5. Theo Clements — 5/31 (16.13%) Next fixture looms, and with it, no doubt, fresh additions to the honours board. See you at the crease — or not, as the case may be. 🦆🍩

🦆 LPCC Duck Club — Week of 28 July to 4 August 2026

4 ducks
Week 16 · 28 Jul 2026 – 4 Aug 2026
Only four members qualified for admission this week, but nine matches gave everyone every chance, and the Club never turns away a genuine effort. Quality over quantity, as the exclusive zero club likes to say. Sunday 2nd XI — home to Boughton & Eastwell CC Jacob Landman, in at six, fell b Christopher Francis for his 1st duck of the season and 2nd of an increasingly distinguished career, from just 7 innings. Jacob remains a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club courtesy of a first-baller some time back, and now draws level with Alan Probert, who played 2008 to 2009 and reached the very same tally of 2 in only 2 innings, before promptly retiring on a duck himself. Some finish what they start. At number 11, Alexander Nunn joined him, bowled by Archie Rushin for his 2nd of the season and 9th career duck from 32 innings. That's level with Charles Curteis, a name from 2016 to 2020 who took 50 innings to get there — Alexander is getting to the same dubious distinction at rather more pace. The Hundred — away to Egerton CC, Kent Tim Ludick strode out at first drop and was back in the shed before he'd got comfortable — first ball, bowled Cameron Clarke, a proper golden duck. It's his maiden career nought from 9 innings and his 1st of the season, and it sits him alongside - Howard, whose single career duck came in 2006 in his only innings for the club, before he too bowed out for good. Tim will be hoping his own Duck Club membership runs rather longer. Brandon Eloff, at six, survived a couple of deliveries before edging Tom Richards — his 5th duck of the season and 13th of his career, 109th on the all-time list. That draws him level with Joe Martin, who played 2004 to 2016 and needed 86 innings to reach 13 where Brandon's done it in 77 — triumph through adversity, and rapid triumph at that. Brandon isn't fighting this alone either: fellow duck-club members Johan Eloff (14 career ducks) and Christian Eloff (3) share the family name, though neither troubled the scorers this week. He also remains a standing member of the Only Two Quacks club alongside Praveen Tunga. Week in Summary Four ducks from nine matches — the art of not scoring practised sparingly this week. Boughton & Eastwell and Egerton both took their toll, and Brandon Eloff continues to make a serious fist of the season race. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 🥇🍩 - Thomas Beeney — 8 ducks, 27 innings, 29.63% - Spencer Gray — 5 ducks, 20 innings, 25.00% - Brandon Eloff — 5 ducks, 23 innings, 21.74% - Anthony Karassellos — 5 ducks, 27 innings, 18.52% - David Holdstock — 4 ducks, 5 innings, 80.00% Spare a thought for David Holdstock, quietly running the most alarming strike rate in the club without yet cracking the summit. Next fixture, same open invitation: middle stump, minimal footwork, maximum glory. The honours board awaits its next volunteer. 0️⃣🏏

Father Michael Beeney (38 career noughts) watches on with quiet pride. 🍩 Sunday — 2nd XI v Milstead CC (home) David Holdstock, caught behind off Edward Rowe after 4 balls, notches his 4th duck of the season — his 4th in just 4 innings for the club, a flawless record already good for 247th all-time. He joins Matthew Ward (2011–2012, 4 from 10) on the same tally. Consistency of a very particular kind. 📊 The Week Six ducks, eight matches, and Andrew Bennett doing more damage with the ball than most manage in a month. Marden's golden double was the week's undoubted highlight — or lowlight, depending which end of the innings you were watching from. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Thomas Beeney — 8 ducks, 24 innings (33.3%) - Spencer Gray — 5 ducks, 20 innings (25.0%) - Anthony Karassellos — 5 ducks, 24 innings (20.8%) - David Holdstock — 4 ducks, 4 innings (100%) - John Karassellos — 4 ducks, 12 innings (33.3%) Fixtures resume next week — plenty of scope yet for the club's least wanted honour. Mark Christmas wasn't far behind, recording career duck number forty-six. Henry Campbell picked up the first duck of his season, taking his career tally to eleven. Then came perhaps the headline act... Thomas Beeney collected his fifth duck of the season, bringing his career total to fifty-four and earning entry onto the prestigious Most Ducks In A Match Honours Board after becoming one of five victims in the innings. When history books are written, this match will receive its own chapter. 2nd XI v Snodland Community Brandon Eloff reached double figures with career duck number ten, and his second this season. 3rd XI v Kings Hill Spencer Gray simply refuses to stop. Career duck number four. Season duck number four. The man is on a mission. Gene Smith also joined proceedings with the first duck of his season, taking his career tally to five. 4th XI v Town Malling Jono Sisley found himself added to the register. Zach Wilde continued climbing with career duck number fourteen, his third of the campaign. Sunday 1st XI v Rainham Anthony Karassellos completed an excellent fortnight by recording career duck number twenty-four, moving onto three ducks this season. Nav Singh also celebrated his inaugural Duck Club induction with the first duck of his career. Sunday 2nd XI v Grafty Green Spencer Gray completed the set. Career duck number five. Season duck number five. Joint leader. Midweek XI v Cudham Wyse Jordan Austin made his Duck Club debut, collecting the first duck of both his career and the season. --- 🏆 2026 Duck Hunting Leaderboard Three weeks have completely reshaped the race for this year's Golden Duck. At the summit, Thomas Beeney and Spencer Gray now sit level on five ducks apiece, but they could hardly have arrived there more differently. Thomas has once again demonstrated the consistency that has made him a Duck Club legend, while Spencer has exploded through the field after a remarkable three-week spell, climbing from the chasing pack to joint top almost overnight. Just behind them sits Theo Clements on four ducks. Considering Theo also has over 370 runs this season, he's attempting the difficult double of being both one of the club's better batsmen and one of its leading duck hunters. The chasing group is beginning to form nicely: * Anthony Karassellos moves onto three seasonal ducks and continues adding to his extraordinary career total of twenty-four. * Daniel Baker remains in contention with three. * Euan Beardwell has quietly surged to three official leaderboard ducks despite seemingly getting out for nothing every other weekend. * Johan Eloff, Jamie Wheeler and Zach Wilde all remain within striking distance. With half the season still to play, absolutely nobody in the top ten can consider themselves safe. --- 🦆 New Duck Club Members The committee would like to officially welcome several new recruits who recorded the first duck of their careers over the past three weeks. * Ashley Cairns * David Holdstock * Nav Singh * Jordan Austin Membership may be involuntary, but it is permanent. Congratulations... we suppose. --- Career Milestones Several significant landmarks were reached during the catch-up period: 🥇 Luke Welsman joins the exclusive 54 Duck Club, drawing level with Thomas Beeney. 🥈 Thomas Beeney records career duck 54 and enters the Most Ducks In A Match Honours Board. 🥉 Mark Christmas edges ever closer to the half-century milestone with career duck 46. 🎖 Anthony Karassellos continues building one of the greatest Duck Club careers ever seen, reaching 24 career ducks. --- Until next week... Remember: runs are temporary. Ducks are forever.

LPCC Duck Hunting Season 2026 – Week 4 Report

14 ducks
Week 4 · 9 May 2026 – 10 May 2026
Six matches this week — four league fixtures on Saturday and two games on Sunday — provided ample opportunity for ducks to flourish. But did the weekend live up to expectations? We dive into the scorecards to see who now leads the charge for Duck of the Year 2026 and whether any of Duck Club’s more obscure subcategories gained new members. --- Double Duck Weekend Propels a New Leader We begin with the crushing 1st XI defeat away to Lordswood Cricket Club. Runs were plentiful, unfortunately only for Lordswood. Three Linton batsmen managed to scramble a single run to avoid adding to their duck tallies. I was not among them. Saturday’s dismissal without scoring brought my career total to 51 ducks, drawing level with John Karassellos and Ian Brattle. However, I did not remain there for long. What better way to honour Ian Brattle — the holder of the legendary six consecutive ducks in the 1975 season — than with a double duck weekend? Another duck on Sunday saw me bunny-hop over both JK and Brattle to reach 52 career ducks. This milestone also places me alongside Luke Welsman who holds the exclusive and highly prestigious “50 Ducks Before Age 30” category. More importantly, I now emerge as the outright leader in the 2026 Duck of the Year standings with three ducks for the season. JK will have his work cut out if he is to retain the Duck of the Year trophy he won in 2025. --- Second XI – A Rare Duckless Affair The 2nd XI produced a disappointingly duck-free scorecard, so we move swiftly on. --- Third XI – Four Ducks and Two New Members The 3rd XI more than compensated for the Second Team’s restraint, recording four ducks: * Euan Beardwell * Spencer Gray * Paul Baker * Tim Thirkell Tim Thirkell – King of the Ducks Tim continues to soar above the flock with an astonishing 104 career ducks. It is lonely at the summit. Euan Beardwell Euan records his fourth senior duck for Linton across four seasons, drawing level with Matt Ward, who remarkably accumulated all four of his ducks in his final season before quietly departing the game. Spencer Gray Spencer was joined by both sons, Will Gray and James Gray. Sadly, only the father succumbed, meaning the coveted Father and Son Duck and Family of Ducks categories remain unchanged. Paul Baker A second father-and-son combination featured, with Dan Baker playing alongside his father Paul. Again, only the elder Baker was tempted by the duck. Both Spencer Gray and Paul Baker record their first ducks for the club and are formally inducktrinated into the LPCC Duck Family. --- Fourth XI – Dr Safeer Strikes Again Dr Safeer recorded his second duck of the season against the Orpington Ocelots, lasting seven balls before departing. This brings him level with Louis Turney on two career ducks. --- Sunday Cricket – A Hen Appears On Sunday, Claire Rootes departed without troubling the scorers. As Duck Club is an inclusive institution, Claire becomes the latest member and earns recognition as a Hen — the female equivalent of a duck. --- NVKO Update The NVKO fixture against Addington Cricket Club was conceded, granting Linton a bye into the next round where we will face Chestfield Cricket Club. Following last week’s encounter in the KVCL, we are hoping for a more favourable outcome. --- Sunday 1st XI – Another for the Author, and Ian Hollingworth Joins the Party The Sunday 1st XI fixture, moved to Rumwood, delivered two late-order ducks: * Myself (completing the double duck weekend) * Ian Hollingworth For a player with over two decades at the Park and a famously gung-ho approach to batting, it is remarkable Ian has not featured more prominently in Duck Club lore. This was Ian’s 35th career duck, drawing him level with Stan Wratton, whose extraordinary Linton career spanned more than 40 years. --- Sunday 2nd XI Collapse – Four More Ducks The Sunday 2nd XI were bowled out for 66, producing another rich harvest. Noah Stevens Noah Stevens recorded his second adult duck for the club. Nolan and Zach Wilde Nolan Wilde and Zach Wilde both fell for ducks while playing together. This earns them a place in Duck Club Hall of Fame under the prestigious Father and Son Duck category. Jamie Wheeler Jamie Wheeler recorded his first adult duck and is warmly welcomed into the LPCC Duck Club. --- Duck of the Year 2026 Standings (After Week 4) 1. Tom Beeney – 3 ducks 2. John Karassellos – 2 ducks 3. Dr Safeer – 2 ducks 4. Noah Stevens – 2 ducks 5. Nolan Wilde – 1 duck 6. Zach Wilde – 1 duck 7. Jamie Wheeler – 1 duck 8. Will Gray – 1 duck 9. Spencer Gray – 1 duck 10. Paul Baker – 1 duck 11. Claire Rootes – 1 hen --- The season is still young, but the field is beginning to take shape. LPCC Duck Hunt 2026 – Week 3 Update

3 ducks
Week 3 · 2 May 2026 – 3 May 2026
A new leader has emerged in the race for LPCC Duck of the Year 2026. With last week’s duck still fresh in the memory, John Karassellos rose to the occasion on Sunday in the 2nd XI fixture against Marden… by adding another. Marden piled on 307, which proved far too much, with the 2s bowled out for 124 in reply. Included in that total was JK’s second duck of the season — and his 51st all-time. That milestone sees him pull clear of the pack and draw level with Ian Brattle, who holds a special place in Duck Club folklore for one of the most remarkable records: six consecutive ducks during the 1975 season at the Park. Brattle also features in the exclusive “50 ducks before a 50” subcategory — a club so niche it still only has two members. JK, of course, was Duck of the Year 2025. While he’s made an early statement, the season is young — plenty of time for a recovery… or for others to reel him in. In a match that promised much for Duck Club subcategories, Russel Wilde returned to the LPCC side, representing the wider Wilde family alongside Nolan and Zach. Russel, already etched into history with a Debutante Duck back in 2022, didn’t disappoint — now sitting on 2 ducks from just 3 appearances. However, with no ducks for Nolan or Zach, the coveted “Family of Ducks” category remains unchanged… for now. Russel is certainly one to watch. Elsewhere, on Saturday, Will Gray recorded his first duck of the season in his third game, earning a place on this year’s leaderboard. Will now has 6 adult ducks for Linton (a reminder: junior ducks don’t count towards official totals), drawing level with Mick Filmer. Filmer’s career is notable not just for its longevity, but for its curious duck-free comebacks — returning after breaks in 1988 and again in 1993 without adding to his tally. A man who knew when to avoid the spotlight. No other ducks were recorded on a rain-affected Saturday.

🦆 Duck Club Returns – Opening Weekend 2026

5 ducks
Week 1 · 18 Apr 2026 – 19 Apr 2026
Welcome back to another glorious Duck Hunting season at Linton Park Cricket Club! The 2026 campaign got underway in style this weekend and, crucially, did not disappoint. With five matches across Saturday and Sunday, there was no shortage of opportunity for those dreaded—but celebrated—ducks. As always, best to get those naughty noughts out of the system before the league season fires up in May. And I’m pleased to report… the Duck Club is already thriving. 🏏 Saturday – Bearsted Battles & Early Casualties Linton Park kicked things off with a full club double-header against local rivals Bearsted, with fixtures home and away. At Bearsted Green, the 1st XI got underway. Duck Club regular Jordan Austin opened proceedings and narrowly avoided early honours, grafting his way to 2 before being trapped in front by Alex Lush. Unfortunately, Johan Eloff wasn’t as fortunate—registering the first duck of the 2026 season. A strong start to the campaign for Johan, who now moves to 12 career ducks in just 52 innings, boasting an impressive 23% duck rate. He draws level with LPCC great Burt Buckoke, whose four-decade career (1928–1954) yielded the same tally in 55 innings. All eyes will be on Johan this season to see how far he can push that number. Not to be outdone, Sam Boyns also added to his collection, bringing up his 12th duck for the club. With 148 innings under his belt, Sam maintains a respectable 8% duck rate, now level with Martin Larkin, a familiar name from the 80s and 90s, who reached the same milestone in just 70 innings (albeit better known for his exploits with the ball). 🔥 2nd XI – A Hall of Fame Moment Meanwhile, back at home against Bearsted 2nd XI, things truly heated up. In the closing stages of the innings, chasing quick bonus runs and glory, I strode to the crease with intent… and departed just as quickly. A thick edge, a simple catch, and history was made. Duck number 50. A milestone moment. Bat raised. Crowd (mostly) silent. This achievement secures formal entry into the Duck Club Hall of Fame—an elite gathering of individuals whose ability to accumulate the dreaded duck is unmatched. This landmark innings moves me to 15th in the all-time standings, surpassing David Castle and drawing level with fellow Duck Club member Jordan Austin. Together, we now stand alongside John Ames (1952–1978), who recorded 50 ducks across 418 innings. For context: My 50 ducks: 327 innings (15%) Ames’ 50 ducks: 418 innings Efficiency matters. 🏏 3rd XI – Into Double Figures The 3rd XI clash with Brasted Chart & Toys Hill added another name to the honours board. Jonno Sisely brought up his 10th LPCC duck in just 27 innings, joining the ranks of Theo Clements (present), Brian Fuller (1968–1976), and Don Hartridge (1940–1952). A fine achievement—and a reminder that no one is ever truly alone in the Duck Club. And for perspective, things could always be worse. Special mention must go to Magnus Boxer and E Hayes, who maintain a flawless 100% duck rate. Truly remarkable consistency. 🌱 Sunday – A Mixed Bag Sunday’s fixtures provided a quieter, more selective harvest. The 1st XI emergency fixture against Mallu was, disappointingly, a vegan affair—completely free from fowl. However, the 2nd XI trip to Rumwood to face New Ifield delivered one addition: Alex Nunn – now on 10 career ducks (45 innings), joining Jonno in double figures. Near misses came from Zach Wilde and Nolan Wilde, both falling for 1. A single run away from Duck Club folklore—particularly in what would have been a rare and celebrated Father & Son Duck double. Plenty of time for that yet… 📅 Looking Ahead A strong opening weekend for the Duck Club, with milestones, new members, and early-season form all on display. With the league season fast approaching, the question remains: Who will rise (or fall) to the occasion next weekend? We watch. We wait. We celebrate. 🦆

1982 Season 16 reports

🦆 Duck News — Weekend of 7-8 August 1982

0 ducks
Week 16 · 7 Aug 1982 – 8 Aug 1982
Two matches, two results, and — brace yourselves — not a single duck to show for it. The full 1982 top order marched out, faced their overs, and every last one of them troubled the scorer. A blank weekend for the exclusive zero club, and a rare one at that. We won't pretend this isn't a little disappointing. The art of not scoring is a proud Linton tradition and this weekend it simply wasn't practised. No golden ducks, no pairs, no family affairs to report — just eleven men a side quietly getting off the mark like it's the most natural thing in the world. Frankly, unnatural. Still, a fallow weekend for the ducks is not a fallow weekend for the season. The race for Duck of the Year rumbles on regardless, and the current pecking order makes for interesting reading. 0️⃣ Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 🥇 Sean Cook — 4 ducks from just 6 innings, a scarcely believable 66.67% strike rate. At this pace he may retire the trophy before September. 🥈 Steve Cheale — 3 from 7, ticking along at 42.86%. Every third visit to the crease is apparently optional. 🥉 Fred Cheesman — 5 ducks from 17 innings and 29.41%, the current volume leader even if the percentage boys are chasing him down. 4️⃣ Malcolm Pay — 3 from 26, a more modest 11.54%, playing the long game. 5️⃣ Paul Bowles — 3 from 37, 8.11%, the elder statesman of the group proving that consistency of a very particular kind takes patience. Sean Cook holds the raw pace, Fred Cheesman the raw total — plenty of season left for either to pull clear, and plenty of time for the rest of the chasing pack to come good. 🏏 So, an uneventful weekend for the collectors among us. The ducks evaded capture this time, but nobody should get comfortable — form like this rarely lasts, and Linton's middle order has let the club down (in the best possible way) too often for anyone to relax. Next fixture, normal service will surely resume. See you at the crease. 🦆

Some traditions never go out of fashion. - At number six, Martin Larkin fell bowled Terry Franks for his 1st duck of the season and 4th of a 28-innings career, enough for 121st on the all-time roll. Larkin is also a long-standing member of the Retirement Duck club, having once bowed out of his playing days on a nought — though today's effort is very much business as usual rather than a farewell tour. Fittingly, he shares the honours-board moment with his teammate: both men keeping step with William Blight's own duck against Gore Court, twenty-five years on almost to the week. Week in Brief Two ducks from four matches, both arriving in the same innings against Maidstone YMCA — proof, if proof were needed, that misery loves company. The other three fixtures passed entirely fowl-free, which either speaks well of the batting or poorly of the bowling, depending on where your loyalties lie. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 1. 🦆 Duck News — Bank Holiday Weekend, 1st–3rd May 1982

4 ducks
Week 2 · 1 May 1982 – 3 May 1982
The 1982 season is barely a week old and the exclusive zero club has already welcomed new business. Three fixtures, four ducks, and one thoroughly memorable arrival — the art of not scoring is alive and well at Linton Park. Saturday 1st May — Bidborough CC (away) Malcolm Pay departed early at first drop, caught Eddie Keates bowled J- Kerby, for the first duck of his season. His 17th career nought in 143 innings lifts him to 35th in the all-time table, level company with Robert Murray and Trevor Back, both also parked on 17. His brother Colin Pay carries one of his own, so a taste for the zero clearly runs in the Pay family blood. On this very day back in 1965, Fred Greenfield made a duck against Staplehurst CC on his way to a career 23, a Retirement Duck club man who signed off 28th all-time. Further down the order Fred Cheesman continued his season of dubious consistency, bowled T Ham for his second duck of the campaign, now 5 career ducks from just 17 innings, a poultry-thin record that holds him at 96th all-time. Fred remains a proud holder of the rare Full House, duck at every position 1 through 11, and sits in the Tourist Duck top ten alongside his Only Two Quacks pairing with Adam Pooley. Like Malcolm, he shares his on-this-day company with Fred Greenfield's 1965 vintage. Sunday 2nd May — Chestfield CC (home) Nigel Thirkell fell bowled Richard Tolson for his first duck of the year, his 30th in a marathon 402-innings career, holding at a lofty 16th all-time — genuinely elite territory. He belongs to duck-club royalty of a different kind, with the Thirkell name littered through the honours boards: father John on 90, brothers Tim on 49 and Simon on 3, and relative Stuart on 1. Nigel himself carries Homebody Duck and Tourist Duck top ten membership, plus an Only Two Quacks pairing with Jim Hall. Back on this day in 1959, Frank Brattle also fell for nought, against Bearsted CC, en route to a career 38 and 9th all-time. Monday 3rd May — Bearsted CC (away) And so to the main event. J Dunn, on debut, was bowled B Lewis without troubling the scorers — a genuine first appearance in senior colours and an instant Debutante Duck. With the season still young, he already features among 1982's One and Done watch list. On this same day in 1959, Tony Tipples suffered identical fortune against Harrietsham CC, finishing his own career on 7. A tidy little haul of four ducks across three matches to open the campaign. No pairs, no family affairs this week, but plenty of honours boards dusted off in the process. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 🥇 Fred Cheesman — 4 inns, 2 ducks (50%) 2. J Dunn — 1 inns, 1 duck (100%) 3. Steve Gower — 1 inns, 1 duck (100%) 4. Jim Hall — 2 inns, 1 duck (50%) 5. Four fixtures, five noughts, and one properly historic sibling ceremony down in Cornwall. The exclusive zero club welcomes its latest inductees. Sunday 4th September — Tour XI at Cornwall Police CC The touring party delivered the week's genuine rarity: a Two of a Quack, brothers Nigel Thirkell and Tim Thirkell both bowled by D Jenkin in the same innings. Both brothers, fittingly, echo P- Martin, who ducked for the club on this same calendar day in 1949 against East Peckham & Nettlestead. Worth noting the family isn't finished there — father John Thirkell sits on a barely believable 90 career ducks, the club's all-time number one, with siblings Simon (2) and Stuart (1) also paid-up members. A dynasty built entirely on the art of not scoring. Week in summary Five ducks from four matches. 🦆 Duck Report — 1st to 5th August 1981

3 ducks
Week 14 · 1 Aug 1981 – 5 Aug 1981
A quiet week by Linton standards, but quality over quantity: three matches, three ducks, and one thumping entry into the record books that'll be the talk of the bar for weeks. 🏏 Saturday 1st August — 1st XI vs Old Anchorians CC (h) The top order took a hammering. In at three, Jim Hall was run out for nought — the fielder responsible lost to history, recorded only as "Unsure" — his second duck of the season and 47th of an extraordinary career, good enough for 6th on the all-time list of 997. A paid-up Debutante Duck, two-time Duck of the Year (1970 and 1977), and a fixture of the Lone Duck, Homebody Duck and Tourist Duck top tens, Jim remains one of the club's most decorated non-scorers, and still chipping away at his Full House. On this very day in 1964, Basil Sears (1947–1975, 33 career ducks) was adding to the archives against Headcorn CC — some things never change. Moments later, Gareth Thomas holed out caught and bowled by J. Lycett without scoring — his first duck of the season and second of a young career, from just 8 innings, sliding him to 193rd all time. He shares the same on-this-day billing as Jim: Basil Sears, 1964. A member of the Retirement Duck club from a past farewell, Gareth has a long way to go before that honour is relevant again. 🔥 Wednesday 5th August — Midweek XI vs Maidstone Police (h) Now, the headline. Opening the batting, Jon Harris was caught by Harry Dunk off Evans without scoring — a routine line in the scorebook, but a landmark one in the ledger. It's his 50th career duck, moving him to 2nd on the all-time chart of 997, second only to the legendary John Thirkell (1943–1977, 90 ducks) and clear of everyone else to have pulled on a Linton shirt. It's also his second duck of the season, and with Duck of the Year 1981 already on his honours board he's handsomely placed to defend the crown. A Full House campaigner and Homebody and Lone Duck top-ten regular, Jon now stands one nought closer to cricketing immortality — or at least a testimonial cake. On this day in 1895, Ernest Cruttenden (1881–1912) made his own duck against Rochester CC — 86 years on, the club is still finding new ways to fail with style. 📊 Week in Summary Three matches, three ducks, no pairs and no family affairs to report — a restrained week that let one man's milestone take centre stage. The 1st XI's top order fancied an early bath, while the Midweek XI's contribution came dressed as history. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season 1981 leaderboard - Paul Bowles — 4 ducks in 36 innings (11.1%) - Martin Thompson — 3 in 15 (20.0%) - David Carden — 2 in 6 (33.3%) - Tim Thirkell — 2 in 8 (25.0%) - Trevor Back — 2 in 10 (20.0%) 🍩 Next up The season presses on and the ducks show no sign of retiring, even if some of the club's finest occasionally do. A paid-up member of the Retirement Duck club from a past farewell, Thompson proves there's life in the old guard yet. On this same date in 1961, William Agate was doing his own bit for posterity with a duck against Charles Arkcoll. The Week in Brief Two matches, two ducks, both perishing at number six, both bowled — a position and a method of dismissal apparently allergic to runs this week. Slim pickings so far this season, but the harvest is only just getting started. 🦆 Duck News — 30 August to 5 September 1980

5 ducks
Week 19 · 30 Aug 1980 – 5 Sep 1980
Five ducks hit the water across three fixtures as the season heads into its final stretch, headlined by a spectacular top-and-tail collapse on tour in Cornwall. Let's get into it. Saturday 30 August — 1st XI v British Rail Ashford (h) David Carden departed at first drop, caught A Owen off J Jenkins, without scoring. It's his 1st duck of the season and 3rd of a career now 53 innings deep, good (or bad) enough for 134th on the all-time list. On this very day back in 1965, Frank Brattle — 38 ducks across a career spanning 1937 to 1971, 9th all-time — was performing the identical trick against Bearsted CC. Some Linton Park traditions are handed down through the generations. Sunday 31 August — 1st XI v Staplehurst CC (a) Allan Cooper edged behind at four, caught John Hughes off John Munn, for his 3rd duck of the season and 25th of a thoroughly decorated LPCC career — 21st all-time from 144 innings. Cooper's name is already inked twice into the honours board for shared quacking, alongside both Jim Hall and Jon Harris — fitting, since both were about to catch him up (see below). On this day in 1974, Mike Iliffe — 41 ducks, 1966 to 1980, 7th all-time — fell exactly the same way against Whitstable. Friday 5 September — Tour XI v Cornwall Crusaders (a) The end-of-season tour to Cornwall was rather less restful than advertised for the top and tail of the Tour XI order. Openers Paul Bowles and Jim Hall fell in matching fashion, both bowled by H James without scoring — a new-ball double strike guaranteed to delight the Crusaders and unsettle everyone else. For Bowles, a 1st duck of the season and a hefty 33rd career nought, 14th all-time from 428 innings, adding to a cabinet already containing Duck of the Year honours from 1966 and 1968. For Hall, also his 1st of the season, it's a mighty 44th career duck — 6th all-time — and a name already sat on the Duck of the Year 1980 board among a wall of others, including one for "nearly" completing the Full House at 10 of 11 positions. Then, as the innings wound down, last man Jon Harris was run out — "unsurely", says the book — for his 7th duck of the season, stretching his lead at the top of the season table. It's his 48th career duck, 3rd on the all-time roll, and with position 11 now ticked off, it completes his own Full House — a duck recorded at every batting position from 1 to 11. A chip off an unlucky block, too: his relative Richard Harris carries 36 career ducks of his own in Linton Park colours. Remarkably, all three Tour XI victims share the same historical echo: David T Lowen, who made his own duck on this exact calendar date in 1970, against A. Trembeths. Three ducks, one innings, one ghost from a decade earlier watching on approvingly. Week in summary Five ducks from three matches, three of them arriving in a single unfortunate Tour XI innings. The 1st XI contributed one apiece across their weekend fixtures. A tidy week's work for the exclusive zero club. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Jon Harris — 24 innings, 7 ducks, 29.17% - Tim Thirkell — 28 innings, 5 ducks, 17.86% - Ross Brice — 9 innings, 4 ducks, 44.44% - David Iliffe — 16 innings, 4 ducks, 25.0% - Allan Cooper — 17 innings, 3 ducks, 17.65% Jon Harris holds a commanding lead at the top, but with the season still to run there's plenty of time for a late surge from the chasing pack. 🏏 See you all at the next fixture — the ducks, as ever, will be waiting. 🦆0️⃣

A proper family affair too — his father John Thirkell sits on a mighty 90 career ducks, with siblings Nigel (28) and Simon (1) also paid-up members, so ducking is clearly hereditary round the Thirkell household. 1 duck
Week 12 · 12 Jul 1980 – 18 Jul 1980
A remarkably restrained week for the Duck Club. Four matches contested, and the ducks mostly kept their heads down — bar one immaculate exception on the Friday. 🌙 Midweek XI — Detours CC, 18 July Trevor Back strode out at five and departed the way so many before him have, caught G Marshall, bowled B Kingston, without troubling the scoreboard. It's his second duck of the season and the 14th of an increasingly distinguished LPCC career, now sat 41st of 986 in the all-time table from 86 innings — a record built with the quiet consistency of a man who treats a nought as a personal brand. Trevor is no stranger to the honours boards, holding places in both the Lone Duck and Homebody Duck top tens — evidently he manages to duck perfectly well without even leaving home. He also shares billing in Only Two Quacks with Allan Cooper and Quacking Together with Jon Harris, proof that misery, like a good tea urn, is best shared. A neat footnote for the historians: on this very day in 1964, Frank Brattle — who played from 1937 to 1971 and finished with 38 ducks, 9th on the all-time list — also trudged back for nought, against Rumwood CC. The calendar, it seems, has a sense of humour all of its own. 📊 The Week in Brief One duck from four matches is a lean haul by Duck Club standards — either the bowling was off the boil or the batters simply couldn't be bothered to give us anything worth celebrating. Either way, Trevor carries the flag alone this week, and the collection plate stays disappointingly light. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 1980 1. Jon Harris — 5 ducks / 16 innings (31.25%) 2. 🦆 Duck Club Weekly — 5th to 6th July 1980 🦆

5 ducks
Week 11 · 5 Jul 1980 – 6 Jul 1980
A quieter harvest this week, but quality over quantity — five ducks across the weekend, and two of the club's most storied names among them. 🏏 Saturday — Medway Valley at home David Iliffe fell early at first drop, caught behind off Pettitt, for his 3rd duck of the season and 7th of a distinguished career — now 76th in the all-time standings. Handily, on this very day back in 1943, Herbert Sunley was also making a duck, against Mr Ashby's XI no less — some things never change. Not to be outdone, Tim Thirkell followed him back, also caught off Pettitt, for his 4th of the season and 45th career duck — a mighty 5th on the all-time list, and a man who already owns Full House honours (a duck at every position 1 to 11) plus a place among the Homebody, Lone Duck and Ducks on the Road elite. Fittingly, Tim shares this same calendar date in duck history with Herbert Sunley too — 1943 clearly a vintage year for nought. 🏏 Saturday/Sunday — Reeds Aylesford away The away trip produced a hat-trick of sorts. Trevor Back departed bowled by Colin Watson for his 1st duck of the season, 13th career — level with Derek Pantony (1947–1968), and drawing his customary parallel with Paul Bowles, who made a duck on this same day in 1968 against Charles Arkcoll. Then came the man himself — Jon Harris, the club's all-time number 4 with a jaw-dropping 46 career ducks, caught at number 10 for his remarkable 5th duck of the season. Jon's honours board reads like a museum wing: Duck of the Year 1976 AND 1980, Full House, Lone Duck top 10, Tourist Duck top 10, Debutante Duck — the man was practically born for this. He too echoes Paul Bowles's 1968 vintage duck against Charles Arkcoll. Closing out the innings, Tony Gauna went the same way as Trevor and Jon — bowled by Colin Watson — for his 2nd of the season and 23rd career duck, level with Colin Dicker (1972–1978). Colin Watson clearly fancied his chances at Reeds Aylesford, claiming three of Linton's five wickets for nought. 📊 Week in Summary Five ducks, two matches, and Colin Watson doing more damage with the ball than most bowlers manage in a month — three victims for no runs between them. Jon Harris's 5th of the season keeps him running away with the Duck of the Year race, while the Thirkell and Harris names continue their long tenancy near the top of the all-time charts. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Jon Harris — 5 ducks in 15 innings (33.33%) - Tim Thirkell — 4 ducks in 17 innings (23.53%) - David Iliffe — 3 ducks in 10 innings (30.00%) - Malcolm Pay — 3 ducks in 15 innings (20.00%) - Ross Brice — 2 ducks in 6 innings (33.33%) 🍩 The season rolls on, and with Colin Watson lurking for Reeds Aylesford, who's brave enough to face him next time round? See you at the crease — or, more likely, back in the pavilion. 0️⃣🦆 --- One quick note unrelated to the report: a couple of team machines (Kleptocrat1 and turbosammy-Defiance-Pro-16) are behind on skill/tooling updates — worth a nudge to whoever owns them to start a Claude session so it syncs automatically.

Week 10 · 28 Jun 1980 – 3 Jul 1980
Three fixtures, five ducks, and the 1st XI shouldering every one of them this week — a fine advert for consistency of a very particular kind. 🏏 Saturday 28 June — Meopham CC A bumper afternoon for the zero club, with three wickets falling for nought in the same innings. Opener Brian Piper fell early, caught Sambrook bowled Phelps, his 1st duck of the season and 8th of a 145-innings career, good for 64th on the all-time list. Small comfort: on this very date in 1975, Phil Hickman was making the same walk against Tilling Steven. At seven, Martin Mears followed him back, bowled Phelps, his own 1st of the season and 12th career duck, moving to 45th all-time. A charter member of "Quacking Together" alongside Jim Hall, Martin shares that same 1975 on-this-day companion in Phil Hickman. But the day belonged to Jon Harris. Caught Campbell bowled Pennalls at number ten, this was his 4th duck of the season and a startling 45th of his career — 4th on the all-time Linton chart, no less. Jon's honours board reads like a life membership certificate: Full House (a duck at every position, 1 to 11), top-ten entries in both Lone Duck and Homebody Duck, Ducks on the Road and Tourist Duck top tens, a Debutante Duck from long ago, and Quacking Together twice over, with Jim Hall and with Trevor Back. His 4th this season also sits him on the Duck of the Year 1980 board — the race for the title is very much his to lose. And it runs in the family: father Richard Harris carries 36 career ducks of his own. Phil Hickman, once again, keeps him company on this date in history. 🏏 Sunday 29 June — Rainham (Kent) CC Ross Brice, caught and bowled by David Lawler at first drop, notched his 2nd duck of the season and 8th career duck from a brisk 22 innings, landing 74th on the all-time table. A former Duck of the Year in 1979, Ross evidently likes a title. On this same date in 1907, Ernest Cruttenden was similarly dismissed against Town Malling CC, en route to his own Duck of the Year in 1895. 🏏 Thursday 3 July — Leybourne CC Malcolm Pay rounded off the week, caught Bottle bowled David Edmonds at four, his 3rd duck of the season and 14th career duck, 40th all-time from 103 innings. Brother Colin Pay keeps one lonely career duck of his own — the Pays aren't troubling the family boards yet. Back on this date in 1960, Robert Murray was suffering the identical fate against Tovil. 📊 Week in Summary Five ducks, three matches, one team doing all the work — Meopham alone yielded three in a single innings, a proper cluster for the collection. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. 🦆 Duck News — 21 to 25 June 1980 🦆

3 ducks
Week 9 · 21 Jun 1980 – 25 Jun 1980
Three matches, three ducks, and every single one of them landing on the 1st XI's card this week. The exclusive zero club welcomes no new faces this time round, but two of its most seasoned members were only too happy to top up the account. Saturday 21 June — v Horton Kirby CC (h) Keith Williams enjoyed himself enormously, accounting for two Linton batsmen in the same innings and, in the process, adding two more names to the week's roll of dishonour. David Iliffe, in at three, was trapped lbw without scoring — his 2nd duck of the season and 6th of a career now spanning 23 innings, good (or bad) enough for 82nd on the all-time list. Neatly, the calendar has previous here: on this very day back in 1975, Colin Dicker was completing an identical walk against Hythe CC, one of 23 ducks that carried him to 27th all-time and a brace of Duck of the Year titles either side of it. Iliffe can also claim family form — kinsman Mike Iliffe already carries 41 career ducks of his own, so the trait is evidently hereditary. One place later, Tim Thirkell fell to the same bowler for his 3rd of the season and 44th of a career — 5th in the entire 986-strong all-time table, a rarefied altitude few will ever trouble. The honours board already knows him well: Duck of the Year 1972, a member of the exalted Full House club for having ducked at every position from 1 to 11, and a permanent fixture in both the Homebody and Lone Duck top tens. The date obliges again — 21 June 1975 was also when Colin Dicker met his end against Hythe CC. And should anyone doubt the hereditary theory above, the Thirkell name is practically a duck dynasty in its own right: kinsman John carries 90 career noughts, Nigel 28, and Stuart 1 more for the collection. Sunday 22 June — v Dimanchians CC (h) Allan Cooper departed at two, bowled by C Cunliffe, for his 2nd duck of the season and 24th of his career — 24th on the all-time list too, appropriately enough. Cooper is a seasoned member of the "Only Two Quacks" fraternity, with shared-duck honours already logged alongside Jim Hall, Jon Harris and Trevor Back. History was watching once more — on this same date in 1935, Percy Brattle was falling for nought against Bearsted CC, one of 16 ducks that eventually earned him Duck of the Year in 1969. The week's third fixture, midweek on the 25th, passed the Duck Club by entirely — a rare case of the ducks evading capture. Week in summary Three matches, three ducks, and a clean sweep for the 1st XI. Keith Williams can consider himself an honorary Duck Club patron after a two-for at Horton Kirby, while the weekend's business leaves Tim Thirkell knocking on the door of the season's top spot. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 1. Jon Harris — 3 ducks / 11 innings (27.3%) 2. Tim Thirkell — 3 ducks / 15 innings (20.0%) 3. Martin Larkin — 2 ducks / 6 innings (33.3%) 4. Allan Cooper — 2 ducks / 7 innings (28.6%) 5. David Iliffe — 2 ducks / 7 innings (28.6%) Jon Harris clings to top spot, but Tim Thirkell's Saturday effort has him breathing down his neck. And, fittingly, on this day in 1970 Ron Hickman was doing the honours against Boughton Monchelsea CC, one of 29 career ducks on his way to 18th of 986 and a spot on both the Quacking Together and Runaway Duck (1965) honours boards. 📊 Week in Summary Three ducks, three matches, and the 1st XI cornering the market entirely — the 2nds, 3rds and 4ths escaping unscathed this week. Week 1 · 26 Apr 1980 – 27 Apr 1980
Season 1980 creaks into life, and with the very first ball-by-ball ink barely dry, the Duck Club has already found its opening member. Two fixtures on the books this weekend, and only one proved fertile hunting ground — but quality over quantity, as ever, is the club's watchword. 1st XI v Chatham Nomads CC (Home) Coming in at number 8, David Iliffe departed for nought, bowled by D Barton — a tidy, uncomplicated dismissal, the kind that asks no questions and gets none in return. It's his 1st duck of the season and the 5th of a career now running to 17 innings, which lodges him at a very respectable 91st of 980 in the all-time standings. The Iliffe name is no stranger to these pages either, with a fellow member of the family carrying 40 career ducks of his own — proof that a taste for the zero can run in the blood. Neatly enough, on this very calendar day back in 1968, Cliff Anscombe also strolled back for a duck, against West Farleigh CC of all sides. Cliff played from 1957 to 1975, finished with 25 career ducks and sits 22nd all-time — a Debutante Duck to boot, having opened his account with one, and Duck of the Year in 1957. History, it seems, likes an anniversary. Elsewhere across the weekend's second fixture, the opposition bowlers came away empty-handed — no further additions to report, much to the collective relief of whoever was padded up next. Week in Summary One duck from two matches is a quiet return by the club's usual standards — a single, dignified entry rather than a stampede. Still, the season is younger than a fresh pair of whites, and there's a long summer of dubious batting ahead in which to make up the numbers. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - David Iliffe — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% Early days, and the field is wide open. With fixtures rolling on, the honours board waits for its next volunteer — bring your bat, bring your nerve, and may the bowlers find your edge. 🦆🏏0️⃣

1979 Season 24 reports

🦆 Duck News — 6 October 1979

0 ducks
Week 24 · 6 Oct 1979
One match ventured out onto the field this week, and — remarkably, suspiciously, almost insultingly — not a single duck was laid to rest. The zero club, for once, recorded a zero of its own. Eleven bats went out, eleven bats presumably troubled the scorer in some fashion, and the honours board gathers dust for another week. Whether this represents a genuine outbreak of competence or merely a temporary ceasefire in hostilities between bat and ball, the Duck Club cannot say. We can only report what the scorebook tells us, and this week the scorebook is disappointingly free of fowl. Do not despair. The art of not scoring is a skill honed over generations at Linton Park, and it does not simply vanish because of one clean sheet. Normal service — and by "normal" we mean "abnormal, in the very best way" — will surely resume before long. 🍩 A quiet week for the ignominious. Make of that what you will. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 🏏 - 🥇 Ross Brice — 6 ducks in 15 innings, a startling 40.0% strike rate for failure - 🥈 Allan Cooper — 5 ducks in 20 innings, 25.0% - 🥉 Jim Hall — 4 ducks in 24 innings, 16.67% - 4️⃣ Mike Iliffe — 3 ducks in 11 innings, 27.27% - 5️⃣ Fred Greenfield — 3 ducks in 14 innings, 21.43% Ross Brice sits proudly atop the pile with two ducks in every five visits to the crease — a consistency of a very particular kind, and one that separates the merely unlucky from the truly committed. The chasing pack will need to pull their fingers out, and their bats in, if they hope to catch him before the season closes. 0️⃣ Until the next time willow meets leather and somebody's stumps meet the same, keep your eyes on the middle and your bat nowhere near the ball. The Duck Club never sleeps for long.

🦆 Duck News — 29 September 1979 🦆

3 ducks
Week 23 · 29 Sep 1979
🏏 1st XI v Lordswood CC (h) A single fixture on the books this week, but Lordswood CC made sure it counted — three additions to the ledger inside one Linton Park innings. Paul Bowles opened the batting and, true to a well-worn habit, opened the account of ducks too — caught Colin Gardener, bowled V. Corbin. It's his 3rd of the season and the 32nd of an extraordinary career spanning 394 innings, keeping him a lofty 14th in the all-time standings of 980. A two-time Duck of the Year (1966 and 1968), a fixture of the Ducks on the Road top 10, and one half of the Only Two Quacks pairing with Adam Pooley, Paul scarcely needs introducing to this column anymore. Fittingly, on this very date back in 1973, club stalwart Nigel Thirkell was doing much the same against Bexhill CC — some anniversaries keep quacking back. At number five, Don Fermor introduced himself to senior cricket in the most Duck Club way imaginable — caught Andy Coltham, bowled Kevin Masters, first innings, first duck. A debut nought is no small thing: it earns immediate, lifelong membership of the Debutante Duck club, that select order whose very first act at the crease was to depart without scoring. Welcome, Don — 1 from 1 already slots you in at 292nd on the all-time list, with a flawless 100% record you'll be quietly hoping not to maintain. As it happens, Nigel Thirkell was on identical date-in-history duty back in 1973 too. Rounding out the innings, Mike Iliffe fell for nought at number eight, caught Colin Gardener again, this time off Henderson Carrington. It's Mike's 3rd duck of the season and 40th of his career from 261 innings, good enough for 7th on the all-time list — rarefied poultry company indeed. He isn't carrying the torch alone either: son David Iliffe already has 4 career ducks of his own, a fine family tradition quietly taking shape. And yes, once more, 29 September 1973 saw Nigel Thirkell doing exactly this. Week in Summary Three ducks, one match, and Colin Gardener rather enjoying himself in the field — two of Saturday's three victims fell into his hands. A tidy, efficient afternoon's work for the Lordswood attack, and a productive one for the Duck Club ledger. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. Ross Brice — 6 ducks / 15 innings (40.0%) 2. Allan Cooper — 5 ducks / 20 innings (25.0%) 3. Jim Hall — 4 ducks / 24 innings (16.67%) 4. Mike Iliffe — 3 ducks / 10 innings (30.0%) 5. Fred Greenfield — 3 ducks / 14 innings (21.43%) Mike's afternoon at Lordswood keeps him firmly inside the top five and breathing down Jim Hall's neck for the podium. That's the lot from this outing — the season presses on, the runs remain optional, and the next fixture promises fresh opportunities for the art of not scoring. See you at the crease 🦆🏏0️⃣

0 ducks
Week 22 · 22 Sep 1979 – 23 Sep 1979
A rare and faintly troubling turn of events at Linton Park this weekend: two matches played, eleven wickets and more falling in the ordinary course of things, and not a single naught to show for it. 🏏 The Duck Club's scouts were out in force across both fixtures and returned, disappointingly, empty-handed. Every batsman who walked to the crease found his way off the mark before walking back — a state of affairs the committee views with some suspicion. Whether this represents a genuine outbreak of competence or simply a temporary drought in the art of not scoring, only next weekend will tell. Rest assured, normal service is expected to resume shortly. The zero club does not take kindly to being kept waiting, and with the season drawing towards its close there remains plenty of time for the standings below to be shuffled once more. 0️⃣ Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard — 1979 0️⃣ 🥇 Ross Brice — 6 ducks from 15 innings (40.0%) — a formidable rate that puts real daylight between him and the chasing pack 🥈 Allan Cooper — 5 from 20 (25.0%) 🥉 Jim Hall — 4 from 23 (17.39%) 4️⃣ Fred Greenfield — 3 from 14 (21.43%) 5️⃣ Trevor Back — 3 from 16 (18.75%) Ross Brice sits handsomely clear at the summit with the season entering its final weeks, though at a 40% strike rate for noughts he'll want to watch his back — nobody wants to be caught napping this close to the finish line, least of all by the very thing that got him there. So there it is — a quiet weekend for the Duck Club, but a quiet weekend only ever means the ducks are gathering strength for the next one. 🦆 Duck News — 15 to 19 September 1979 🦆

2 ducks
Week 21 · 15 Sep 1979 – 19 Sep 1979
A modest haul from the closing weeks of the '79 campaign, but a modest haul in the Duck Club is still a haul worth toasting. Two additions to the ledger this week, both from the 1st XI, both worth a moment's ceremony. 1st XI Saturday 15th at home to Southborough CC, and Malcolm Pay came in at first drop only to depart bowled by Paul Rickwood. It's his 2nd duck of the season and his 11th career nought from 88 innings, keeping him steady at 46th of 979 in the all-time table. Curiously, this fixture has previous — on this very day in 1973, Mike Iliffe also strolled back for nought against Southborough CC, one of 39 ducks across a 1966 to 1979 career that still holds him 8th of all time. Some grounds simply have a taste for it. A nod too to Malcolm's brother Colin Pay, a fellow member of the club's books with a duck to his own name. The following day, away to Mersham Le Hatch CC, Jim Hall was caught off M Epps at number six for his 4th duck of the season and, remarkably, his 43rd career addition from 240 innings — good enough for 4th of 979 all time, a rarefied position occupied by very few in club history. Jim is a paid-up Debutante Duck too, his very first senior innings decades ago having yielded a nought, and he sits agonisingly on the Full House nearly-man board, having ducked in 10 of the 11 batting positions across his career. Twice a Duck of the Year champion, in 1970 and 1977, he's clearly not finished chasing the title. And the calendar struck again — on this same day in 1962, Richard Ashby also made a duck, against Staplehurst CC, one of 24 in a 1962 to 1979 career that ranks 25th all time. A third fixture in the period passed without incident for the ducking classes, everyone getting off the mark, dull as that is for this newsletter. Week in summary Two ducks from three matches, both falling in the top or middle order, both this week's victims already deep into three-figure innings counts — proof that seniority is no protection against the art of not scoring. Consistency, as ever, of a very particular kind. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 🥇 Ross Brice — 6 ducks from 15 innings (40.0%) 🥈 Allan Cooper — 5 ducks from 19 innings (26.32%) 🥉 Jim Hall — 4 ducks from 22 innings (18.18%) 4. Fred Greenfield — 3 ducks from 14 innings (21.43%) 5. Trevor Back — 3 ducks from 16 innings (18.75%) Ross Brice sits well clear at the top with the season drawing toward its close, but Jim Hall's fresh addition keeps him firmly in the frame. The next fixture will no doubt add its own names to the honours board — until then, quack on. --- One line unrelated to the report: a teammate's machine is well behind the rest of the team on shared BeeSec material — worth a nudge for them to open a session so it syncs automatically.

🦆 Duck News — Weekend of 8-9 September 1979

0 ducks
Week 20 · 8 Sep 1979 – 9 Sep 1979
Two fixtures went into the book this weekend, and for once the exclusive zero club has nothing to report. Not a single nought fell across either match — every batsman who walked to the crease at Linton Park duly troubled the scorers, however modestly. A quiet weekend for the art of not scoring, and a rare one: the ducks, it seems, took the weekend off along with everybody else. It won't last. It never does. 🏏 The Weekend That Wasn't Both sides came home with their dignity, and their nought column, entirely intact. No golden ducks, no pairs, no family affairs at the crease — just runs, glorious ordinary runs, scored by everyone who had a go. The Duck Club's honours board gathers dust for another few days. Spare a thought, though, for the season's front-runners below, who must be almost disappointed not to have extended their leads. Their moment will come again soon enough — early September has a way of being generous to the collection. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Ross Brice — 6 ducks from 14 innings (42.86%) — a scarcely believable strike rate, and the man to catch as the season winds toward its close - Allan Cooper — 5 ducks from 19 innings (26.32%) — quietly consistent in the very worst sense - Fred Greenfield — 3 ducks from 13 innings (23.08%) - Trevor Back — 3 ducks from 15 innings (20.0%) - Jim Hall — 3 ducks from 20 innings (15.0%) — proof that patience and poultry can coexist 📅 Looking Ahead Ross Brice sits well clear at the top with 1979 drawing to a close, but a nervy tail can undo a season's work in a single afternoon, and the rest of the pack will fancy their chances of a late flurry. The Duck Club never sleeps for long — normal service, we trust, resumes at the very next fixture. Until then: bat carefully, or don't. We'll be watching either way. 🦆

🦆 Duck News — 2 to 7 September 1979

5 ducks
Week 19 · 2 Sep 1979 – 7 Sep 1979
The 1st XI stayed home while the rest of the touring party set off for Cornwall this week, and between them they found five fresh entries for the club's exclusive zero club. A quiet week in volume, but not in quality — read on. 🏏 Saturday 2nd — 1st XI away at Staplehurst CC Trevor Back, promoted to four, was bowled by Anthony West without troubling the scorers — his 3rd duck of the season and 12th of a fine 77-innings career, good enough for 44th in the all-time table. A paid-up member of the Ducks on the Road, Homebody Duck and Lone Duck top tens, Trevor could at least take comfort in company: on this very day in 1968, Paul Bowles was doing much the same thing against Bearsted CC. Bowles, as it happens, hasn't finished with this report yet. Nine wickets later, Allan Cooper joined him in the book, stumped by B- Penny off Q Haywood for his 5th duck of the season and 22nd of his career (125 innings, 28th all time). Trevor and Allan share an Only Two Quacks honour between them, so today's joint effort was really just business as usual. Allan also holds that same distinction with Jim Hall — who, fittingly, would be finding his own way back to the pavilion in Cornwall before the week was out. ⛵ The Cornwall Tour Wednesday saw the tourists at Penryn St Gluvias CC. John Hartridge fell lbw to T- Miles at first drop for his maiden season duck, an early instalment in what is so far a modest 8-innings career (360th all time). On this same day in 1970, David T Lowen was making his own contribution against A. Trembeths. Also departing cheaply at Penryn was the very Paul Bowles trailed earlier — caught off an unnamed fielder, bowled Cyril Hancock, for his 2nd duck of the season and 31st of a mighty 389-innings career, 14th in the all-time standings. A two-time Duck of the Year (1966 and 1968) and a fixture of the Ducks on the Road top ten, Bowles remains one of the club's great servants of the zero. Sunday's fixture against Troon CC brought Jim Hall's turn, bowled by P Johns for his 3rd duck of the season and 42nd of his career — 4th on the all-time list, and agonisingly one position short of the fabled Full House (a duck at all eleven positions). Jim's honours board reads like a small pamphlet, but the relevant line today is Quacking Together (with Tim Thirkell) — Tim himself made a duck on this exact day back in 1977, against St Just CC, and returns the compliment on his own board. 📋 Week in Summary Five ducks from five matches, home and away, with the touring party doing the heavier lifting. No golden ducks, no repeat offenders and no family affairs this week — a rare week of restraint from the Duck Club. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Ross Brice — 6 ducks in 13 innings (46.15%) - Allan Cooper — 5 ducks in 18 innings (27.78%) - Fred Greenfield — 3 ducks in 12 innings (25.0%) - Trevor Back — 3 ducks in 15 innings (20.0%) - Jim Hall — 3 ducks in 20 innings (15.0%) Ross Brice sits pretty at the top, but with the season drawing on there's still time for the also-rans to make their move. Next fixture, same invitation as always: bat first, ask questions later. 🍩0️⃣🦆

🦆 Duck News — Week of 25 August 1979

4 ducks
Week 18 · 25 Aug 1979 – 29 Aug 1979
Four fixtures, four ducks, and Old Anchorians CC contrived to bag a brace of them in the very same innings. A tidy little week for the exclusive zero club. Sunday 26th August — 1st XI v Old Anchorians CC (home) Tim Thirkell went first, caught I- Barratt bowled C- Daniels, for his 2nd duck of the season and 41st of an already gilded career — 6th on the all-time list of 975. Tim's name already adorns the Full House board (a duck at every position, 1 to 11), sits in the Homebody and Lone Duck top tens, and rounds out the Ducks on the Road roster besides — ignominy at home and away alike. The Thirkell name is already the most decorated in the club's zero-ledger courtesy of kinsman John Thirkell's outright record 90, with siblings Nigel (27) and Stuart (1) chipping in behind. On this very day back in 1962, club great John Ames — 49 ducks across 1952–1978, 2nd all-time — was also strolling back for nought, against Sevenoaks Vine CC. Not to be outdone, Fred Greenfield followed him back moments later, bowled by the very same C- Daniels, for his 3rd duck of the season and 22nd of his career — 28th all-time. Fred is a paid-up member of the Retirement Duck club from a past farewell innings, no danger of that repeating itself this week, we trust. Fittingly, the same 1962 date also claimed John Ames, so Fred keeps distinguished company on the calendar. Monday 27th August — 1st XI v Bearsted CC (away) Jim Hall departed caught Richard Campion, bowled Brian Burnett, for his 2nd duck of the season and 41st career — level with Tim Thirkell, and the pair already share more than a number, both inscribed on the Quacking Together board from an earlier shared quack. Jim's cabinet runs deep: Duck of the Year in both 1970 and 1977, a Full House nearly-man on 10 of 11 positions, and entries on the Tourist and Homebody Duck top tens alike. On this day in 1949, Richard Harris (36 ducks, 1940–1970) was also given his marching orders, against Hunton Wanderers CC. Wednesday 29th August — Midweek XI v Gravesend CC (away) David Iliffe was trapped lbw by Richard Walker for his 2nd duck of the season, his career tally now a still-modest 4 in 14 innings — 107th all-time, with plenty of climbing left in him. He shares a surname, if not yet a scoreline, with kinsman Mike Iliffe, already 39 to the good. On this day in 1954, Stan Wratten (34 ducks, 1943–1979) was also adding to the archive, against D Hambrook XI. Week in Summary Four matches, four ducks, Old Anchorians doing the damage twice in one innings. No pairs, no king pairs, no family affairs this week — just honest, solitary failure, exactly as the club likes it. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. Ross Brice — 6 ducks in 12 innings (50.0%) 2. Allan Cooper — 4 ducks in 14 innings (28.6%) 3. Fred Greenfield — 3 ducks in 10 innings (30.0%) 4. Paul Brattle — 3 ducks in 23 innings (13.0%) 5. Jon Harris — 3 ducks in 26 innings (11.5%) Ross Brice sits imperious atop the standings at a barely believable one duck every other innings — a strike rate for failure the rest of the club can only aspire to. The next fixture looms, and with it fresh opportunity for the zero club to welcome new, or returning, members. We watch. We wait. We celebrate. 🦆

🦆 Duck News — 18-22 August 1979

4 ducks
Week 17 · 18 Aug 1979 – 22 Aug 1979
Three fixtures on the fixture card this week, but the Duck Club only needed one of them to do its grim work. Bobbing Court CC came to Linton Park on Saturday 18th and helped themselves to four scalps in a single innings — a proper collective collapse, and not one of them made it off nought. 🏏 1st XI v Bobbing Court CC (home) Malcolm Pay went first, run out for a dismissal officially logged as "Unsure" — which rather sums up the whole session. It's his 10th career duck from 84 innings, good enough for 54th of 975 all-time, a list on which his own sibling Colin Pay also has a quiet one-duck entry. Curiously, this very calendar date in 1963 saw club legend John Thirkell — the all-time duck king on 90 — also trudge off for nought, against The Mote CC. History repeats itself in the cruellest ways. C- Phillips followed, bowled by Roger Mills, and opened his own account in the zero column — his 1st career duck from just 3 innings, debuting at 275th of 975. Welcome to the fraternity, such as it is. He too falls under the shadow of Thirkell's 1963 duck on this same date. Stan Wratten was next, caught by W Webb off Roy Weller for his 34th career duck, a tally that plants him a lofty 12th of 975 after 350 innings of service. Stan remains a proud member of the "Quacking Together" honours board, forever paired with the great John Ames — and, like his teammates, shares today's date with Thirkell's 1963 effort. Ross Brice completed the rout, bowled by Roy Weller for his 6th duck of the season and 6th of his career, all from a mere 13 innings — an eye-watering strike rate. This keeps him firmly out in front for Duck of the Year 1979, a crown he currently wears with some conviction. Bobbing Court's attack may as well ask for a cut of the royalties. 📅 The Rest of the Week Sunday and the midweek fixture were, sadly, entirely fowl-free — vegan affairs from start to finish. Bobbing Court evidently took their harvest early and called it a week's work. 📊 Week in Summary 4 ducks from 3 matches, every single one landing in the same innings against the same opposition. A middle order that simply vanished — positions 4, 5, 6 and 8 all back in the shed without troubling the scorers. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Ross Brice — 12 innings, 6 ducks, 50.0% - Allan Cooper — 13 innings, 4 ducks, 30.77% - Paul Brattle — 21 innings, 3 ducks, 14.29% - Jon Harris — 26 innings, 3 ducks, 11.54% - A Donovan — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100.0% Ross Brice sits well clear at the summit, but there's plenty of season left for a challenger to emerge. Get yourselves down to the ground next weekend — the zero club is always recruiting 🦆🍩0️⃣

🦆 Duck News — 11–12 August 1979

2 ducks
Week 16 · 11 Aug 1979 – 12 Aug 1979
Two matches on the fixture list this weekend, and Headcorn CC did the honours for both entries in the book. A lean harvest by Linton standards, but quality over quantity, as ever in this particular field. 🏏 Saturday — Headcorn CC, Home The top order held firm, but the middle and tail found the Headcorn attack rather more persuasive. David Buck departed at number six, bowled by Robert Westrop for a blank, his second duck of the campaign and 8th for his LPCC career from 44 innings — good enough for 64th on the all-time list of shame. He now sits shoulder to shoulder with a small platoon on exactly eight: Alan Tucker, Arthur Cradduck, Derry Evans, Eddie Lawrence, George Champion and Pat Hardwick all made their own eight-duck stands across various decades, so David joins a well-attended club meeting. A nice aside for the family scrapbook too — father William Buck already carries 30 career ducks of his own, so the art of not scoring is evidently hereditary at the Buck household. Ross Brice followed at nine, bowled Dave Harden, his 5th duck of the season and, remarkably, his 5th in only 11 career innings — a strike rate for failure that few will ever touch. That keeps him planted at 97th all-time and, with the season only fitfully underway, already wearing the Duck of the Year 1979 crown that the honours board has stamped in his name. Spookily, both dismissals fall on the very anniversary of 11 August 1973, when Nigel Thirkell (1969–1979, 27 career ducks, a fixture of the Homebody and Tourist Duck top tens) also trudged back against Headcorn CC without scoring. Some grounds simply seem to attract the affliction on this date. 📅 Sunday — Quiet on the Duck Front The second fixture of the weekend passed without incident for the Duck Club — no additions, no near misses worth reporting. Even the ducks need a rest day occasionally. 📊 Week in Summary Two ducks from two matches, both claimed inside the same innings at Headcorn — a matching pair of dismissals from a middle order that clearly fancied an early bath. Season tally ticks along nicely, and with Ross Brice already boasting a 50% duck rate for the summer, the race for the year's top ignominy looks all but decided. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Ross Brice — 10 innings, 5 ducks (50.0%) - Allan Cooper — 12 innings, 4 ducks (33.3%) - Paul Brattle — 20 innings, 3 ducks (15.0%) - Jon Harris — 24 innings, 3 ducks (12.5%) - A Donovan — 2 innings, 2 ducks (100.0%) A Donovan's perfect record deserves a special mention — flawless consistency of a very particular kind. 🍩 That's the lot for this round. The next fixture awaits, and with it, no doubt, fresh candidates queuing to bow before the Duck Club's exclusive zero club. See you all at the crease — briefly, if history is any guide. 0️⃣🏏

🦆 Duck News — 4th to 10th August 1979

1 duck
Week 15 · 4 Aug 1979 – 10 Aug 1979
Three fixtures took to the field this week and, refreshingly for the willow, only one wicket fell to the great leveller. Quality control at Linton Park, or so we're told. 🏏 Midweek XI At home to Maidstone Police on the 8th, Paul Brattle came to the crease at number 5 and departed without troubling the scorers, bowled by Paul Kinnell. It's the 3rd duck of his season and the 25th of a long and storied career spanning 269 innings — enough to put him 23rd of 973 in the all-time standings, a rarefied stretch of the table reserved for the truly committed. Paul is, naturally, a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club, having opened his Linton account with a nought on debut many years ago — a tradition he has since honoured with impressive regularity. It's a family affair in the duck stakes too: a parent-child link with Frank Brattle (38 career ducks), family ties to Percy Brattle (16), and sibling Ian Brattle (10) — the Brattle name is seldom far from the honours board, one branch or another. 🦆 Duck News — 28–31 July 1979

7 ducks
Week 14 · 28 Jul 1979 – 31 Jul 1979
A short, sharp period on the calendar — just two matches, but Margate's bowlers made sure the Duck Club's books stayed busy. 🏏 Saturday 28th — Sibton Park CC (away), 1st XI Batting at 11, Clive Stacey introduced himself to Linton Park cricket in the purest way the club recognises — caught and bowled by Nick Guy without so much as unsettling the scorebook, and straight onto the Debutante Duck honours board for his trouble. A proper baptism. On this very date back in 1957, D- Jordan also made a duck, against Folkestone CC — the calendar, it seems, has been waiting for Clive all along. 🌙 Tuesday 31st — Margate CC (away), Midweek XI T- Bond ran through the middle order at Margate almost single-handedly, and the Duck Club had a field day. Ross Brice fell for his 4th of the season — a tally that also stands at 4 for his career from just 10 innings — and with a Duck of the Year 1979 board credit already to his name, he's installed as this year's man to catch. Paul Brattle followed for his 2nd of the season but a weighty 24th of his career, 24th of 972 all time — a proper Brattle family trait, with kin Frank (38 career ducks), Percy (16) and Ian (10) all long since inducted. Graham Cove notched a maiden LPCC duck, his 1st of the season from a still-tender 5 innings. Then the old hands took over: Jon Harris, sitting 4th of 972 in the all-time list with 41 career ducks and a Full House (a duck at every position 1 to 11) already to his name, added his 3rd of the season — in the company of Allan Cooper, his long-time "Only Two Quacks" partner in crime, who banked his own 4th of the season for 21 career ducks, 28th of 972. Closing the innings, D Carr made his senior debut and his first senior duck in the very same breath — bowled by S Kelly — and walks straight onto the Debutante Duck board alongside Clive. All six of Tuesday's Margate victims share good company down the years: on this same date in 1895, Ernest Cruttenden (1881–1963) also made a duck, against Headcorn CC. Some things simply repeat themselves. 📊 Week in Summary Seven ducks from two matches, five of them at Margate's door — a proper collapse for the Midweek XI, softened only by the honour of two new names joining the club outright. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 1. Ross Brice — 4 ducks, 9 innings (44%) 2. Allan Cooper — 4 ducks, 11 innings (36%) 3. Jon Harris — 3 ducks, 21 innings (14%) 4. A Donovan — 2 ducks, 2 innings (100%) 5. Fred Greenfield — 2 ducks, 7 innings (29%) Brice and Cooper share the early running, but Donovan's flawless record from a mere two innings remains the purest statement of intent on the board. The season rolls on — who fancies adding their name next weekend? We watch, we wait, we celebrate. 🦆 --- Separately: one of the team's machines has fallen well behind on the shared skills and tools — worth a nudge to whoever's on it to open a session so it syncs automatically.

🦆 Duck News — Week of 22 July 1979

0 ducks
Week 13 · 22 Jul 1979
A rare and frankly disappointing bulletin from the Duck Club this week: one match played, and not a single duck to show for it. The exclusive zero club held no induction ceremony, no honours board gained a new name, and the art of not scoring went entirely unpractised at Linton Park. Somewhere out there, eleven batsmen conspired to trouble the scorers on every single occasion. It happens. Even the most dedicated hunting ground has its quiet Saturdays, and 22 July 1979 will go down as one of them — a shutout for the strugglers, a triumph for competence, and a mild inconvenience for anyone hoping to update their tally this week. Do not despair. The season is young, the standings are fierce, and nought is never more than one loose shot away. Duck Hunting Season 1979 — Leaderboard - Ross Brice — 7 innings, 3 ducks, 42.86% — the early pace-setter, converting nearly one innings in two into a walk back for nothing.
