Autumn's last hurrah at Linton Park, and the 2nd XI made sure the season didn't slip away without one final offering to the zero club. 🏏 2nd XI v Linton Park CC Openers beware — Brian Piper, aided and abetted by the safe hands of Tony Gauna, ran up a small production line at the crease this weekend, claiming two LPCC batsmen in the same manner within the same innings. A ruthless double act. First to go, at number two, was Ian Webb, caught Gauna bowled Piper for his 1st duck of the season and 3rd of an increasingly eventful career — now 138th of 960 in the all-time roll of dubious distinction, from 19 innings. Ian is a long-standing paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club, having opened his account with a nought back on debut, though this one's very much a repeat offence rather than a first. Keep it in the family — his relative Ken Webb also carries 3 career ducks, so the trait, such as it is, runs true. And in a fine bit of calendar symmetry, on this very day in 1977 Tim Thirkell — 39 ducks across 1967–1978, 6th on the all-time list, Duck of the Year 1972 no less — was doing exactly the same thing against Lordswood CC. One place down the order, John Bloomfield followed him back, caught Gauna bowled Piper for nought — his 5th duck of both the season and his career, from just 18 innings, and a leap to 94th of 960 overall. A rapid accumulation by any standard. Fittingly, this very fixture also produced an on-this-day echo: back in 1977, none other than his own teammate Ian Webb was recording a duck against Lordswood CC on the same date, then sitting on 3 for his career. History does like to rhyme in this club. 📊 Week in Summary Two matches, two ducks, one bowler-keeper combination doing all the damage. Modest numbers, but concentrated carnage — Piper and Gauna will want their names in lights, or at least in this newsletter, which is close enough. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. Keith Miller — 5 ducks, 14 innings (35.71%) 2. John Bloomfield — 5 ducks, 15 innings (33.33%) 3. Jim Hall — 5 ducks, 36 innings (13.89%) 4. Malcolm Pay — 5 ducks, 39 innings (12.82%) 5. Mike Iliffe — 3 ducks, 10 innings (30.00%) John Bloomfield's weekend effort keeps him snapping at Keith Miller's heels for top spot — the race for Duck of the Year is well and truly alive. Next fixture, fresh victims. The zero club never closes its books. 🦆🍩

4 ducks
Week 21 · 23 Sep 1978 – 27 Sep 1978
A quieter but no less ceremonious week for the exclusive zero club, with three fixtures in the period and four new entries to the ledger. Curiously, on this very day back in 1972, club legend Tim Thirkell also made a duck against West Farleigh — some anniversaries are best not celebrated twice. Batting at eleven, A Donovan opened his senior account in the most understated way possible, bowled by Norman Underdown for nought on debut. A duck first time out secures immediate and unarguable induction into the Debutante Duck club, a rite of passage as old as the fixture list itself, and sets him off at 236th of 960 all-time. He follows in family footsteps too — relative Terry Donovan already sits on 18 career ducks, so the art of the nought clearly runs in the blood. Remarkably, he shares his historical echo with teammate Bloomfield: two Linton batsmen, one 1972 ghost, one afternoon. 🌙 Wednesday 27th — Midweek XI v The Mote CC (away) Opening the innings — and, evidently, opening the account for the day — Paul Bowles was caught by David Morris off Roger Selleck without scoring. His 29th career duck moves him to a rarefied 17th of 960 all-time, propping up an honours cabinet that already includes back-to-back Duck of the Year titles in 1966 and 1968, a fixture on the Ducks on the Road top ten, and the celebrated Only Two Quacks pairing with Adam Pooley. Fittingly for an away-day regular, this one came on the road. On this same date in 1964, Robert Murray also departed for nought. At five, Malcolm Pay was bowled by Malcolm Bristow for his 5th duck of the season, drawing level with Jim Hall and Keith Miller at the top of the current Duck Hunting Season table, and his 9th career duck from 72 innings — good enough for 59th of 960. His sibling Colin Pay carries a single career duck of his own, so between them the Pay family keeps a cautious foot in the club. Like Bowles, Pay finds company in Robert Murray's 1964 duck — a ghost doing double duty this week. 📊 Week in Summary Four ducks from three matches, with West Farleigh and The Mote both taking their pound of Linton flesh. Two separate deliveries in the period found a decades-old echo waiting for them — the ghosts of ducks past clearly keeping their own fixture list. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Keith Miller — 5 ducks / 14 innings (35.71%) - Jim Hall — 5 ducks / 36 innings (13.89%) - Malcolm Pay — 5 ducks / 38 innings (13.16%) - John Bloomfield — 4 ducks / 14 innings (28.57%) - Mike Iliffe — 3 ducks / 9 innings (33.33%) Next fixture, next opportunity. 🦆 Duck Report — The Cornwall Tour, 9-10 September 1978

5 ducks
Week 19 · 9 Sep 1978 – 10 Sep 1978
The touring party pushed on into Cornwall this weekend and returned with exactly the sort of yield the Duck Club was founded to honour: five ducks in two days, a rare sibling double, and the club's own Duck of the Year extending their lead over the field. 🏏 Saturday 9th — Tour XI at Perranarworthal CC Keith Miller went first, bowled by B Bennett, a 4th duck of the season and 8th of a career now 20 innings deep, 58th in the all-time list of 955. Already installed as this season's Duck of the Year 1978, on this evidence the title is being defended with real commitment. Jim Hall followed, caught Brotherton off Copelin, a 5th duck of the season and a mighty 39th career duck from 216 innings — 5th on the all-time chart, a two-time former Duck of the Year (1970 and 1977), and a name so entwined with the honours board they have separate "Quacking Together" entries with three different teammates, Jon Harris among them, as proved again today. Then S Miller, bowled Sloggett, a 2nd duck from a Duck Club career only 2 innings old — a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck fraternity from their very first knock. Fittingly, the day was shared with sibling Keith: the Millers' joint failure earns a "Two of a Quack" entry on the family honours board, the rarest ceremony this club has to offer. Closing the innings, Jon Harris — caught Docking bowled Sloggett — brought up a 3rd duck of the season and 38th of a career (230 innings, rank 8 of 955) that already boasts the exceedingly rare Full House, a duck recorded at every position from 1 to 11. The habit runs in the family too: kin Richard Harris carries 36 career ducks of their own. On this very day in 1977, Andrew Moss also made a duck against Cornwall Crusaders — fitting anniversary company for all four names above. 🏏 Sunday 10th — Tour XI at Paul CC Keith Miller went again, run out for nought, completing a grim pair across the weekend's two fixtures — a 5th season duck, drawing level with Jim Hall, and a 9th career duck. On this same day back in 1955, John --'s Taylor also made a duck, against Old Roffensians. 📊 Week in Summary Five ducks from two matches, the touring party thoroughly restocking the zero column. The Miller siblings' shared failure is the headline of the weekend, Keith's pair the footnote nobody asked for. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. Keith Miller — 13 inns, 5 ducks (38.46%) 2. Jim Hall — 34 inns, 5 ducks (14.71%) 3. Malcolm Pay — 35 inns, 4 ducks (11.43%) 4. Mike Iliffe — 7 inns, 3 ducks (42.86%) 5. John Bloomfield — 13 inns, 3 ducks (23.08%) Keith and Jim share the season lead on ducks, but Keith's fearsome 38% strike rate keeps them out in front where it counts. The tour rolls on — who joins the club next? 🦆 --- Separately, and unrelated to the above: two other machines on the team have fallen behind on shared config — Kleptocrat1 (151 commits) and turbosammy-Defiance-Pro-16 (117 commits, 2 unresolved problems) — nothing to action here, just worth having whoever uses those machines start a session so it pulls automatically.

Seventy-six years earlier to the day, F E Wallis made a duck against Town Malling CC in 1902 — proof that this fixture list has always had a taste for symmetry. Week in Summary Three ducks from two matches, with Brian Piper doing the heavy lifting via his weekend pair, and David Iliffe opening his account at the death of the innings. No golden ducks, no king pairs, no family doubles this time — the Club will take its triumphs where it finds them. Ordinarily a two-match window doesn't leave much room for ceremony, but Sunday's trip to face Biddenden CC delivered a tidy little brace of noughts and a genuinely rare bit of company at the crease. 🌱 Sunday NVKC — Biddenden CC At number five, Malcolm Pay departed for his 1st duck of the season, caught P Curtis bowled D Fraser, and quietly slots in as the 91st most prolific quacker in club history on 5 career ducks from 36 innings. Consistency of a very particular kind, spanning over a century. And on this very day back in 1972, Alan Cradduck was also dismissed for nought — against Bobbing Court CC no less — en route to his own Duck of the Year in 1974 and a tidy 27 career ducks. History, as ever, repeats itself in the most unscoreable way. One place down the order, Jim Hall followed him back for his 1st duck of the season too, caught M Westrup bowled D Fraser, and continues his long and distinguished residency at 8th on the all-time leaderboard with a formidable 35 career ducks from 184 innings. Mr Hall is, frankly, a walking honours board in his own right — a Debutante Duck from way back, twice Duck of the Year (1970 and 1977), a fixture in the Ducks on the Road and Homebody Duck top tens, agonisingly one position shy of the full set in Full House, and a serial collaborator in no fewer than five separate Quacking Together partnerships. He now draws level on 35 with Jon Harris, another card-carrying member of the Full House club, in a meeting of two of the club's great and thoroughly ignominious careers. Same fixture, same bowler, same fate twice over — D Fraser clearly fancied his chances against the LPCC middle order that day, and the middle order duly obliged. 📊 The Week in Numbers Two ducks from two matches, both surrendered to the same Biddenden attack in the same innings. Five Duck of the Year titles (1952, 1954, 1955, 1967 and 1971) and top-ten residency in both the Ducks on the Road and Homebody categories confirm what the numbers already show: this is a man who has made an art of the nought. Fittingly, the family trade continues — son Tim Thirkell sits on 35 career ducks of his own, level with Jon Harris above, and Nigel Thirkell isn't far behind on 26. On this day in 1951, John --'s Taylor also fell for a duck, against Hunton Wanderers CC — small consolation for a man who has now outducked practically the entire club roster. 📋 The Week in Brief Three ducks, three different days, not a single repeat offender — a rare show of restraint from the Duck Club this week. 🦆 Duck News — 30–31 July 1977

A quiet weekend by the exclusive zero club's usual standards — just the one duck laid across two fixtures — but what it lacked in volume it made up for in pedigree. 🏏 Saturday 30 July — Away at Sibton Park CC The 1st XI's trip to Sibton Park brought the weekend's sole casualty. Neatly, this one arrived almost to the day of history repeating itself. On this very date in 1972, Andrew Moss — who turned out for the club 1968 to 1974 and finished with 9 career ducks, rank 52 of 939 — also trudged off for nought, against Glynde & Beddingham CC. Fittingly, he too shared today's date with Stan Wratten's 1954 effort at D Hambrook. The only other fixture of the weekend passed off entirely duck-free — a rare outbreak of competence LPCC will not be dwelling on. Week in Summary Two ducks from two matches, both from the same top order, both at Staplehurst. Tim Thirkell's effort draws him level at the top of this season's charts — the race for Duck of the Year is very much alive. 1 duck

🏏 Saturday 7th — away to Headcorn CC The 1st XI's trip to Headcorn produced two early casualties. A paid-up Debutante Duck, a Full House completist (a duck at every position, 1 to 11) and a fixture of both the Lone Duck and Tourist Duck top tens, Jon's history runs deep with two of Sunday's ducklings — long-standing "Quacking Together" and "Only Two Quacks" honours shared with Jim Hall and Allan Cooper respectively. Jim Hall (2nd of the season, 23rd career, 24th all-time) and Allan Cooper (3rd of the season, 14th career, 37th all-time) both departed without scoring in the very same innings — the pair already share an "Only Two Quacks" board from seasons gone, and duly renewed it. Jim remains the Full House nearly-man, agonisingly one position short. Both men's parallel points to Brian Piper, whose duck against Sennocke CC fell on this same date back in 1973. 🥇 Wednesday 11th — home to West Kent Wanderers CC, Midweek XI No name commands more respect in these pages than John Thirkell, and he obliged again — his 2nd duck of the season but a scarcely believable 88th of his career, still comfortably first of 930 on the all-time list. Five separate Duck of the Year titles (1952, 1954, 1955, 1967 and 1971) already grace his mantelpiece. Fittingly, his on-this-day parallel is his own flesh and blood — son Nigel Thirkell, who ducked on this exact date in 1973. Nigel (25 career ducks) and fellow son Tim (32) keep the family name well represented on the honours boards. Alongside him, David Buck opened his season's account with his 2nd career duck from just 6 innings — early days yet, but he comes from good stock, with father William Buck sitting on 28 of his own. By pure coincidence David's parallel is also Nigel Thirkell's 1973 duck. Week in Summary Six ducks fell across three matches. Two came in the very same innings at Sibton Park, and two father-son lines were quietly represented without either completing the set. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season 1976 — Top 5 1. 6 ducks

Three fixtures, six ducks, and the 1st XI shouldering the entire burden this week while the rest of the club watched on, suspiciously unscathed. On this very day in 1960, John Abnett (1954–1963) also walked back for nought against Halfway House — some anniversaries just won't quit. At 11, Jon Harris fell for his 3rd duck of the season, moving to 29 career ducks (12th of 927). Jon barely needs introducing to this column — Debutante Duck, Duck of the Year 1976, Full House, Homebody and Lone Duck top 10, Tourist Duck top 10, and twin Quacking Together entries with Jim Hall and Trevor Back. His father Richard carries 36 career ducks of his own, so clearly the apple hasn't fallen far. Jon shares Stan's 1960 Abnett anniversary too — a house of noughts, this one. 🏏 Sunday 13th June — away at Bobbing Court CC Paul Brattle opened the batting and opened his season's duck account in the same stroke, caught Weller bowled Elgar for his 1st of the season and 17th career (31st of 927) — a Debutante Duck of long standing. He joins a thoroughly stocked Brattle dynasty on the honours boards: father Frank on 38, kinsman Percy on 16, brother Ian on 9. On this day in 1971, Graham Abel also fell to nought against these very opponents — Bobbing Court seemingly has a taste for it. Debut boy G- Kemsley marked his LPCC bow with an immediate duck at 5, bowled Aylward — one innings, one duck, and a tidy double induction into both One and Done (1976) and Retirement Duck in a single afternoon. Efficient, if nothing else. Then Jon Harris strode out again at 9 and departed again, caught Gorf bowled Aylward, his 4th of the season and 30th career — a grim pair across successive days and grounds, YMCA Maidstone to Bobbing Court CC. The club salutes consistency of a very particular kind. 🏏 Tuesday 15th June — home to Hollingbourne CC Tim Thirkell, first wicket down, was bowled by Tony West for his 2nd duck of the season and 30th career, drawing level with Jon Harris on that very number. On this day in 1969, Frank Brattle also made a duck against Bobbing Court CC. Tim's own bloodline is a duck dynasty in miniature — father John holds the club's all-time record on 87, brother Nigel sits on 25, and kinsman Stuart on a lonely single. Tim adds Duck of the Year 1972, Full House, Homebody and Lone Duck top 10, and Ducks on the Road top 10 to an already crowded mantelpiece. 📋 Week in Summary Six ducks from three matches, every single one falling to the 1st XI — the 2nds, 3rds and 4ths got away scot free this week, which never lasts. Three fixtures went ahead across the long weekend and, remarkably, the exclusive zero club admitted only one new entry. This is Paul's 26th career duck in 247 innings, good enough for 17th on the all-time roll of 926, a list he has graced with genuine distinction: Duck of the Year in both 1966 and 1968, a fixture in the Ducks on the Road top 10, and one half of the Only Two Quacks pairing with Adam Pooley. Consistency of a very particular kind. Fittingly, on this very day in 1972 — four years to the date — Nigel Thirkell also strolled back for nought, against Bearsted CC, one of the 25 career ducks that has him sat just behind Paul at 21st in the all-time standings. 🌱 The Rest of the Weekend Monday's Spring Bank Holiday fixture and Tuesday's follow-up both passed without incident on the duck front — every batsman troubling the scorers at least once, which either speaks well of the batting or poorly of the bowling, we shan't speculate. A rare weekend where restraint, rather than ignominy, carried the day. Three matches, one duck: the quietest haul the club has logged in some time, and Paul Bowles stands alone as the weekend's sole representative of the art of not scoring. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 🥇 Allan Cooper — 2 ducks in 6 innings (33.3%) 🥇 Mike Iliffe — 2 ducks in 6 innings (33.3%) 🥉 Nigel Thirkell — 2 ducks in 10 innings (20.0%) 4️⃣ Ian Brattle — 1 duck in 1 innings (100.0%) — triumph through adversity, immediately 5️⃣ Stan Wratten — 1 duck in 2 innings (50.0%) A congested field at the top, with Cooper and Iliffe locked together and Brattle boasting the sort of duck rate the rest of the club can only admire from a safe distance. 🦆 Duck Report — 22 to 25 May 1976 🦆

2 ducks
Week 5 · 22 May 1976 – 25 May 1976
Three fixtures across the period, and the exclusive zero club welcomed just two new entries this week — economical in number, but both from the top order of Linton Park pedigree. 🏏 Saturday 22nd May — YMCA Maidstone (h) Jim Hall departed at number 2, bowled by Geoff Dearing, for his 1st duck of the season and 22nd of a long and admirably consistent career — good enough (or bad enough) for 25th on the all-time list of 926. Jim remains a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club from his own long-ago first innings, a former Duck of the Year (1970), and a fixture of the Lone Duck, Homebody Duck and Tourist Duck top tens — a duck for every occasion, home or away. He's also just one slot from Full House nearly-man honours, having now ducked from ten of the eleven batting positions available; number 2, it seems, still owed him one. On this very day in 1955, one John Abnett (1954–1963) was performing the identical ceremony against Halfway House, en route to 18 career ducks of his own. 🏏 Sunday 23rd May — Lordswood CC (h) If Jim provided the opener, John Thirkell provided the headline act. Caught P- Moore, bowled R- Hills, John notched his 1st duck of the season and, remarkably, his 87th for the club — a tally that sits utterly alone at the summit, 1st of 926, underwritten by five separate Duck of the Year titles (1952, 1954, 1955, 1967 and 1971). Ducking, for the Thirkells, is something of a family trade — fellow club members Tim (29 career ducks) and Nigel (25) keep the surname handsomely represented on the honours board. Back on this same date in 1959, Basil Sears (1947–1975) was registering his own nought against Gore Court CC, on his way to 33 for the club. The third fixture of the period passed off disappointingly duck-free — all batsmen present, correct, and irritatingly capable of getting off the mark. A quiet week by volume then — 2 ducks from 3 matches — but a heavyweight one by pedigree, with the club's most decorated collector of all time among the fallen. Triumph through adversity, as ever, is a two-way street. 8 ducks

Allan Cooper then ran himself out — the guilty fielder lost to the fog of scorebook history — for his 2nd of the season and 13th career duck. And at number 11, Ian Brattle was bowled for his 1st of the season, but the real headline sits on the board: his 9th career duck from a mere 15 innings, and the 7th in an unbroken row. 🦆 Duck Club Season 1976 Opens — 24-25 April

2 ducks
Week 1 · 24 Apr 1976 – 25 Apr 1976
Two Saturday fixtures marked the dawn of the 1976 Duck Hunting Season, and while most of the club escaped unscathed, the 1st XI's trip to Aylesford Paper Mills CC yielded the season's first brace of ducks, delivered back to back down the order. 🏏 1st XI — Aylesford Paper Mills CC (away, 25 April) At number six, Trevor Back was stumped — Cliff Anscombe swooping in behind the stumps off Colin Watson — for the season's opening duck. It's his first blob of 1976, and his third for the club in 13 innings, good enough for 147th on the club's all-time roll of ignominy. Trevor is a committee man of some standing down at Linton, holding top-ten places on both the Ducks on the Road and Homebody Duck boards — evidently he manages to duck wherever he's playing — and the Lone Duck top ten besides. Neatly, his "Only Two Quacks" honours-board partner is his own team-mate Allan Cooper, who was next out. And on this very date back in 1965, John Ames — 48 ducks across an era-defining 1952-1975 career, second on the all-time list — also trudged off for nought, against Maidstone AKCC. Distinguished company to keep, even in defeat. One place down the order, Allan Cooper followed him back for company, caught off a fielder recorded in the book only as "Unsure" off the bowling of A Keynes. It's Allan's first duck of 1976 too, and his twelfth in a 69-innings career, sitting 40th on the all-time list. He and Trevor share that same "Only Two Quacks" pairing on the board — and today they proved it, walking the same road a ball apart. Fittingly, the calendar repeated itself for Allan as well: this same date in 1965, that man John Ames again, also gone for nought against Maidstone AKCC. Some days the Duck Gods simply insist on a theme. 📊 Week in Summary A tidy two ducks from two fixtures, both from the same 1st XI innings, both middle order, both keeping suspiciously prompt company with one another on the honours boards. No pairs, no families, no golden ducks this week — just a dignified, matching brace to open the 1976 books. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard Early days yet, so it's a two-horse race at the top: - Allan Cooper — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - Trevor Back — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% Plenty of cricket left for the rest of the club to come charging through and knock this pair off their perch. 🦆 Next up: more scorecards, more nought-watch, and no doubt more names queuing for the honours board. The Duck Club never rests — see you next weekend.

Two fixtures, four ducks, and the closing weeks of the season proving that nobody is safe from the quack until stumps are drawn for the year. 🏏 Saturday — West Farleigh CC Jim Hall departed for nought at number five, bowled by Eric Mitchell, bringing up his 6th duck of the season and 21st in an LPCC career now spanning 121 innings — good enough for 25th in the all-time standings. 🦆 Duck Report — Saturday 13 September 1975

2 ducks
Week 21 · 13 Sep 1975
A tight afternoon at home to Southborough CC produced two additions to the exclusive zero club, and this week's card carries a distinctly familial flavour. 1st XI v Southborough CC (home) First to fall was John Thirkell, undone at four by Richard Russell for his 3rd duck of the season — a modest tally by his own extraordinary standards, given John sits proudly at #1 in the all-time Linton Park duck rankings with 85 to his name from 769 innings. A five-time Duck of the Year (1952, 1954, 1955, 1967, 1971), a fixture of the Ducks on the Road, Homebody Duck and Lone Duck top tens, and a paid-up member of the Quacking Together honours alongside Bob Arnold and William Buck, John remains the standard against which all Linton ducks are measured. On this very day in 1969, Derry Evans (1966–1971, 8 ducks, #59 all-time) also strolled back for nought against St Lukes Maidstone CC — the calendar has a long memory. Batting at six, son Tim Thirkell followed his father back to the pavilion, caught by Paul Willcock off the bowling of Terry Kingsmill. It's Tim's 7th duck of the season, vaulting him into a share of the season lead, and his 28th career duck, good for 14th on the all-time list from 181 innings. Tim carries the rare Full House board, a duck registered at every position 1 through 11, plus Duck of the Year honours from 1972 and a Quacking Together entry with Jim Hall. By curious coincidence, Tim shares his father's parallel exactly: Derry Evans made his nought on this same calendar date back in 1969 too. 🦆 A Family Affair Father and son, back to back, in the same innings against the same opposition — John and Tim Thirkell combine for a proper Duck and Ducklings, one of the rarest ceremonies the club has to offer. Between them the Thirkells carry 113 career ducks this afternoon, proof that whatever else runs in the family, so does the art of not scoring. Younger sibling Nigel Thirkell, a duck-club member in his own right with 23 to his name, will no doubt be taking notes. 📊 Week in Summary One match, two ducks, one thoroughly Thirkell weekend. Southborough's Russell and Kingsmill, with an assist from Willcock behind the stumps, can both chalk up scalps against Linton Park's 1st and 14th most prolific duck collectors of all time — not a bad afternoon's work for the visitors. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1975 1. Colin Dicker — 7 ducks, 22 innings (31.82%) 2. Tim Thirkell — 7 ducks, 41 innings (17.07%) 3. Nigel Thirkell — 6 ducks, 36 innings (16.67%) Tim Thirkell now shares the season lead with Colin Dicker on 7 apiece, though Dicker's fearsome strike rate keeps him marginally ahead on ignominy. With Nigel lurking in 5th too, the Thirkell name could yet dominate this year's Duck of the Year race three ways over. See you at the next fixture — the ducks are never far away. 🦆🏏

D- Masters can consider his week made. 1st XI v Medway Electricity (home, 1 June) Tim Thirkell, in at four, was taken by P- Hirons off Masters' bowling for his first blob of the summer — the 22nd of a career now standing at 149 innings and good enough for 23rd on the all-time chart of 911. Thirkell keeps distinguished company on the honours boards: Duck of the Year back in 1972, a Full House man for having now ducked in seemingly every position the order can offer, and a fixture in both the Homebody Duck and Lone Duck top tens. The surname is no stranger to the ledger either — between his kin John, Nigel and Stuart, the Thirkell clan has banked over a hundred career noughts of its own, so the talent, such as it is, runs in the family. On this very day in 1903, Rev W A Carr made exactly the same walk back against 1st Innings Maidstone CC — some anniversaries keep themselves. Three down at seven, Alan Cradduck fell to the same rampant Masters, bowled for his second duck of the season already. It's his 24th for the club from a brisk 85 innings, vaulting him to 18th all-time — just five places shy of Thirkell himself. A paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club from his very first innings, and Duck of the Year in 1974, Cradduck also shares the Reverend Carr's 1903 anniversary. Whatever the good vicar did to the cricketing gods that June, it's still working eighty years on. Elsewhere The other three fixtures across the period were, disappointingly, entirely vegan — not a single fowl among them. Perhaps everyone else was saving themselves for the leaderboard. In summary — two ducks, one match, one very busy bowler. The season tally ticks on. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Paul Croucher — 2 ducks / 4 innings (50%) - Alan Cradduck — 2 ducks / 6 innings (33.3%) - Benny Bell — 1 duck / 1 innings (100%) - Ian Brattle — 1 duck / 1 innings (100%) - Colin Dicker — 1 duck / 2 innings (50%) Croucher holds the summit for now, but with Cradduck already doubling up and Masters clearly steaming in with intent, this one has plenty of scorecard left to run. Allan Cooper (caught) notched his 4th of the season and 10th career, one of the club's serial "Only Two Quacks" partners. On this day in 1973, Paul Bowles made his own duck against Dimanchians — good company for this trio. The week in numbers 10 ducks across 3 matches — a proper cluster. Consistency of a very particular kind. His 1st duck of the season and 24th of a long and storied career — 201 innings deep and sat 16th on the all-time list. Fittingly, on this very day back in 1956, Richard Harris — 36 career ducks, 6th all-time, who played from 1940 to 1970 — was doing precisely the same thing against Marden CC. Paul Brattle followed almost immediately, bowled Hollbourne for nought — his 1st of the season, 12th overall, and 39th on the club's roll from 92 innings. Duck-club membership clearly runs in the family: kinsman Frank Brattle carries 38 career ducks, Percy Brattle 16, and brother Ian 1. Paul is also a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club from an earlier innings, and shares today's page in the history books with Harris's 1956 effort too. Down the order, R Fermor got to work. Allan Cooper went first, bowled for his 1st of the season and 7th career duck — 53 innings in, 63rd all-time. Allan is something of a serial offender in company, holding not one but three "Only Two Quacks" partnerships on the honours board, with Jim Hall, Jon Harris and Trevor Back all having shared the walk back with him over the years. Tony Gauna was next, trapped lbw by Fermor for his 1st duck of the season and 6th of his career from 43 innings, good for 77th on the all-time list — the honours board can wait. And completing Fermor's afternoon, Ron Hickman fell bowled for his 1st duck of the season but a hefty 23rd for his career, from just 51 innings — 19th all-time and no stranger to this column. Ron already shares a "Quacking Together" board with clubmate Alan Cradduck, and once managed a Runaway Duck season back in 1965 — an entire summer without a run to his name. He too, naturally, keeps company with Richard Harris's 1956 vintage. Week in summary Five ducks, one match, one bowler (R Fermor) doing for three of them down the order — a proper tail-end procession, and a banner day for the zero club if not for the scorebook. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Alan Cradduck — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - Gordon Dent — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - Ron Hickman — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - Allan Cooper — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% - Paul Bowles — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% A three-way tie at the summit — plenty of season left for someone to break clear. 🏏 Next fixture awaits, and with it the club's usual quota of nervous nineties in reverse. See you at the crease — or, more likely, back in the pavilion. 0️⃣🦆

2 ducks

Neatly, on this very day back in 1968, Cliff Anscombe made a duck against these same West Farleigh opponents, en route to a career haul of 24 and a place inside the top 15 all time. Cliff's own journey began with a Debutante Duck and included the 1957 Duck of the Year crown — Gordon has some way to go yet, but the calendar has drawn a neat line between them. 🏏 Sunday 28th — Aylesford Paper Mills CC (away) Alan Cradduck fell for nought at number nine, bowled by Grahame Clinton — his first duck of the young 1974 season and the 16th of his career in 63 innings, good enough for 29th on the all-time list. Alan is no stranger to this particular honour: a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club since his very first senior innings, he also owns a Ducks in a Row honour (five on the bounce, a fine run of utterly abject form) and once shared a Quacking Together entry with Ron Hickman. With the season only just under way, this outing plants an early flag in the 1974 Duck of the Year race — currently a field of one, and Alan's to lose. On this same calendar day in 1956, R Vincent also departed for nought against West Farleigh CC — a solitary 1956 season that still nets him 134th all time on 3 ducks. Different opposition, different era almost, same unmistakable result. 📋 Week in Summary Two matches, two ducks, both away from home, both falling to the 1st XI — a tidy if unspectacular start to the hunting season. No pairs, no family affairs, nothing yet to trouble the higher reaches of the honours board. Plenty of season left for that. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1974 1. Alan Cradduck — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% 2. Gordon Dent — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% Early days, but a flawless start for both — the kind of consistency the Duck Club holds dear. Saturday 28th July — away at Sibton Park CC The middle order took a battering at Sibton Park, with Rawlings doing the damage twice in short order. Colin Dicker went first, caught by Tim Wren off David Rawlings at number eight, for his third duck of the season and a career tally that now stands at 4 in just 12 innings — a strike rate for nought that keeps him comfortably in the current Duck of the Year 1973 conversation. He sits 91st in the all-time list, and on this very day back in 1957, D- Jordan was also walking back for a duck, against Folkestone CC, en route to a career total of 2. Charlie Le Milliere followed him back to the pavilion next ball, bowled by the same David Rawlings at number nine. A first duck of the season and, more notably, a maiden career duck from just 6 innings — welcome to the club, Charlie, rank 251 of 895 and counting. Fittingly, he shares that same 1957 echo as Colin: on this day, D- Jordan was out in exactly this fashion, proof that Duck Club anniversaries have a habit of doubling up. Sunday 29th July — away at The Mote CC Tim Thirkell offered no resistance at The Mote, bowled by R- Read at number seven for his second duck of the season and 19th of a considerable career built over 108 innings — good enough for 23rd on the all-time list. Tim is a fully paid-up honours-board fixture: a Full House man (a duck at every position, one to eleven), and a top-ten name in both the Ducks on the Road and Homebody Duck categories, with Duck of the Year 1972 already on the mantelpiece. Rather charmingly, his own father John Thirkell — the club's all-time number one with 81 career ducks — currently sits atop this very season's leaderboard, so the art of not scoring is evidently hereditary. On this day in 1963, Gordon Fenner also made a duck, against Birkenhead Grasshoppers CC, on his way to 34 for the club. Week in summary Three ducks from two matches, all three at Sibton Park and The Mote's expense, and Rawlings can rightly claim a brace of his own from the Saturday fixture. Nothing golden among them — every departing batsman at least troubled the scorers for a ball or two before troubling nobody at all with the bat. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - John Thirkell — 7 innings, 4 ducks (57.14%) - Jon Harris — 24 innings, 4 ducks (16.67%) - Colin Dicker — 9 innings, 3 ducks (33.33%) - Allan Cooper — 10 innings, 3 ducks (30.00%) - Alan Cradduck — 13 innings, 3 ducks (23.08%) John Thirkell leads the way, but with a whole season still to play there's ample time for the field to close in. 🦆 Duck News — 21–25 July 1973

1 duck

And in a fine bit of calendar symmetry: on this very day in 1956, John Abnett — of the 1954–1969 era, and a man who once reeled off four ducks in a row — also trudged off for a duck, against John Larkings' side. Abnett sits on 18 career ducks and 24th of 895 all-time. Seventeen years apart, same date, same fate. The zero club has a long memory. 📅 Week in Summary One duck from four matches is a lean return by Duck Club standards — the bowlers of Kent evidently had their minds elsewhere this week. Still, a single high-quality entry beats a dozen scrappy ones, and Cliff's contribution keeps the season ticking along nicely. 5 ducks

🦆 Duck Club Bulletin — 16 & 17 June 1973

2 ducks

A quiet weekend for the exclusive zero club — just two additions to report, both arriving in the same fixture. No honours board entries yet for Tony, but the numbers are climbing steadily. Fittingly, he shares his moment in history with Alan — on this very day in 1939, X Rayner was also falling to Castle Hill CC, Kent, on the way to a career that would end, as all the best ones do, in a Retirement Duck. A tidy little tail-end double at Bobbing Court, then — numbers 9 and 11 both walking back for nought in the same innings, proof that misery, much like the ball, does occasionally find company. 📊 Week in Summary Two matches, two ducks, both from the same fixture and the same beleaguered end of the batting order. 🦆 Duck News — 9th & 10th June 1973

3 ducks
Week 7 · 9 Jun 1973 – 10 Jun 1973
A tidy little harvest this week: two fixtures, three ducks, and every last one of them credited to the 1st XI. Modest in number, rich in pedigree — the art of not scoring is alive and well at Linton Park. Saturday 9th June — v Rumwood CC Mike Iliffe opened the weekend's account at number six, caught Don Clayton off S. Simmonds, departing without so much as a murmur from the scorebook. It's his first duck of the 1973 season and his 23rd in a career spanning 157 innings, good enough for 15th on the all-time list of 888 names — a place of dubious distinction, and one Mike now occupies rather comfortably. On this very day back in 1963, a young Ron Hickman was going through the same ritual against Gore Court CC, one of the 21 career ducks that carried him to 21st on the all-time honours board. History, it seems, enjoys an anniversary. Sunday 10th June — v Sheldwich CC Sheldwich's Jonathan Stanford evidently took a shine to Linton's lower order, helping himself to a brace for the Duck Club in the same innings. Jim Hall went first, caught J. Holt at number seven — his own first duck of the season and the 10th of an already storied career from 63 innings, moving him to 43rd all-time. Jim remains one of the club's great collectors, his honours cabinet groaning under the Lone Duck top 10, the Tourist Duck top 10, the Homebody Duck top 10, a Full House nearly-man credential and no fewer than three separate Quacking Together memberships, all resting atop a Debutante Duck pedigree from a long-ago first innings and a Duck of the Year title back in 1970. Two wickets later Alan Cradduck followed him through the gate, caught Brian Newman off the same rampant Stanford, for his second duck of the season and 13th of his career, edging him to 33rd on the all-time list. Alan brings his own Debutante Duck credentials plus a place in the select Ducks in a Row club for five on the spin, and holds a Quacking Together honour with none other than Ron Hickman — the very name Mike Iliffe was echoing from 1963 earlier in this report. Small club, the zero club. Fittingly, both Jim and Alan can trace a shared footstep back to this same date in 1961, when Robert Wood was doing exactly likewise against Tovil — one of 21 career ducks that carried him to 20th on the all-time list, and, like Jim, a fellow Debutante Duck alumnus. Week in summary Three ducks, two matches, one very satisfied Sheldwich bowler. The 1st XI cornered the market entirely this week — the 2nd, 3rd and 4th XIs will presumably want a word about pulling their weight. 🦆 Duck News — Weekend of 19–20 May 1973

1 duck
Week 4 · 19 May 1973 – 20 May 1973
A quiet weekend by Duck Club standards — two fixtures, one nought — but when the club's own top-ranked ambassador of ignominy is the one supplying it, one is plenty. 🌱 Sunday — NVKC v Addington Village CC John Thirkell, LPCC's undisputed record holder — sitting 1st of 884 in the all-time standings — walked in at number two and departed bowled by J Dicker without troubling the scorers. It's his 2nd duck of the current season and his 79th in a career now spanning 711 innings, a rate of consistency the rest of the club can only stand back and admire. Five-time Duck of the Year (1952, 1954, 1955, 1967 and 1971), a fixture of the Ducks on the Road, Homebody Duck and Lone Duck top tens, and a dual member of the Quacking Together honours alongside both Bob Arnold and William Buck — John's name on the board is less an entry than a permanent fixture. The name runs deep in these parts too: sons Tim (17 career ducks) and Nigel (7) are both paid-up members of the club in their own right, so quite how anyone gets a ball past this family remains one of Linton's enduring mysteries. And in a pleasing quirk of the calendar — on this very day in 1969, Mike Iliffe (1966–1973, 22 ducks, 16th all-time) also made a duck, against West Farleigh CC. The duck, it seems, always knows what day it is. 📊 Weekend in Brief Just the one duck from two matches this weekend — a modest harvest, though quality has never troubled John Thirkell where quantity is concerned. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard — Top 5 1. John Thirkell — 3 innings, 2 ducks (67%) 2. David Stevens — 1 innings, 1 duck (100%) 3. Brian Fuller — 2 innings, 1 duck (50%) 4. Allan Cooper — 3 innings, 1 duck (33%) 5. Ken Webb — 3 innings, 1 duck (33%) David Stevens leads on a flawless percentage so far, but with John Thirkell setting the pace on volume, the race for Duck of the Year 1973 is only just getting started. 🍩 Same time next weekend, then — bats at the ready, ducks at large. See you out there. 🦆

They always do. 🏏 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 🏏 Still very much live at the top of the table this season: 1️⃣ John Thirkell — 6 ducks from 17 innings (35.29%) — the early pace-setter, making a proper habit of it 2️⃣ Alan Cradduck — 5 ducks from 14 innings (35.71%) — technically the higher strike rate, if that's a thing worth boasting about 3️⃣ Dick Langridge — 3 ducks from 10 innings (30.00%) 3️⃣ Nigel Thirkell — 3 ducks from 10 innings (30.00%) — the Thirkell name doing rather too much work on this table 5️⃣ Mike Iliffe — 3 ducks from 17 innings (17.65%) — getting there on volume alone A reminder that this table exists purely in the spirit of celebration, never shame. Consistency of this particular kind is its own sort of achievement. 0️⃣ A week for the "nearly men" of the honours board to breathe easy, and for the rest of us to wonder who'll be first to break the drought. 🦆 Duck News — August Bank Holiday Weekend 1971

4 ducks
Week 18 · 28 Aug 1971 – 30 Aug 1971
The traditional Bank Holiday triple-header did what it always does and delivered a tidy little harvest for the exclusive zero club — four ducks across three matches, Linton Park once again proving that runs are optional and ignominy is forever. 🏏 Sunday 29th — Staplehurst CC (away) Mike Iliffe went early at four, run out for the second time this season — a chaotic dismissal that at least spares him any blame for shot selection. It's his 18th career duck, tucking him into 23rd spot on the all-time list of 867, and on this very day back in 1954 Stan Wratten was doing exactly the same thing against D Hambrook XI. Some traditions simply refuse to die. 🎗️ Monday 30th — Bank Holiday at Bearsted CC (away) A proper Bank Holiday massacre, this one, with three names added to the list in a single innings. Leading the charge, inevitably, was John Thirkell — caught Mick Gibson, bowled Bryan Elswood, for his 6th duck of the season and 73rd of a career that already sits him unrivalled at the very top of the all-time standings, number 1 of 867. The reigning Duck of the Year for 1971 extends his own lead over his own field, a man competing largely with his own legend at this point, and a proud member of the Quacking Together set alongside both Bob Arnold and William Buck down the years. On this day in 1965 Frank Brattle also fell to nought against these very same Bearsted opponents — the ground clearly has form. Not far behind him, Richard Ashby was bowled by Derek Morgan for his first duck of the season, the 24th of his career and good enough for 13th on the all-time list. Already a fixture of the Ducks in a Row club for five in succession, and a regular in the Tourist Duck top 10 — fitting, given this one came on the road too. He shares Brattle's 1965 anniversary with Thirkell above. And propping up the innings at number 11, Alan Wilkes fell to the very same Derek Morgan — the bowler's second scalp of the afternoon — for his own first duck of the season, his 22nd career, 14th on the all-time roll. A veteran of the fabled 1964 Runaway Duck campaign, when he contrived to go an entire season without a run, and a paid-up member of Only Two Quacks with both Bob Arnold and John Ames. He too keeps Frank Brattle company from 1965. 📊 Week in Summary Four ducks, three matches, one very productive Bank Holiday Monday for Derek Morgan, who accounted for two of Bearsted's victims personally. Staplehurst managed one scalp by more chaotic means entirely. A quiet weekend for everyone except the scorebook's zero column. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. John Thirkell — 6 ducks / 16 innings (37.5%) 2. Alan Cradduck — 5 ducks / 11 innings (45.45%) 3. Dick Langridge — 3 ducks / 9 innings (33.33%) 3. Nigel Thirkell — 3 ducks / 9 innings (33.33%) 5. Cliff Anscombe — 3 ducks / 19 innings (15.79%) Thirkell leads by tally, but Cradduck's strike rate remains the more terrifying statistic of the two. Roll on next weekend — the ducks never take a Bank Holiday off, and neither should you. 🦆🍩

🦆 Duck News — 22 to 25 August 1971

5 ducks
Week 17 · 22 Aug 1971 – 25 Aug 1971
Two fixtures, five ducks, and Linton's exclusive zero club took in three new arrivals in a single Wednesday innings that Gravesend will remember fondly. As ever, the art of not scoring found its practitioners. Saturday 22 August — 1st XI away at Mersham Hatch David T Lowen departed at first wicket down, bowled by W Jeanes, for his 1st duck of the season and 3rd of an otherwise perfectly respectable career — 34 innings deep, ranked 115th of 867 in the all-time reckoning. On this very day in 1953, J Barclay was doing much the same against Charles Arkcoll, en route to 7 career ducks and the 1953 Duck of the Year crown before bowing out, as tradition dictates, on a duck of his own. Down at number 11, Percy Brattle offered token resistance before falling to B Campbell — his 1st of the season, 16th of a career that has already earned him the 1969 Duck of the Year sash and 26th spot in the all-time table. The Brattle name runs deep in these parts: father Frank carries 38 career ducks of his own, with kinsman Paul adding 4 more to the family ledger. Percy, too, finds a companion in history — J Barclay, 1953, same day, same fate. Wednesday 25 August — Midweek XI at home to Gravesend CC A proper collapse into the zero club here, with three ducks inside one innings. David Tolhurst, bowled by Kevin Jarvis, recorded his 1st duck of the season — and, remarkably, his 2nd in just 2 career innings, a flawless 100% record so far. A long-standing paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club from his first senior knock, he now finds company on this same calendar date back in 1904, when T Woollett suffered identically. Dick Langridge, trapped lbw by the same Kevin Jarvis, brought up his 3rd duck of the season and 20th of a long career — 134 innings and counting, 18th on the all-time list. Son Barry has 6 career ducks of his own, so the trait is evidently hereditary. Dick, too, tips his cap across the decades to T Woollett's 1904 effort. Nigel Thirkell completed the rout, bowled by John Casely, for his 3rd duck of the season and 5th career nought from just 18 innings, ranking 78th all-time. Nigel is a fixture of the Homebody Duck and Tourist Duck top tens, and shares his Only Two Quacks distinction with clubmate Jim Hall. The surname carries some weight in these records — father John Thirkell sits top of the all-time pile with a scarcely believable 72 career ducks, while sibling Tim adds 11 more, and kinsman Stuart a further 1. Nigel, like his teammates, joins T Woollett on this day in 1904. Week in summary Five ducks from two matches, with Kevin Jarvis alone accounting for two of Gravesend's victims, and Dick Langridge and Nigel Thirkell both advancing to their 3rd of the season in the very same innings — misery, it seems, loves company. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 1. Alan Cradduck — 5 ducks / 10 innings (50.0%) 2. John Thirkell — 5 ducks / 15 innings (33.3%) 3. Dick Langridge — 3 ducks / 9 innings (33.3%) 4. Nigel Thirkell — 3 ducks / 9 innings (33.3%) 5. Cliff Anscombe — 3 ducks / 19 innings (15.8%) Alan Cradduck still leads the chase, but with the Thirkell dynasty stacking ducks at both ends of the order, the race for 1971's crown is far from settled. 🦆 Duck Club Dispatch — 8th to 11th August 1971 🏏

2 ducks
Week 15 · 8 Aug 1971 – 11 Aug 1971
Only two fixtures on the card this week, and only one of them misbehaved — but it more than made up for the quiet one. Saturday 8th August — 1st XI v Sibton Park CC (home) The afternoon's first casualty was John Thirkell, undone at number 5 by P McKen. It's their 5th duck of the summer and the 72nd of an extraordinary career spanning 682 innings — a tally that sits them at number 1 of 865 in the entire LPCC record book. The honours board reads like a roll of dishonour in itself: Duck of the Year in 1952, '54, '55 and '67, a fixture in the Ducks on the Road, Homebody Duck and Lone Duck top tens, and joint custodian of Quacking Together with both Bob Arnold and William Buck. With the club deep in the 1971 season, their board already carries a Duck of the Year 1971 entry too — evidently this campaign belongs to them, running at a positively economical 11% duck rate for the all-time leader. Neatly, on this very day back in 1892, Jack Fryer — who played 1881-1906 and finished with 12 career ducks, good for 33rd all time — also strolled back for nought, against Royal Engineers CC. History repeating itself, as it so often does in the Duck Club. But the real story came one place later. At number 6, Tim Thirkell followed straight after, bowled by G Keutenius — and given the family connection to John, this is instantly a Duck and Ducklings moment, a parent and child both back in the hutch in the very same innings, a ceremony the club offers all too rarely. Tim's duck is their 1st of the season and 11th of the career from 48 innings, a 23% strike rate placing them 38th of 865 all time. They're also a fully paid-up member of the Full House club, having now made a duck from every position 1 through 11 in a Linton career, and keep regular company in Quacking Together with Jim Hall. Fittingly, they share their on-this-day company with John — Jack Fryer's 1892 nought at Royal Engineers CC covers the whole family this time round. For the record, sibling Nigel already carries 4 career ducks and family member Stuart 1 — clearly a household that takes to the crease with quiet ambition and leaves it rather more quietly still. Week in Summary Just the two ducks recorded this week, and both fell in the very same innings, to the very same family. The other fixture of the period passed off entirely fowl-free — a rare and presumably relieved outcome for whoever was watching. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 🏆 - Alan Cradduck — 5 ducks / 9 innings (55.56%) - John Thirkell — 5 ducks / 14 innings (35.71%) - Cliff Anscombe — 3 ducks / 18 innings (16.67%) - Graham Abel — 2 ducks / 4 innings (50.0%) - Ron Hickman — 2 ducks / 4 innings (50.0%) Cradduck leads for now, with Thirkell snapping at their heels — that battle looks set to run the length of the season. 🦆 Same time next fixture, same dubious honour up for grabs. Get your ducks in a row, Linton — or rather, don't. 0️⃣

Thirkell, who graced Linton Park from 1943 to 1970, sits proudly at #1 of 857 all-time with a staggering 67 career ducks and no fewer than four Duck of the Year titles to his name (1952, 1954, 1955, 1967) — proof, if proof were needed, that even the very greatest of failures can become a career. 📊 Week in Summary One duck from three matches is a lean return by Duck Club standards — the other two fixtures passed by disappointingly fowl-free. Still, quality over quantity: O'Toole keeps the season ticking over nicely. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard — Top 5 1. David Piper — 4 ducks / 13 innings (30.77%) 2. 5 ducks

Two fixtures, five ducks, and the 1st XI shouldering the entire weekend's ignominy. The exclusive zero club opens its books once more. 🏏 Saturday — away at Beverley CC, Kent Last man in, last man to fall: Brian Fuller departed at number 11, bowled by R- Gawler, for his 2nd duck of the season and 6th of a career now spanning 20 innings — 61st on the club's all-time roll of dishonour. Back on this same 12 July in 1964, Len Conway (1954-1965, 12 ducks, and a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club) suffered an identical fate. Then B Formoy went to work like a fox loose in the henhouse. Terry Groves fell to him for his 5th career duck from 19 innings, good for 78th all-time — sharing that same 12 July 1964 duck-date with Conway. Jon Harris followed, also bowled Formoy, for his 7th career duck in 25 innings and 56th on the all-time roll — no small feat for a man who already owns a Full House (a duck at every position 1 to 11), sits in the top 10 for both Lone and Tourist Ducks, and carries lifetime membership of the Debutante Duck club from a debut long since forgotten. A relative, Richard Harris, already has 36 career ducks to his name, so the aptitude clearly runs in the blood. Completing what amounted to a Formoy hat-trick of sorts, Nigel Thirkell went the same way at number 8, his 2nd career duck from just 5 innings, adding his name to the Homebody and Tourist Duck top 10s — every bit the family business, with relative John Thirkell (67 career ducks), sibling Tim (7) and family member Stuart (1) all having blazed the trail before him. Fittingly, Nigel too shares this Conway-vintage date of 12 July 1964. 📊 Week in Summary Five ducks from two matches, three of them harvested by B Formoy in a single devastating spell — the kind of burst that empties a top order and fills the Duck Club register in one visit. The 1st XI carried the whole weekend unassisted, top to bottom of the order. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Jim Hall — 4 ducks from 9 innings (44.4%) - Benny Bell — 4 ducks from 14 innings (28.6%) - Alan Cradduck — 3 ducks from 10 innings (30.0%) - Frank Brattle — 3 ducks from 16 innings (18.8%) - Andrew Moss — 3 ducks from 23 innings (13.0%) Jim Hall sets the pace for now, but the season has miles left to run. Three fixtures, four ducks, and the Rumwood CC clash proving a particularly fertile hunting ground for the men in white. The 1st XI carried the entire burden this week — let's get into it. 🏏 Saturday 6th June – Rumwood CC (Home) Frank Brattle fell at first drop, bowled by M. Wells for his 3rd duck of the season and 37th of an illustrious career spanning 347 innings — that's 5th in the club's all-time roll of dishonour. On this very day back in 1967, none other than the legendary John Thirkell — the club's undisputed number one duck-getter with 66 to his name — was also trudging back against Civil Service CC, Kent. Good company to keep, Frank, if company on nought can ever be called good. Down at seven, Benny Bell edged behind off K. Lane to register his 2nd of the season, moving to 17 career ducks and a very tidy 20th on the all-time list. Same calendar date, same John Thirkell parallel — 1970 really is shaping up to be the summer of ghosts from '67. And at eight, debutante-in-spirit David Piper continued a torrid start to senior cricket, caught Venner bowled Carter for his 2nd duck of the season, level with his career tally of 2 from just 5 innings — an eye-watering 40% strike rate for the art of not scoring. Early days yet, David, but the Duck Club welcomes all comers. 🏏 Saturday 6th–Monday 8th June – Boughton Monchelsea CC (Home) Rounding out the innings, veteran Ron Hickman was bowled by Trevor Back at number ten for his 1st duck of the season, his 13th career nought from 31 innings — 31st all-time and a paid-up member of both the "Quacking Together (with Alan Cradduck)" honour and the eternally grim "Runaway Duck 1965" board, the season he went an entire summer without troubling the scorers. On this day in 1969, Fred Greenfield was doing much the same against Hartley Country Club — Fred's since gone on to join the Retirement Duck club, so Ron can at least take comfort he's not there yet. 📊 Week in Summary Four ducks from three matches, and Rumwood CC clearly fancy themselves as duck-hunters — three of the week's four fell to them alone. The 1st XI monopolised proceedings entirely; the 2nds, 3rds and 4th were, disappointingly, vegan this week. No pairs, no king pairs, no family affairs to report — just honest, solitary failure, the purest form the Duck Club has to offer. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard – Top 5 1. Frank Brattle — 9 innings, 3 ducks, 33.33% 2. David Piper — 5 innings, 2 ducks, 40.0% 3. Jim Hall — 5 innings, 2 ducks, 40.0% 4. Richard Ashby — 5 innings, 2 ducks, 40.0% 5. Benny Bell — 7 innings, 2 ducks, 28.57% A tight scrap at the top with three men locked on 40%. Someone needs to break clear or nick a run to spoil the fun entirely. 🍩 Until next time, the crease remains open and the Duck Club's doors ever wider. Who fancies joining the exclusive zero club next weekend? We watch. We wait. We celebrate. 🦆0️⃣

🦆 LPCC Duck Club Bulletin — 30 May to 4 June 1970

4 ducks
Week 5 · 30 May 1970 – 4 Jun 1970
A tidy little haul this week, and the honours board is busier than the pavilion tea urn. Four ducks, all in claret and blue for the 1st XI, and one of them arriving in company — the rarest kind of nought the club has to offer. 🏏 1st XI — A Busy Week for the Zero Club Tim Thirkell opened the account against Tovil, caught behind for nought — his 1st duck of the season and 7th of an increasingly distinguished career, moving him to 55th on the all-time list. Tim sits on a proper honours-board CV: the Full House (a duck at every position 1-11), spots in the Lone Duck and Homebody Duck top tens, plus Ducks on the Road, and a shared Quacking Together entry with Jim Hall. On this very day in 1955, John Thirkell — the club's all-time duck king with 66, and no stranger to Tim's own family tree — was busy doing exactly the same thing against Marden. The art of not scoring, it seems, runs in the blood. Then came Hythe CC, and a genuine club rarity — a Duck and Ducklings double. Frank Brattle, lbw for nought at number 6, brought up his 2nd duck of the season and a mighty 36th of his career, good for 5th on the all-time roll — level with Richard Harris (1940–1969) on the same tally. Moments later Percy Brattle, caught and bowled at number 9, notched his 1st duck of the season and 14th career, climbing to 27th all-time and adding to his existing Duck of the Year 1969 honour. Parent and child, back to the pavilion in the same innings — the Duck and Ducklings ceremony doesn't get performed often, and it's a proper feather in the family cap. Both, fittingly, share the same on-this-day parallel — Benny Bell also ducked on this date in 1969, against Tovil of all sides. Andrew Moss rounded things off against Tovil Nomads, caught for nought at first drop — his 2nd duck of the season and 3rd career, now 104th on the all-time list and a paid-up member of the Retirement Duck club from a past farewell. On this day in 1903 — a full 67 years earlier — Rev W A Carr was doing precisely the same thing against Maidstone's 1st Innings. Some traditions really do run deep at Linton Park. 📋 Week in Summary Four matches, four ducks, one of them a full-blown family occasion. The 1st XI cornered the market entirely this week — 2nd, 3rd and 4th XIs escaped unscathed, for now. A quiet week for the Duck of the Year race, but plenty of movement lower down the honours board. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Jim Hall — 2 ducks in 4 innings (50%) - Richard Ashby — 2 ducks in 5 innings (40%) - Frank Brattle — 2 ducks in 7 innings (28.57%) - Andrew Moss — 2 ducks in 12 innings (16.67%) - Nigel O'Toole — 1 duck in 1 innings (100%) 🍩 Next up, more fixtures and no doubt more volunteers for the zero club. Get out there, middle it or don't — either way, we'll be watching. 0️⃣🦆

5 ducks

🦆 Duck News — 16 to 19 May 1970

3 ducks
Week 3 · 16 May 1970 – 19 May 1970
Only one team went hunting this week, but the 1st XI made it count with three ducks in two matches — and one of them arguably the biggest name in club history. 🏏 Saturday 16 May — Headcorn CC John Thirkell fell first, bowled by Brown for nought batting at four. Hardly news to John, who sits at the very summit of the all-time standings with 66 career ducks from 639 innings — a peak few will ever trouble. A four-time Duck of the Year alumnus (1952, 1954, 1955, 1967) and a fixture of the Lone Duck, Homebody Duck and Ducks on the Road top tens, he shares his "Quacking Together" honours with none other than Bob Arnold. Fittingly, on this very day in 1959 Arnold himself — the club's second-highest scorer with 47 career ducks across 1949–1964 — was also trudging back for nought, against Gore Court CC. The duck gene runs in the family too, with kin Tim (6 career ducks) and Nigel Thirkell (1) both carrying the torch. Jim Hall followed him back soon after, bowled by Sparks for nought batting at ten — agonisingly close to completing the Full House, having now ducked in 10 of the 11 batting positions. It's his 4th career duck from 27 innings, and with the "Duck of the Year 1970" board currently bearing his name, he's the early pace-setter in this season's race for dubious glory. Elsewhere on 16 May, back in 1959, Bob Arnold was busy adding to his own tally against Gore Court — Jim keeps good historical company. 🏏 Sunday 19 May — Loose CC (away) Benny Bell edged behind for nought at number two, caught Crouch bowled Wolford. His 16th career duck from 59 innings puts him 23rd on the all-time list. On this same day back in 1951, Gordon Bugge (1946–1953, 3 career ducks) was also dismissed without scoring, against Aylesford Paper Mills CC. 📋 Week in Summary Three ducks, two matches, all courtesy of the 1st XI — and two of them fell in the very same innings against Headcorn. Not quite an epidemic, but the season's zero column keeps ticking over nicely. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Alan Cradduck — 1 duck / 1 innings (100%) - David Piper — 1 duck / 2 innings (50%) - Graham Mountford — 1 duck / 2 innings (50%) - Jim Hall — 1 duck / 2 innings (50%) - Richard Ashby — 1 duck / 2 innings (50%) Next fixture awaits, and with it, no doubt, further additions to the ledger. 🦆 Duck Report — Saturday 9th May 1970

3 ducks
Week 2 · 9 May 1970
Rumwood CC away day, and the exclusive zero club welcomed three new subscriptions in the very same innings — a miserable afternoon for the middle and lower order, but a rather good one for the honours board. 1st XI at Rumwood CC David Piper, promoted to first wicket down, fell to David Gale to open the day's account — his 1st duck of the season and, in what is still very much an infant career, his 1st in just 2 innings. That plants him 243rd of 852 on the all-time list, with plenty of ignominy still to accrue. Neatly enough, on this very date in 1959 Brian Mills was doing precisely the same thing, one of four career ducks for a man who himself began life at Linton with a Debutante Duck. Richard Ashby followed at number 8, lbw to the same David Gale — greedy work from the bowler, generous work from the batting order. It's Richard's 1st duck of the summer, but his 21st for the club in a marathon 158 innings, a tally lofty enough to sit 13th of 852 all time. He remains a proud member of Ducks in a Row (five consecutive, no mean feat of consistency) and the Tourist Duck top 10. And once again, 9th May 1959 echoes down the years — Brian Mills, keeping Richard company across the decades. Then at number 9, history of a different kind: Graham Mountford, bowled Don Clayton, opens his senior account with a duck on debut, earning immediate and permanent induction into the Debutante Duck club. Not the start anyone dreams of, but a start nonetheless, and one shared — appropriately — with Brian Mills, who marked this same calendar date back in 1959 in exactly the same fashion. Week in Summary Three ducks from a single match, David Gale personally responsible for two of them — a fine day with the ball, a torrid one for Linton Park's top order. No pairs and no family affairs to report this week, just a clean sweep through the middle and lower order. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Alan Cradduck — 1 duck from 1 innings (100%) - Graham Mountford — 1 duck from 1 innings (100%) - Richard Ashby — 1 duck from 1 innings (100%) - David Piper — 1 duck from 2 innings (50%) - Andrew Moss — 1 duck from 4 innings (25%) Still early days in the hunting season, with five names locked at the top and nothing to separate them but innings played. The next fixture awaits its own inevitable additions — until then, bat straight, watch the honours board, and beware David Gale. 🦆🍩0️⃣

🦆 Duck Report — 2 to 5 May 1970

Slim pickings on the calendar this week, but the 1st XI made sure the exclusive zero club took delivery of three fresh members between Bobbing Court and Maidstone Police. 1st XI At Bobbing Court CC (away, 3rd May), Andrew Moss opened the batting and departed just as promptly, stumped by T Ades off P Bedelle. His 1st duck of the season and 2nd of a 41-innings career, good enough for 135th of 851 in the all-time table. Andrew already keeps a seat reserved in the Retirement Duck wing from a past farewell — no danger of that today, just business as usual. Maidstone Police then visited Linton Park (home, 5th May) and left with a brace. Mike Iliffe, at six, was bowled by G Mountford — his 1st of the season and 13th for the club from 80 innings, edging him up to 29th of 851 and within sight of the top 25. Curiously, on this exact date in 1956, Richard Harris also strolled back for nought, against Marden CC Kent, en route to a mighty 36 career ducks. Then came Alan Cradduck at number eight, bowled by Cruttenden — and since this was his maiden senior innings, it's a genuine Debutante Duck, first ball of a career answered with the very worst kind of welcome. He's straight onto the honours board, filed alongside Ron Hickman under Quacking Together and carrying a nod to the rare Ducks in a Row phenomenon. Remarkably, Richard Harris was at it again on this same date in 1956 too — clearly a day the cricketing gods reserve for noughts. Week in Summary Three ducks, both incidents confined entirely to the 1st XI, and a debutant thrown straight into the deep end at Maidstone. The art of not scoring remains alive and well. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Alan Cradduck — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - Andrew Moss — 3 innings, 1 duck, 33.3% - Mike Iliffe — 3 innings, 1 duck, 33.3% Cradduck leads on pure ruthless efficiency, though early season percentages should be read with a pinch of salt. Next fixture looms, and with it, no doubt, further additions to the register. One match, one queue for the crease, and Mote A did the honours as the LPCC 1st XI supplied a full house of the season's dying embers. 🏏 1st XI v Mote A Terry Whittaker came in at five and departed bowled by M. Taylor without scoring — his 3rd duck of the season and a hefty 29th for the career, good enough for 10th on the all-time roll of shame from 257 innings. A chip off the old block too — his forebear Richard Harris carries 36 career ducks of his own. And yes, 1964 strikes a third time: Robert Murray, same day, same fate, against Linton Park CC. 📅 Week in Summary Three ducks from one match, the entire haul supplied by the 1st XI at the hands of Mote A. Two of the three shared a bat-together, quack-together bond, and all three fell on a date that has apparently had it in for Linton batsmen since at least 1964. Brian Relf — 3 ducks in 7 innings (42.86%) Brian Relf's afternoon at Mote A wasn't just a career milestone — it keeps him lodged firmly in this season's top five. 🦆 Duck News — 16-17 August 1969

3 ducks
Week 17 · 16 Aug 1969 – 17 Aug 1969
A short but perfectly formed weekend for the exclusive zero club, with Linton's 1st XI doing all the honours: three ducks across two fixtures at home to Bowaters CC and Mote A. Quality over quantity, as the man said. Saturday 16 August — v Bowaters CC Andrew Moss departed at first drop, caught Alf Jewiss off Peter Sivyer, for his maiden duck of the campaign — and, from 30 career innings, his very first for the club, landing him 211th of 845 in the all-time table. A paid-up if premature member of the Retirement Duck honours board, though nobody's suggesting he's going anywhere just yet. On this very day in 1953, John Ames was doing much the same, walking back for nought — Ames went on to 42 career ducks and 3rd all-time, so Andrew has some catching up to do. Down at eight, Tim Thirkell fell lbw to Trevor Mannering, his 3rd duck of the season and 4th in just 18 career innings — 96th of 845 and climbing. Tim already carries handsome silverware: Full House (a duck at every position 1-11) and top-ten placings in both the Lone Duck and Homebody Duck charts. The family name is no stranger to this honours board either — kinsman John Thirkell sits at Number One all-time with 65 career ducks, a mark Tim can only dream of troubling. And, as with Andrew, 16 August 1953 also produced a John Ames special — the coincidence department is working overtime this week. Sunday 17 August — v Mote A Percy Brattle was bowled by C- Robbins for his 4th duck of the season and 12th of his career, 33rd of 845 all-time — and with it he seizes the 1969 Duck of the Year crown outright, a title very much live and very much his to lose. Six innings, four ducks, a magnificent 66.67% strike rate of failure — the season's runaway leader in the art of not scoring. The Brattle name runs deep in Duck Club lore too: father Frank sits on 34 career ducks, with Paul Brattle also on the books with one. On this day in 1957, none other than John Thirkell — that same all-time record holder — made a duck against Bowaters CC. The ghosts of ducks past are clearly paying close attention this August. Week in summary: 3 ducks from 2 matches, the 1st XI cornering the entire market single-handedly. No pairs, no golden ducks, no family doubles this time — just honest, workmanlike collapses. On this very day back in 1957, Cliff Anscombe was doing much the same trick against Ron Aiston's XI, en route to a Debutante Duck and the 1957 Duck of the Year crown; Cliff finished with 15 to his name, so Mike has ground to make up yet. Lower down the order, Percy Brattle was caught behind — Peter Prince taking the catch off Ian Lambert — for his first duck of the season and ninth of his career, moving to 61 innings and 44th on the all-time list. Percy already wears the sash for Duck of the Year 1969, and this one keeps the title very much on his own head rather than anyone else's. He arrives with pedigree too — a parent in the Club on 32 career ducks and another relative on the books besides, proof that the art of not scoring runs in the blood. Percy shares his on-this-day company with Cliff Anscombe as well, both men undone on the 26th of May twelve years apart. 📊 Week in Summary Two matches, two ducks, both from the very same fixture — Bearsted CC clearly enjoy their trips to Linton. The other match on the card passed off disappointingly duck-free. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. Mike Iliffe — 5 innings, 2 ducks (40%) 2. Dave Hales — 1 innings, 1 duck (100%) 3. Paul Brattle — 1 innings, 1 duck (100%) 4. Percy Brattle — 1 innings, 1 duck (100%) 5. 🦆 Duck Report — 20 May 1969

3 ducks
Week 4 · 20 May 1969
Just the one fixture on the books this time, but Linton Park's 1st XI made sure it counted, with West Farleigh CC helping the exclusive zero club welcome three new inductees on a single, chastening afternoon. 🏏 1st XI v West Farleigh CC (Home) First to the crease and first to the pavilion was Mike Iliffe, bowled Colin Clark at four for his 1st duck of the season and 10th of a solid career — 56 innings deep and sitting 37th of 839 in the all-time charts. Splendidly, on this exact calendar date back in 1950, club legend John Thirkell — still the all-time number one on 64 — also walked back for nought, against Charles Arkcoll. History, it seems, quacks in rhyme. Next up, Dave Hales at seven, bowled Ron Kemp, and what an entrance — a genuine first-ever innings for the club, and it's a blob. Instant life membership of the Debutante Duck club beckons, with the rarer Quack-to-Quack honour lurking should this prove his only appearance — though we'd rather see him back at the crease than in the record books just yet. He shares his inauspicious start with the same 1950 echo above — good to know he's not alone. Closing the innings' misery was Tim Thirkell, also bowled Ron Kemp, for his 2nd career duck in 10 innings, 183rd of 839 all-time. Already a name across three separate top-10 tables — Ducks on the Road, Homebody Duck and Lone Duck — and a Full House member besides, having now ducked at every position from 1 to 11. Fittingly, it was his own father John, top of the all-time tree on 64, who supplied today's 1950 parallel — the art of not scoring is evidently hereditary in the Thirkell household. 📊 Week in Summary Three ducks, one match, both West Farleigh bowlers sharing the spoils — Ron Kemp claimed two, Colin Clark the third. No pairs, no golden ducks, no family doubles this week — the ducks kept a respectful distance from one another, for once. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Dave Hales — 1 inn, 1 duck, 100% - Paul Brattle — 1 inn, 1 duck, 100% - Basil Sears — 2 inn, 1 duck, 50% - Fred Greenfield — 2 inn, 1 duck, 50% - Stan Wratten — 2 inn, 1 duck, 50% Dave Hales top of the pile on his very first outing — a bold way to introduce yourself to the club's least wanted table. 🦆 Duck Report — 11 & 12 May 1969

2 ducks
Week 3 · 11 May 1969 – 12 May 1969
Two fixtures on the books this weekend, and Gore Court CC away proved the only ground willing to entertain the club's favourite pastime — the noble art of not scoring. 🏏 Saturday, 1st XI — Gore Court CC (away) Openers John Ames and John Thirkell shared a distinctly forgettable afternoon, both undone by the same tormentor, Derek Gould, within the same top order. Ames went first, back in the pavilion for his 1st duck of the 1969 season and 41st of an already storied career spanning 309 innings — good enough for outright bronze in the all-time table, 3rd of 838. He's a paid-up member of several exclusive fraternities on the honours board: Ducks in a Row (four on the spin, no less), a fixture in the Homebody Duck top 10, and joint custodian of not one but two Quacking Together pairings, with Roy Clarke and with Stan Wratten. As it happens, this very calendar day in 1963 saw Roy Clarke — one half of that pairing — also stroll back for nought, against Charles Arkcoll. Some duos really do share a brain. Thirkell followed him back not long after, caught by John Young off the same relentless Gould, for his own 1st of the season and a frankly monumental 64th of his career — the outright all-time record, 1st of 838, a total nobody at Linton Park looks likely to trouble any time soon. Four-time Duck of the Year (1952, 1954, 1955, 1967), a permanent resident of the Lone Duck, Homebody Duck and Ducks on the Road top 10s, and paired for posterity with both Bob Arnold and William Buck, Thirkell's name reading "0" on the card is less an event than a tradition. Keen students of the family tree will note his kin Tim Thirkell already carries a career duck of his own — the acorn, evidently, does not fall far. And by pleasant coincidence, Thirkell too shares his duck's date with Roy Clarke's 1963 effort against Charles Arkcoll — the same day, six years apart, doing what Linton men have always done best. 📋 The Week in Brief Two matches, two ducks, both from the same innings at Gore Court — Derek Gould can consider his afternoon's work a triumph, ours a shared exercise in adversity. The other fixture passed off, disappointingly, entirely duck-free. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard — Top 5 1. Paul Brattle — 1 duck / 1 innings (100%) 2. Basil Sears — 1 duck / 2 innings (50%) 3. Fred Greenfield — 1 duck / 2 innings (50%) 4. Stan Wratten — 1 duck / 2 innings (50%) 5. Dick Langridge — 1 duck / 3 innings (33%) Early days yet in the race for Duck of the Year — plenty of scope for movement. 5 ducks

Two fixtures, five ducks, and the 1969 vintage already showing real class in the art of not scoring. On this very day in 1959, Tony Tipples (1952–1961) was likewise sent packing, one of seven ducks on his way to 55th on the same table. Stan Wratten opened the batting and the ducking alike, bowled T Jones without scoring — his 29th career duck from 292 innings, good for 8th all-time, and a proud member of the Quacking Together honours alongside John Ames. On this same day in 1958, the ever-reliable Frank Brattle was also making nought, one of 32 in a Linton Park career spanning 1937 to 1969. Fred Greenfield was next, caught W Webb bowled T Jones for his 17th career duck from a brisk 107 innings — 19th all-time, and a paid-up member of the Retirement Duck club from a past farewell. Same 1958 vintage of Frank Brattle keeping him company. Dick Langridge followed, caught T Gabbadon bowled W Webb, his 16th career duck from 104 innings — 21st all-time, and evidently a family trait, with son Barry Langridge already 6 ducks into his own club career. Frank Brattle's 1958 effort makes it a hat-trick of on-this-day company for the Bobbing Court quartet. And then, fittingly, the day's grandest ceremony: at number ten, Paul Brattle marked his very first senior innings for the club with a duck straight off the bat, bowled W Webb without scoring. A genuine Debutante Duck, and he arrives in good company — father Frank Brattle (32 career ducks) and relative Percy Brattle (8) already fixtures of the honours board. Paul's maiden nought sits him alongside a deep vein of history on exactly one career duck apiece, including A Barker, who managed the same feat between 1885 and 1904 and was Duck of the Year in 1885. Week in summary Five ducks from two matches, four of them supplied by Bobbing Court CC alone — a proper cluster for the away side to enjoy. No pairs and no king pairs this week, but a new name joins the club in style on his debut afternoon. Week in Summary Three ducks, two matches, one team doing all the heavy lifting while the 2nds, 3rds and Sunday sides kept their heads down entirely.
