Cliff Anscombe fell first, bowled at first wicket down for nought — his 15th career duck from 76 innings, good enough for 19th on the all-time list. Cliff is a long-standing Debutante Duck (his own first innings was a blob too) and a former Duck of the Year back in 1957, so this one merely swells an already distinguished collection. On this very day in 1952, none other than club record-holder John Thirkell (61 career ducks, still top of the pile) was also trudging back against Maidstone Trades — Cliff keeps exalted company. Benny Bell went next, contriving to be out hit wicket off Back — no assistance required from the opposition. His 8th career duck from 31 innings sits him 44th all-time, and, as it happens, shares his day with Thirkell's own 1952 exploits. Terry Whittaker (lbw, Back) made it three, his 23rd career duck from 203 innings — a lofty 10th all-time. Terry carries the Quacking Together honour alongside Brian Relf on his board, plus a Retirement Duck entry from a past farewell, though nobody is suggesting today marked any such thing. And it was fitting that Brian Relf himself completed the rout, bowled at number 11 for his 21st career duck (44 innings, 12th all-time). Brian's own honours shelf groans under Debutante Duck, Quack-to-Quack, Retirement Duck and that same Quacking Together pairing with Terry above — quite the family of trophies, even if today's contribution was just another line in the ledger. Sunday, at home to Paddock Wood CC, offered no respite. John Ames opened and was bowled by K- Burr without scoring — his 38th career duck from 286 innings, 4th all-time behind only the true greats. John's board is heaving: Ducks in a Row (four on the bounce), a place in the Homebody Duck top 10, and shared Quacking Together billing with both Roy Clarke and Stan Wratten. On this same day in 1956, a young R Vincent was marking his own debut with a duck against West Farleigh CC — the sort of start John himself will remember fondly. Best of all, Louis Buels introduced himself to senior cricket in the purest Duck Club fashion — bowled by P- Bradshaw for nought on his very first appearance. An instant, unarguable induction into the Debutante Duck club, membership bestowed on arrival rather than earned. He joins Vincent, above, in duck-on-debut company, twelve years and a Duck Club generation apart. A weekend total of 6 ducks from 2 matches, with Micky Back single-handedly responsible for four of them — a proper opening to the 1968 books. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Benny Bell — 1 inn, 1 duck, 100% - Brian Relf — 1 inn, 1 duck, 100% - Cliff Anscombe — 1 inn, 1 duck, 100% - John Ames — 1 inn, 1 duck, 100% - Louis Buels — 1 inn, 1 duck, 100% Everyone tied at the top and the season barely a weekend old — the race for Duck of the Year 1968 is wide open. The books stay open next fixture, and the Duck Club awaits its next honorand with characteristic enthusiasm. 🦆🍩0️⃣

His 3rd duck of the season — and, remarkably, his 3rd innings of the season. Three trips to the crease, three ducks, a strike rate of failure that borders on the metronomic. As a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club, Jim's very first Linton innings also brought nought, so this is clearly a man playing to type. He climbs to 112th of 826 all-time, and finds himself in fine historical company: on this same date in 1902, F E Wallis was doing precisely the same thing against Town Malling CC, en route to being crowned Duck of the Year in 1907. Two days later, away at West Farleigh CC, opener Mike Stephens was bowled by Peter J Day for his 1st duck of the season and just his 1st in 12 senior innings — a rare visitor to these pages rather than a regular. He moves to 312th of 826 all-time. And on this very date back in 1943, a young Stan Wratten was doing the same against the Royal Artillery Wing, on his way to a career haul of 28 and 7th place on the all-time table. 📊 The Week in Numbers Three matches, two ducks — restrained by Duck Club standards, but every nought still counts toward the greater glory. Jim Hall's perfect record is the story of the week: three innings, three ducks, triumph through adversity of a very particular kind. Whether the streak survives a fourth visit to the crease remains the season's most pressing question. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard, 1967 - Jim Hall — 3 innings, 3 ducks (100%) - John Thirkell — 17 innings, 3 ducks (17.65%) - Alan Cridland — 5 innings, 2 ducks (40%) - Ossie Fryer — 5 innings, 2 ducks (40%) - Terry Whittaker — 11 innings, 2 ducks (18.18%) Jim Hall shares top spot with John Thirkell on 3 apiece, though John has needed rather more innings to get there. Plenty of season left for a reshuffle. The next fixture awaits, and with it, the next round of nominees for the exclusive zero club. Bring your bat. Or don't bother. 🦆 0️⃣

Five for the collection this week as the Duck Club's summer campaign continues in fine, feathery form. Terry Groves followed him back moments later, caught Maskell bowled Seager for his 1st LPCC duck from just 4 innings — 351st on the leaderboard and a fine way to introduce himself to the club's finer traditions. Terry carries Quacking Together honours alongside Brian Relf and a Retirement Duck credential from a past farewell. Twelve years to the week earlier, in 1955, Bob Arnold was falling to the same fate against Headcorn on his way to a scarcely believable 47. Then came Jim Hall — making his LPCC debut and marking it in the purest Duck Club fashion, caught Thornwell bowled Cooper for nought first innings, straight onto the Debutante Duck board. A remarkably decorated arrival for a single knock: already inside the Ducks on the Road, Tourist Duck, Homebody Duck and Lone Duck top tens, a Full House nearly-man on 10 of 11 positions, Only Two Quacks pairings with Allan Cooper and Nigel Thirkell, and Quacking Together company in Jon Harris, Martin Mears and Tim Thirkell. Ossie Fryer completed Cooper's clean sweep, bowled for his 5th career duck from 16 innings — 70th all-time — and the third man this weekend to keep Arnold's ghost company. 📋 Third fixture of the weekend passed without incident — the Duck Club's one blank across three matches. Week in summary: 5 ducks from 3 matches, one debutant safely inducted, and one bowler doing all the damage on Sunday. Consistency of a very particular kind. Terry shares the "Quacking Together" honour with a certain Brian Relf, which feels rather apt given what happened four balls later. A past Duck of the Year (1964) and eternally one short of completing the club's "Full House" of dismissal positions — he'll need a nought at number one yet. And closing the collapse, Brian Relf, also to J- Kemp, his 2nd of the season and 19th career from a mere 37 innings — a fearsome strike rate that puts him 13th all time. Brian ducked on debut all those years ago and carries the presumptive Quack-to-Quack board for it, and here he was reunited in ignominy with Whittaker, exactly as the honours board suggested he might be. 🌱 Sunday 12th June — 1st XI v Bobbing Court CC Colin Eldred, trapped lbw by A Williamson, notched his 3rd duck of the season and 11th career, from just 55 innings — 28th all time and a past Duck of the Year (1965). On this same day in 1960, John Abnett (1954–1966, 18 ducks, 16th all time, a "Ducks in a Row" man) also fell for nought, against Halfway House. 🏏 Thursday 16th June — 1st XI v West Farleigh CC Fred Greenfield departed caught behind off Peter J Day, his 1st duck of the season and 9th career from 61 innings, 36th of 809. Bob Arnold makes his third cameo of the week — on this day in 1951 he too ducked, against Maths School Rochester. The man is simply everywhere in the on-this-day column. 📊 Week in Summary Six ducks from four matches, all wearing 1st XI colours, headlined by that extraordinary Headcorn quadruple. No goldens, no pairs, no family affairs this week — just honest, workmanlike failure to score. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 1. Colin Eldred — 4 innings, 3 ducks (75%) 2. Paul Bowles — 7 innings, 3 ducks (42.86%) 3. Brian Relf — 3 innings, 2 ducks (66.67%) 4. Richard Ashby — 8 innings, 2 ducks (25%) 5. Terry Whittaker — 13 innings, 2 ducks (15.38%) Four of this week's six duckers sit inside the season's top five — the race for Duck of the Year 1966 is very much alive. Roll on the next fixture, when the exclusive zero club will doubtless welcome new — or returning — members. 🦆🍩

🦆 Duck Report — 4th to 7th June 1966

4 ducks
Week 6 · 4 Jun 1966 – 7 Jun 1966
The zero club welcomed four new arrivals this week, and in a rare show of unity every last one of them wore 1st XI colours. Two matches did the damage; two others let the whole XI off scot-free. 🏏 1st XI — Hartley Country Club CC (away, Sat 6th) A proper collapse into the exclusive zero club here, with top order and tail both paying tribute. John Ames went at first drop, caught off I Gibbons, for his 1st duck of the season and a barely-believable 35th of his career — rank 5 of 809 all-time, the sort of company that requires its own postcode. He's mid-streak on Ducks in a Row (4 consecutive), sits proudly in the Homebody Duck top 10, and keeps Only Two Quacks with Alan Wilkes and Quacking Together with both Roy Clarke and, rather aptly given the week, Stan Wratten. On this very day in 1965, Brian Relf also wandered back for nought, against Tovil and Bridge. Two down the order, Paul Bowles fell to the very same I Gibbons, his 2nd duck of the season and 2nd of his career from just 15 innings — rank 163 of 809. He's the current custodian of Duck of the Year 1966, and banks Ducks on the Road top 10 form alongside Only Two Quacks with Adam Pooley. Like his captain, he joins Brian Relf's 1965 vintage on this date — history repeating with unnerving precision. At number 11, Alan Tucker was bowled by J Lillie for his 1st of the season and 5th career duck in 56 innings — rank 59 of 809. He too finds himself in Brian Relf's 1965 company on this day. Three down, and Hartley's bowlers barely had to work for it. 🏏 1st XI — Reeds CC (away, Mon 8th) Opening the batting is meant to be the safe seat. Stan Wratten didn't get the memo, bowled by C Simmonds for his 1st duck of the season — but a monumental 26th of his career in 259 innings, rank 9 of 809 and closing in on the very summit of the all-time table. Fittingly, he shares Quacking Together with none other than John Ames, making this a two-man week for the ages even if the matches never touched. On this day in 1964, Derek Pantony also made a duck, against Gore Court CC. 📊 Week in Summary Four matches, four ducks, and every single one in 1st XI whites — three of them stacked into one Hartley innings. The other two fixtures this week got away completely unscathed, which the committee will no doubt call "concerning discipline" and the Duck Club will call "a wasted opportunity." Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Colin Eldred — 2 ducks from 3 innings (66.67%) - Paul Bowles — 2 ducks from 6 innings (33.33%) - Richard Ashby — 2 ducks from 7 innings (28.57%) - Malcolm Pay — 1 duck from 1 innings (100%) - Brian Relf — 1 duck from 2 innings (50%) Bowles holds the Duck of the Year 1966 crown for now, but Eldred's strike rate says otherwise given half a chance. 🥇🍩 Next fixture looms, gloves and pads at the ready — the zero club never closes its books for long. See you at the crease. 0️⃣🦆

Duck Club Bulletin — 28 May to 2 June 1966 🦆

5 ducks
Week 5 · 28 May 1966 – 2 Jun 1966
Sevenoaks Vine came to the Park and left with three scalps for the collection, then Folkestone and Bearsted each helped themselves to one more. A tidy little five-duck week — steady, unspectacular, and exactly the kind of consistency the exclusive zero club was built on. 🏏 1st XI — A Full House at Number 4, 9 and 10 Against Sevenoaks Vine CC, Mike Iliffe fell caught and bowled by a- Dakin for his 1st duck of the season and 1st of his career, in just his 2nd innings — an inauspicious opening statement, currently 303rd of 809 in the all-time roll. On this very day back in 1928, club legend Bert Buckoke was doing the identical dance against Bearsted CC, en route to 12 career ducks and two Duck of the Year gongs — Mike, you're in fine company for the calendar, if not yet the tally. Richard Ashby went next, bowled by the same a- Dakin, his 1st duck of the season taking him to 16 career ducks — 18th of 809 all-time, and a fixture of the Ducks in a Row (5 consecutive) and Tourist Duck top 10 boards, so this one barely dented the reputation. Two days later against Bearsted CC he was back at it, caught by Peter Johnson off Bryan Elswood for his 2nd of the season — a grim little pair for Richard this week, out twice inside three days without troubling the scorer either time. His parallel this time round: on this day in 1959, H Clarke was also making a Debutante Duck of himself against Old Williamsonians CC. Brian Relf completed the top-order procession, caught by P- Williams off a- Dakin for his 1st of the season, career duck number 18 — level with both John Abnett (1954–1965) and, fittingly, fellow honours-board man Terry Whittaker, with whom Brian already shares a "Quacking Together" entry. Brian remains a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck and Quack-to-Quack clubs from his own long-ago arrival and farewell — history notes it, this week doesn't rewrite it. Same day in 1928, Bert Buckoke was again the man to beat. Over at Folkestone CC, Frank Brattle was bowled by John Godden for his 1st duck of the season and 26th career — a lofty 7th of 809 all-time — drawing level on the numbers with Gordon Fenner (1941–1966). Frank's father Percy sits in the family ledger too, on 5 career ducks of his own — a nice bit of hereditary form, though not on show this week. On this day in 1937, E Hayes was falling for nought against Charles Arkcoll — small consolation, but tradition is tradition. 📊 Week in Summary Five ducks, four matches, three of them courtesy of the same bowler at Sevenoaks Vine — a- Dakin can consider his week's work done. Richard Ashby's weekend brace is the standout feat, proving that lightning very much does strike twice when there's a nought on offer. No golden ducks, no pairs of the king variety, and no family affairs this time round — just honest, workmanlike failure to trouble the scorers. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. Colin Eldred — 2 ducks / 3 innings (66.67%) 2. Richard Ashby — 2 ducks / 6 innings (33.33%) 3. Malcolm Pay — 1 duck / 1 innings (100%) 4. Brian Relf — 1 duck / 2 innings (50%) 5. Mike Iliffe — 1 duck / 2 innings (50%) Malcolm Pay's flawless 100% remains the standard nobody should aspire to but everyone quietly fears. Colin Eldred leads the chase proper — can anyone catch him before the season's out? 🍩 Next fixture beckons, and with it another chance for the Duck Club to welcome new members or watch old campaigners extend their misery. As ever, we watch, we wait, and we celebrate the art of not scoring. 0️⃣🏏

2 ducks

The 1966 campaign trundles on, and Linton Park's lower order at The Mote CC once more proved that batting is, at its heart, an optional extra. 🏏 1st XI — The Mote CC (away) Two ducks fell in the same innings on Saturday, both dispatched from the unglamorous end of the order — proof that adversity, like tea, is best shared. Gordon, too, finds himself keeping company with John Abnett's ghost — the very same 1955 duck against Halfway House casting its shadow down the order eleven years later. 🦆 Duck News — 14–16 May 1966

4 ducks
Week 3 · 14 May 1966 – 16 May 1966
Three fixtures on the fixture list this weekend, but the exclusive zero club kept its attentions fixed firmly on just the one of them. Maidstone YMCA CC visited on the Saturday and left with four Linton names freshly inducted into the season's dishonour roll, courtesy chiefly of one J- Carter, who helped himself to three of the four wickets in question. Sunday and Monday, by contrast, passed the club's noughts-hunters by entirely — a rare weekend of restraint elsewhere. 🏏 1st XI v Maidstone YMCA CC (home) First to fall was Colin Eldred, bowled by Carter at first drop for his second duck of the season and 10th of an accomplished career — still ticking along nicely at 30th in the all-time list from 54 innings, a shade under one duck in five. Eldred already wears the sash for Duck of the Year 1965 and is a long-standing Retirement Duck club member from a past farewell, so this is very much a man revisiting old haunts. Neatly enough, on this very date back in 1961 Eddie Lawrence (1956–1966) was also trudging off for nought, against Halfway House. Next in was Terry Whittaker, also accounting for Carter's figures, and picking up his first duck of the season for a career total of 18 — good for 15th on the all-time table from 153 innings, roughly a duck every eight visits to the crease. Terry carries the Quacking Together honour alongside Brian Relf and, like Eldred moments earlier, shares his calendar date with Eddie Lawrence's 1961 vintage. Carter's third victim was Paul Bowles, caught behind off his bowling for a maiden career duck from just 11 innings — a rather more modest 9% strike rate for nothingness, but he arrives with the Duck of the Year 1966 crown already on his boards, an early claim staked for the season's grimmest prize. Bowles also nods to the Ducks on the Road top 10 and the Only Two Quacks club with Adam Pooley, and tips his cap to the same 1961 vintage of Eddie Lawrence on this shared date. Finally Malcolm Pay, undone by Tony Grenfell for a career-opening duck in only his fifth innings — a brisk 20% duck rate to be getting on with, and no honours board entries yet, though the season is young. Malcolm joins the Eddie Lawrence anniversary club too, in good company on 14 May. 📅 Elsewhere Nothing further to report from Sunday or Monday's fixtures — either genuinely duck-free cricket, or three batsmen somewhere breathing an enormous, undocumented sigh of relief. 🍩 Week in Summary Four ducks from three matches, all bagged inside a single innings against Maidstone YMCA — a proper cluster, and a fine early data point for Carter's benefit season. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard 1. Colin Eldred — 2 ducks, 3 innings, 66.7% 2. Malcolm Pay — 1 duck, 1 innings, 100% 3. Paul Bowles — 1 duck, 2 innings, 50% 4. Benny Bell — 1 duck, 5 innings, 20% 5. 🦆 Duck News — 28th to 30th August 1965

9 ducks
Week 19 · 28 Aug 1965 – 30 Aug 1965
Three fixtures, nine ducks, and one opposition bowler having the round of his life. The exclusive zero club welcomes its latest inductees. 🏏 Saturday 28th — vs A. Trembeths (home) A torrid morning for the Linton order, with K- Lingard doing almost all of the damage — four wickets, four ducks, not a run given away. Some men chase Ashes glory; Lingard settled for a clean sweep of the Duck Club. Stan Wratten went first, bowled by Lingard for his 3rd duck of the season and 24th of a long career — 9th on the all-time list, and one half of the "Quacking Together" pairing with John Ames. He didn't wait long for company. John Ames followed, run out for his own 3rd of the season and 34th overall — 5th all-time, a fixture of the Ducks in a Row and Homebody Duck honours boards, and reunited with Wratten on the Quacking Together roll right on cue. Colin Eldred was next, caught for his 5th duck of the season — level at the very top of this year's charts and firmly in the hunt for Duck of the Year 1965. John Abnett (Lingard again) added his 1st of the season and 18th career, 14th all-time and another Ducks in a Row man. Then Lingard completed the set, removing Terry Whittaker (3rd of the season, 16th career, 17th all-time) and Brian Relf (2nd of the season, 17th career, 15th all-time) — the very two names inscribed together on the Quacking Together board, doing exactly what it says on the tin. Fittingly, this whole top-order collapse echoes this very date in 1893, when W W Tarrance suffered much the same fate against The Mote CC. Some anniversaries just won't let go. 🏏 Monday 30th — vs Bearsted CC (away) Frank Brattle edged his way to his 3rd duck of the season, 25th career and 6th all-time — and, for the family album, a chip off the old block given kinsman Percy Brattle's own 5 career ducks. Terry Whittaker was back at it too, bowled by Bryan Elswood for his 4th of the season and 17th career, nudging up to 17th all-time. Two matches, two ducks — a proper pair for Terry this week. No king pair on offer (he troubled the scorers for at least a ball each time), but a grim double all the same. Sean Carter completed the trio, caught and bowled by Elswood for his 1st of the season and 4th career. All three, by neat coincidence, share their fate with John Abnett, who made a duck on this very date back in 1958 against W. He does so, incidentally, in good company: siblings Joe and Maurice Fenner already carry five and one career ducks apiece for the club, so failure evidently runs in the blood. Moments later Richard Ashby followed him back, run out for his own 2nd of the season and 11th of his career from 61 innings, ranked 29th all time. A paid-up member of the Ducks in a Row club with five consecutive noughts to his name, and a fixture of the Tourist Duck top 10, Ashby continues to prove that consistency, of a very particular kind, is a virtue. The 2nd and 3rd XIs, wherever they were fielding, kept their collective nerve and their scorecards duck-free — for now. A weekend excursion for the 1st XI took in two away fixtures, Maidstone YMCA CC on the Saturday and Gore Court CC on the Sunday, and the exclusive zero club welcomed five new entries across the two innings. It's his first duck of the summer but his 22nd for the club from 173 innings, good enough for 8th on the all-time roll of ignominy. On this very day back in 1958, Cliff Anscombe — Duck of the Year 1957 and a fully paid-up Debutante Duck — was doing exactly the same thing against Mote A. Gordon keeps it in the family too, with siblings Joe (5) and Maurice (1) already club members in their own right. Derek Pantony followed not long after, caught R Jenner off the same relentless Grenfell, last man in and first man out. His 12th career duck from 36 innings lands him 23rd all-time and, fittingly for a number 11, he's a Duck of the Year 1947 alumnus. Like Gordon, Derek shares his moment with Cliff Anscombe's 1958 vintage. Sunday — away at Gore Court CC Colin Eldred was lbw to Robin Bush at five, a nought that keeps him firmly on course for the Duck of the Year 1965 crown the records already have his name on. Only his 2nd career duck from 17 innings, though he already carries a Retirement Duck credit from a previous farewell — a curious badge for a career still just 17 innings young. On this same May day in 1959, Bob Arnold — 47 ducks, 2nd on the all-time list — was making a nought at this very ground. Roy Clarke was run out at nine, his first duck of the season but a hefty 37th of his career from 220 innings, third on the all-time list. A Duck of the Year 1959 winner and one half of "Quacking Together" with the great John Ames, Roy also echoes Bob Arnold's 1959 effort at the same ground. Brother H Clarke (3 ducks) makes it a family trade. Dick Langridge rounded things off, caught Keith Garrard off Des Ladd at ten for his 2nd duck of the season and 11th of his career from 50 innings, 26th all-time. Kin Barry Langridge (6 career ducks) keeps the family flag flying, and Dick too finds company in Bob Arnold's 1959 nought at Gore Court. Week in summary Five ducks, two matches, one well-travelled 1st XI, and not a single top-three batsman troubled — the damage was all done from five downwards. Grenfell and the Gore Court attack shared the spoils evenly, a couple apiece plus a run out for good measure. Two Linton fixtures this weekend, and one of them decided to give the exclusive zero club a proper working over. Bowaters CC hosted what can only be described as a small massacre of the 1st XI top and middle order — four ducks in a single innings, a genuine triumph through adversity. The other fixture, mercifully or dully depending on your allegiance, passed without a single nought to report. 🏏 1st XI at Bowaters CC — a procession of nothing First to go, at three, was John Thirkell — caught Jack Day, bowled Roy Ecclestone, for the second time this season. That takes him to a staggering 54 career ducks, which remains, and has long remained, top of the all-time pile at 792-deep Linton — the undisputed king of the art of not scoring. A three-time Duck of the Year (1952, 1954, 1955) and a fixture of the Lone Duck, Homebody Duck and Ducks on the Road top tens alike, John ducks with equal distinction whether he's stayed local or travelled. Rather neatly, on this very day in 1936, Percy Brattle (1934-1963) was doing much the same thing against Bearsted CC. At six, Terry Donovan nicked off, caught and bowled Edward Chick, for his 5th of the season and 7th of his career — a tally that sits him 44th all time and keeps him firmly in this year's Duck of the Year conversation, a title he already holds for 1964. He's also a Full House nearly-man, having ducked in ten of the eleven batting positions — number six now ticked off, one slot still cruelly unconquered. Twenty-eight years back to the day, Percy Brattle was completing the very same ritual at Bearsted. Number seven, Richard Ashby, fell bowled to Chick's second victim of the innings, his 6th duck of the season — enough to lead the current Duck Hunting Season standings outright — and his 9th career, good for 33rd all time. A veteran of Ducks in a Row (five consecutive, no less) and a Tourist Duck top-ten regular, an away ground like Bowaters is precisely his natural habitat. Percy Brattle, unusually persistent this week, was there again in 1936. And completing Chick's hat-trick of noughts, at nine, Bob Arnold went caught John Evans bowled Chick — his 2nd of the season but a mighty 47th of his career, second only to Thirkell in the entire 792-strong club history. A Duck of the Year in 1963 and holder of his own Ducks in a Row (four), Bob shares an "Only Two Quacks" honour with Alan Wilkes and a "Quacking Together" board with none other than John Thirkell — and rather fittingly, the two of them renewed that acquaintance in the very same Bowaters innings. Percy Brattle, appropriately, made it four for four in the 1936 parallel stakes. 📊 The week in numbers Four ducks, two matches, one bowler — Edward Chick claimed three of the four victims in a single spell, and Linton's top two all-time duck aristocrats, Thirkell and Arnold, both fell in the same innings. A quiet weekend everywhere else, but Bowaters will do. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Richard Ashby — 20 inns, 6 ducks (30%) - Roy Clarke — 22 inns, 6 ducks (27.3%) - Ron Hickman — 7 inns, 5 ducks (71.4%) - Terry Donovan — 14 inns, 5 ducks (35.7%) - John Ames — 10 inns, 3 ducks (30%) Ashby leads the pack, but with Chick apparently bowling for the opposition on a weekly basis, nobody's tally is safe. 🍩 Roll on the next fixture — the noughts are watching, 0️⃣🦆

4 ducks

Trembeths (Home) Richard Ashby fell at number seven, bowled by H Clancy — his 2nd duck of the summer and 5th of a career now 30 innings deep, level at 61st in the all-time table of 787. His 2nd of the season, 32nd of his career, 4th all-time, with a Duck of the Year gong from 1959 and his own "Quacking Together" pairing with John Ames. Roy comes from good ducking stock — his sibling H Clarke carries 3 career noughts of his own. Like Stan, Roy shares his on-this-day twin in Frank Brattle, ducking against Old Williamsonians on this same date back in 1958. 📊 Week in Summary Four ducks, two matches, entirely a 1st XI affair — the 2nds, 3rds and beyond escaped unscathed this week. At number seven, Ossie Fryer became the second man back for nought, bowled by Colin Warnett — his 3rd duck of the season and 4th of an already eventful career, in just 10 innings. That's 74th on the all-time list at a canter, and rather a promising strike-rate for someone so early in his membership application. And at eleven, Michael Chambers completed the set, trapped lbw by the same Colin Warnett, for his 4th duck of the season and 7th for the club from 26 innings — good enough for 41st all time. Three Linton batsmen, one long afternoon, one thoroughly satisfied Bearsted attack — and all three, curiously, walked off on the precise anniversary of Ernest Cruttenden's own nought against Rochester CC in 1895. The zero club welcomes company across the centuries. 📅 Week in Summary Three ducks from two fixtures, every one of them concentrated into that unfortunate Bearsted innings, with Colin Warnett doing brisk trade among the wickets. A rare weekend of restraint everywhere else — 🍩 stocks briefly ran low. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Bob Arnold — 5 ducks in 8 innings (62.5%) - David Gale — 5 ducks in 16 innings (31.25%) - John Thirkell — 5 ducks in 24 innings (20.83%) - Michael Chambers — 4 ducks in 9 innings (44.44%) - Dick Langridge — 4 ducks in 11 innings (36.36%) With Thirkell extending his all-time lead and Chambers closing in behind, the race for Duck of the Year 1963 remains wide open. 7 ducks

Three days, three fixtures, seven ducks, and a family occasion the club will be dining out on for weeks. The exclusive zero club welcomes its latest inductees below. Saturday 27th July — 1st XI v Tovil A torrid session for the middle-and-lower order at Tovil, where three Linton batsmen shuffled back to the pavilion without scoring — all off the bowling of C- Banes. Dick Langridge went first at six, bowled, his 3rd duck of the season and career from 15 innings, 67th on the all-time list. All three, curiously, share the same historical companion in misfortune: on this day in 1952, Basil Sears likewise departed for nought against Folkestone CC, en route to 17 career ducks across a sixteen-year span from 1947 to 1963. The Langridge pairing is the real story, though — father Dick and son Barry combining for a Duck and Ducklings, the rarest ceremony the club offers, Dick moving to 4 career ducks and Barry to 3 by weekend's end. Barry's contribution also earns him the 1963 "Quacked by Kin" honour, credited to his father. Sunday 28th July — 1st XI v Folkestone CC (away) Dick Langridge wasn't done. Bowled by Derek Waddup, he fell again for his 4th duck of the season and career, completing a grim pair for the weekend — though with bat on ball both times, he stops agonisingly short of King Pair immortality. On this day in 1957, D- Jordan also ducked against Folkestone CC, one of just two in a brief single-season career. Monday 29th July — Midweek XI v Birkenhead Grasshoppers CC The Grasshoppers hopped away with three Linton wickets for nought apiece. Gordon Fenner, trapped lbw by K Acton, took his 2nd duck of the season and 20th of his career from 158 innings — 8th on the all-time list, a family trait shared by brothers Joe Fenner (5 career ducks) and Maurice Fenner (1). Ossie Fryer, stumped off R Stears, made his 2nd of the season, 3rd of his career from 9 innings. And Alan Wilkes, bowled by Stears, brought up his 1st of the season and 17th of his career from 70 innings — 12th all-time, and a paid-up double member of the "Only Two Quacks" club, alongside both Bob Arnold and John Ames. All three Grasshoppers victims share their on-this-day companion too: in 1896, Ernest Cruttenden made a duck against Headcorn CC on his way to 10 career noughts across three decades, 1881 to 1912. Week in Summary Seven ducks, three matches, one glorious father-son double at Tovil, and a clean sweep of Birkenhead's afternoon at the Grasshoppers' expense. Dick Langridge's weekend pair keeps him firmly in the season's title race. Pull up a stool, this is one for the connoisseurs of nought. 🏏 Saturday — v Charles Arkcoll (h) Roy Clarke went first, bowled Ron Hickman at five — his 2nd duck of the season and 27th of a career now 5th on the all-time list of 774. Roy is a paid-up member of the 1959 Duck of the Year honours and shares a Quacking Together board with John Ames, and clearly keeps it in the family — sibling H Clarke carries 3 career noughts of his own. On this day in 1952, John Thirkell also strolled back for company, against Folkestone CC. In came E- Bevan, undone by the same Hickman spell, on his very first senior appearance — a proper Debutante Duck, cricket's cruellest possible welcome. E- also arrives, rather prematurely, on the Retirement Duck honours roll, a badge normally earned rather later in a career. On this day in 1952, John Thirkell was doing exactly the same thing. Then Bob Arnold, bowled John Ames at nine, his 2nd of the season and 41st for the club, 2nd on the all-time chart. With two from two this term Bob currently leads the 1963 Duck of the Year race, sits proudly on Ducks in a Row for four consecutive, and holds Quacking Together status with both Alan Wilkes and John Thirkell. On this day in 1952, John Thirkell got there first too. 🌱 Sunday — v Bobbing Court CC (h) John Thirkell joined the party himself, caught L Taylor bowled P Goodwin at four — his 2nd duck of the season and a 48th career nought that keeps him utterly untouchable atop the all-time list. A three-time Duck of the Year (1952, 1954, 1955), fixture of the Ducks on the Road, Homebody Duck and Lone Duck top tens, and Quacking Together with both Bob Arnold and William Buck, John's company down the decades includes D H Luck, who made a duck against Town Malling CC on this very day in 1906. Stan Wratten kept him company, bowled W Webb at six, his 1st duck of the season and 18th of his career — 10th on the all-time list, and another Quacking Together entry alongside John Ames. D H Luck, again, was up to the same trick on this day in 1906. 📊 Week in Brief Five ducks, two matches, and a 1st XI middle order that simply couldn't get out of its own way. No pairs and no family affairs this week — small mercies. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Bob Arnold — 2 ducks / 2 innings (100%) - Michael Chambers — 2 ducks / 3 innings (66.67%) - Roy Clarke — 2 ducks / 4 innings (50%) - John Thirkell — 2 ducks / 6 innings (33.33%) - B Norman — 1 duck / 1 innings (100%) The next fixture looms, and with it, no doubt, further recruits to the club. Bat carefully out there. 🦆🍩

🦆 Duck Report — 5th to 8th May 1963

6 ducks
Week 2 · 5 May 1963 – 8 May 1963
A brutal double-header against West Farleigh CC, home and away, and the ducks came thick and fast — six of them in two matches, with one bowler doing most of the damage. 1st XI Saturday at home, West Farleigh's Peter J Day had himself a field day, bowling three Linton batsmen for nought and trapping a fourth lbw inside the same innings — a proper procession through the top order. - Frank Brattle (b Peter J Day) opened and fell for his 1st duck of the season, 18th of a career that now sits 8th on the all-time list of 772 — a chip off the old block, with kinsman Percy Brattle carrying 5 career ducks of his own. On this day in 1956, Richard Harris was doing exactly the same thing against Marden CC, en route to a barnstorming 36. - Robert Murray (b Peter J Day) followed him back for his 1st of the season, 14th career, 18th all-time. Same date, seven years earlier, Richard Harris was also making a duck — against Marden CC rather than West Farleigh. - Richard Ashby (lbw b Peter J Day) fell for his 1st this season and 3rd career, 102nd all-time, and remains a paid-up member of both the Ducks in a Row club (five on the spin) and the Tourist Duck top 10 — a man who travels well, just not with the bat. Harris's 1956 effort keeps him company on the anniversary front. - David Gale (b Micky Back) broke Day's stranglehold only in name — Micky Back finished the job — for his 1st ever senior duck in 14 innings, 209th all-time. The date belongs to Harris again, 1956, against Marden. - Michael Chambers (b Peter J Day) rounded off the innings with his 2nd duck of the season already, moving to 5 career and 55th all-time. A fifth appearance for Harris's 1956 duck on this same May date. Over at the return fixture on the Wednesday, away this time, Dick Langridge (b Ray Ford) picked up his 1st senior duck from just 6 innings, 210th all-time. On this day in 1960, Alan Wilkes was doing likewise against Halfway House — one of only two clubs ever to get him, Bob Arnold and John Ames sharing that dubious "Only Two Quacks" double. Week in Summary Six ducks from two matches against the same opponents, four of them off the same over-worked arm of Peter J Day, who might fairly claim honorary Duck Club membership for services rendered. West Farleigh clearly enjoyed themselves. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Michael Chambers — 2 ducks / 2 innings (100%) - B Norman — 1/1 (100%) - Bob Arnold — 1/1 (100%) - Dick Langridge — 1/1 (100%) - David Gale — 1/2 (50%) Early season, and the honours board is filling nicely already. Same again next fixture, gentlemen — the ducks are watching. 🦆

🦆 Duck Report — 27–28 April 1963

5 ducks
Week 1 · 27 Apr 1963 – 28 Apr 1963
Two fixtures, five noughts, and Linton's 1st XI doing all the damage to themselves this week. The zero club welcomes fresh blood and old faithfuls alike. 🏏 Saturday 27th — away to West Farleigh CC A rough afternoon at the crease, with West Farleigh's Ron Kemp helping himself to three LPCC ducks in a single innings — a proper spell of quack-making. First to go was John Thirkell, bowled by Kemp for his 1st duck of the season and a scarcely believable 47th of his career — still the club's all-time leader on 1 of 772, a three-time Duck of the Year (1952, '54 and '55) and a fixture of the Ducks on the Road, Homebody Duck and Lone Duck top tens. The old master, still setting the standard for not scoring. Roy Clarke followed, caught behind off Kemp for his 1st of the season and 26th career duck, good enough for 5th on the all-time list and a Duck of the Year winner back in 1959. Handily, his fall echoes down the years neatly — on this very day in 1952, John Thirkell made his own duck against Maidstone Trades, and here he was doing it again eleven years on, this time dragging company with him. That company was Bob Arnold, also bowled by Kemp, his 1st of 1963 and 40th career duck, 2nd on the all-time chart. Bob's honours board already carries Duck of the Year 1963 — bang up to date — plus a historic Ducks in a Row of four on the bounce. His board also lists "Quacking Together with John Thirkell", and with both men back in the pavilion for nought in the same innings, that pairing has never looked more current. 🏏 Sunday 28th — home to Maidstone AKCC A quieter harvest, but a historic one. B Norman, on debut, was bowled by William Dover for a golden entry into the Debutante Duck honours — the purest way to start a career. It stands as his 1st duck for 1963, and the record book has already filed him under One and Done for the season. Whatever comes next, this is one for the archive. Michael Chambers also fell, bowled by Eddie Page, his 4th career duck from 18 innings, 71st on the all-time list. Sunday's pair both land on a well-thumbed page in the archive — on this same calendar day in 1956, R Vincent made his own duck, his 1st for a career that ran to just one season. 📊 Week in Summary Five ducks, two matches, one very productive bowler in Ron Kemp, and Linton's newest member arriving in style with a debut nought. The 1st XI carried the entire weekend's misfortune — the 2nds, 3rds and Sunday sides escaped unscathed, for now. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - B Norman — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - Bob Arnold — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - Michael Chambers — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - John Thirkell — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% - Roy Clarke — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% Early doors yet in the hunt for Duck of the Year 1963 — plenty of time for the chasing pack to catch Bob Arnold. 🍩 See you next round, Linton — the ducks are never far away. 0️⃣🏏

🦆 Duck News — 22-23 September 1962

3 ducks
Week 22 · 22 Sep 1962 – 23 Sep 1962
The season's final furlongs and Linton Park's bowlers found the edge just often enough to keep the honours board ticking over. Three matches, three ducks, and not a golden one among them — a weekend of quietly professional failure. Saturday 22nd — 1st XI at Maidstone YMCA CC Jack Knowler fell for nought at number seven, bowled by E- Page. Only his second senior innings for the club, and he's already opened his OTHER account — a maiden career duck that lands him 265th of 769 all time. On this very day in 1951, John --'s Taylor was performing the identical trick against Hunton Wanderers CC, one of 15 ducks he'd amass across a decade-plus at the club (1949-1963, 16th of 769). Fine company for a first entry, Jack. Sunday 23rd — Married v Singles The club's oldest grudge match delivered its own casualties on both sides of the ledger. For the Married eleven, Terry Whittaker departed bowled David Gale — his second duck of the season and 11th for the club from 75 innings, 25th on the all-time list. Terry carries the Retirement Duck badge from a past farewell, and more topically, holds Quacking Together jointly with a certain Singles batsman. Sure enough, Brian Relf obliged at the other end, stumped Cliff Anscombe off the bowling of John Crellin, also his second of the season and his 15th career duck from just 30 innings — 15th of 769 all time. Brian is a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck and Quack-to-Quack clubs from innings long past, but today was simply the pair renewing their shared honour in real time, Married and Singles united in nought. Both share the same on-this-day echo: 23 September 1961, Robert Wood fell against Bearsted CC in an identical fixture, one stop on the way to the 20 career ducks (6th of 769) he racked up between 1958 and 1962. Week in brief Three matches, three ducks, no golden ducks, no repeat offenders — just tidy, one-per-match departures from Maidstone to the Married v Singles decider. Robert Wood gets two mentions this week, once in the history books above and once below in the live chase. 4 ducks

A quiet weekend for the run-scorers but a busy one for the Duck Club ledger — four fresh entries recorded across two fixtures, home and away. 🏏 Saturday — v Bowaters CC (Home) Frank Brattle opened the innings and, alas, opened the Duck Club's account for the day too, bowled by Harry Jeffery without troubling the scorers. It's his 2nd duck of the season and 17th for the club in 157 innings, lifting him to a lofty 10th on the all-time chart. He now stands shoulder to shoulder with John Abnett, who reached the same 17 in a rather more efficient 44 innings across 1954–1961, and who owns a place on the "Ducks in a Row" board for four on the bounce. It's his 3rd duck of the season, enough to lodge him at 4th in the current Duck Hunting Season table, and his 25th career duck — good enough for an imperious 5th on the all-time list. Roy already holds the 1959 Duck of the Year title and a place on the "Quacking Together" board alongside the legendary John Ames, so this one merely burnishes an already glittering record of not scoring. His brother-in-arms H Clarke isn't far behind on 3 career ducks himself. 🌱 Sunday — v Staplehurst CC (Away) At Staplehurst, Richard Ashby fell for nought at number 6, run out in circumstances the scorebook diplomatically records as "unsure." It's his 2nd of the season and, remarkably, only his 2nd for the club in 12 innings — though he's already built a five-strong "Ducks in a Row" streak and a spot on the Tourist Duck top 10, evidently a man who saves his finest noughts for away grounds. Spookily, on this very day in 1961, Terry Whittaker also strolled back for a duck against Bowaters CC — history quietly repeating itself. 4 ducks

Saturday brought Linton Park's 1st XI face to face with St Lukes Maidstone CC, and the home top order and tail combined to stage what can only be described as a mass sacrifice to the Zero Club. Summerfield's second victim of the innings, caught by M. Eastman. It's his 3rd of the season, 39th of a storied career spanning 179 innings, and keeps him lodged at a barely believable #2 in the all-time rankings — a proud member of the Ducks in a Row club (four on the spin), and half of two separate quacking partnerships, with Alan Wilkes and with John Thirkell. Bob too joins Stan Wratten's 1945 anniversary club. And at ten, Terry Whittaker was run out in a mix-up nobody could quite explain afterwards. 🦆 Duck Report — 1 & 2 September 1962

1 duck
Week 19 · 1 Sep 1962 – 2 Sep 1962
A quiet weekend on the poultry front — just the two fixtures and a single duck to show for it. Sometimes the hunting season goes like that. Even the finest game keepers have their off days. Saturday 1 September 1st XI v A. Trembeths (home) Coming in at ten, Richard Harris departed caught Bowey, bowled Tootle — a tidy dismissal for the scorebook, if not for Richard. It's his first duck of the season, but the 36th of a long and storied career spanning 174 innings, and it plants him at a genuinely eye-watering 3rd in the entire 767-strong all-time standings. This is not a man dabbling in the art of not scoring — this is a master craftsman. And in a rather splendid quirk of the calendar: on this very day back in 1934, Bert Buckoke also walked back for nought, against Charles Arkcoll of all people. Buckoke, who turned out for Linton Park between 1928 and 1953, finished his career on 12 ducks and a highly respectable 19th all-time, with back-to-back Duck of the Year honours in 1928 and 1950 to his name. Twenty-eight years apart, same fixture window, same fate — the club's ducks have a long memory. Sunday's fixture, mercifully or otherwise, passed off entirely duck-free — eleven batsmen apiece got off the mark, denying the honours board any further custom. Week in Summary Two matches, one duck. Slim pickings by Linton Park standards, but Richard Harris made it count, climbing to within a whisker of the all-time podium. The rest of the club will need to pull their socks up — or rather, pull them down and get back in the hutch — if the season table is to move. 🏆 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - R Davison — 5 ducks / 7 innings (71.43%) - Basil Sears — 4 ducks / 16 innings (25.0%) - Len Conway — 2 ducks / 6 innings (33.33%) - Alan Tucker — 2 ducks / 10 innings (20.0%) - Bob Arnold — 2 ducks / 11 innings (18.18%) R Davison sits well clear at the top with a frankly alarming 71% strike rate for nought — a genuine contender for Duck of the Year if this form holds. 🥇🍩 Next fixture looms, and with it, fresh opportunity for the zero club to welcome new blood or crown old hands. 3 ducks

Two fixtures on the card this weekend, and only one troubled the scorers — the other passed by entirely fowl-free. But the 1st XI's home date with Sevenoaks Vine CC on the Sunday made up for it in style, with three names added to the ledger in the very same innings, courtesy of just two Vine bowlers. The art of not scoring, alive and well at Linton Park. 1st XI v Sevenoaks Vine CC (home, 26th August) John Ames opened the afternoon's misery, bowled by Cliff Judd for his 2nd duck of the season and 27th of an increasingly distinguished career — 193 innings in and still holding 4th place in the all-time standings, rarefied company indeed. Ames already carries a handsome collection of honours: four ducks in a row at one stage, a fixture on the Homebody Duck top ten, and paired-quack history on the books with both Alan Wilkes and Stan Wratten. On this very day back in 1945, Herbert Rayner (1939–1948, 6 ducks, 48th all-time) was making his own contribution to the calendar against 1st Innings Fifth Leicester — Ames keeps that anniversary ticking over, eighty-one years on. Eddie Lawrence followed, caught Rodney Crang bowled R Nash, for a 1st duck of the season and 7th of his career from 39 innings — good enough for 39th on the all-time list. He shares this very Rayner anniversary with Ames, proof that some dates are simply cursed. And then Roy Clarke, undone by the same Cliff Judd delivery that had already claimed Ames, for his 2nd of the season and 24th of his career — 150 innings deep and 5th on the all-time roll of dishonour, one place behind Ames himself. Clarke still wears the 1959 Duck of the Year crown, and his "Quacking Together" pairing with Ames, usually a quiet historical footnote, was very much reactivated this week — the two of them walking off to the same bowler in the same over. A word too for sibling H Clarke, a fellow paid-up member of the family firm on three career ducks. Clarke's anniversary company, once again, is Herbert Rayner. The Week in Numbers Three ducks from two matches, the lot of them delivered by Sevenoaks Vine's opening attack — Cliff Judd claiming two outright. A fine afternoon's work for the bowler, considerably less fine for Linton's middle order. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. R Davison — 5 ducks from 6 innings (83%) 2. Nolan and M. Hollis each claiming a brace apiece for their respective sides. Consistency of a very particular kind. 7 ducks

Monday 7th August — Bearsted CC (away) A two-innings friendly at Bearsted turned into a feeding frenzy — five noughts in one fixture. Opening up, John Ames was bowled by Mike Morton for his 2nd duck of the season (23rd career, 4th of 754 all-time) — then walked out again in the second innings and was caught George Lambell off Peter Longley for his 3rd of the season and 24th career duck. A genuine pair, both halves in the same match. Fittingly, his old honours-board accomplices Roy Clarke and Alan Wilkes — both immortalised alongside him for shared quacking down the years — were there to make it a proper reunion. Gordon Fenner obliged again at eleven, caught George Lambell off Mike Morton, his 3rd duck of the season and 18th career — and with Saturday still fresh in the memory, a pair spread neatly across the weekend. Roy Clarke (b Bryan Elswood) fell without scoring for his 2nd of the season, 22nd career, 5th of 754 all-time — solid work for a man who once carried the 1959 Duck of the Year title. His brother H Clarke sits on 3 career ducks of his own. Alan Wilkes (b Mike Morton) rounded things off with his 2nd of the season and 16th career, 10th of 754 all-time. All four of Monday's fallers share the same on-this-day parallel — back in 1909, C Stevens was doing exactly the same against the Royal West Kent Regiment CC, en route to the 1909 Duck of the Year gong. 📋 Week in Summary Seven ducks from two matches, with Monday's Bearsted friendly doing the heavy lifting — five for nought in one afternoon is precisely the team effort this club exists to celebrate. 4 ducks

Two fixtures, four ducks, and the 1st XI doing all the damage to their own top order this week. The exclusive zero club welcomes no new faces, only old and distinguished members topping up their accounts. 🏏 Saturday 8th July — v Charles Arkcoll (away) Frank Brattle was run out for nought at number two, unsure whose call it was and unlikely to be the one owning up. His 3rd duck of the season and 15th of a long and storied career, vaulting him to 12th of 754 in the all-time table. On this very day back in 1950, John --'s Taylor was performing the identical ceremony against Hayle Place CC — different ground, different decade, same solemn walk. A chip off the old block too, in a manner of speaking: his relative Percy Brattle carries 4 career ducks of his own. 🏏 Sunday 9th July — v A L Newberry XI (home) A torrid morning for the home top and middle order. John Ames departed for nought at number two, bowled by J Newberry, his 1st duck of the season but a mighty 22nd for the career — enough to hold 4th of 754 all-time, a place he shares good company in via his standing membership of Ducks in a Row (four consecutive, no less), the Homebody Duck top ten, and not one but two Quacking Together partnerships. Even legends have off days. On this day in 1902, F E Wallis was doing much the same against Town Malling CC, back when Victoria was barely five years in the ground. John Crellin followed at number six, bowled by A Newberry, for his 3rd duck of the season and, tidily, his 3rd career duck too — a young account still finding its feet, though he's already been crowned Duck of the Year 1961, so evidently finding it in style. He joins a genuinely enormous queue of fellow three-timers stretching back to 1881, proof the art of not scoring has never gone out of fashion. Gordon Fenner rounded things off, run out for nought at number eight, his 1st of the season but 16th of his career, good enough for 8th of 754 all-time. 3 ducks

One place down the order, Frank Brattle followed him back for nought, also bowled Bailey — his 2nd duck of the season, and the 14th of his career, good enough for 13th on the all-time list. A chip off the old block, too: his relative Percy Brattle already sits on 4 career ducks of his own, so the aptitude for the art of not scoring runs in the family. Frank shares his B W Haynes anniversary with Cliff — two Sutton Valence ghosts summoned by one Tilling Stevens over. Batting at nine, Roy Clarke completed the set, given lbw off Bailey for his 1st duck of the season. It is Roy's 21st career duck, remarkably elevating him to 5th of all 754 names ever to grace the club's dubious honours board — a Duck of the Year winner in 1959, and a proud member of the "Quacking Together" pairing with club great John Ames, with whom he shares that exact 21-tally. Roy too finds a companion in 1906's B W Haynes, and can console himself that his sibling H Clarke (3 career ducks) knows the feeling as well. 📊 Week in Summary Three matches, one productive, three ducks — all compressed into a single Tilling Stevens innings. It won't last. With the season stretching out ahead and more fixtures on the horizon, normal service — a nick behind, a plumb lbw, a golden duck for the ages — will surely resume shortly. 1960 Season 22 reports

🦆 DUCK REPORT — 24–25 September 1960 🦆

8 ducks
Week 22 · 24 Sep 1960 – 25 Sep 1960
A blustery end-of-season weekend produced eight ducks across two fixtures, and the exclusive zero club is looking rather plump for it. Two truths were reaffirmed: the art of not scoring is alive and well at Linton Park, and nobody should let Ray Howard near a cricket ball if they value their stumps. Saturday 24th — 1st XI v A. Trembeths Frank Brattle departed to H- Clancy without troubling the scorers, his 4th duck of the season and 12th of an increasingly decorated career from 104 innings — good enough for 15th on the all-time list. A family trait, it seems: kinsman Percy Brattle already carries 4 career noughts of his own. On this very date in 1955, John Carter also strolled back for nought, against Town Malling CC, in what proved his only season in Linton colours. Sunday 25th — a full house against Linton Park CC Three Linton sides took the field, and the zero club signed up six new members for the day. Ray Howard led the way, bowled by John Ames for his 2nd duck of the season (8th career, 32nd all-time from 80 innings) — and then went and did the same to others. With the ball he claimed a treble of duck-scalps in the same innings, sending back Sean Carter, John Abnett and Derek Pantony all bowled. Poacher and gamekeeper on the same afternoon, and arguably better with the ball than the bat. Cliff Anscombe edged behind for his 3rd season and 10th career duck (22nd all-time, 33 innings), a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club and a past (1957) Duck of the Year, still finding new ways to add to the collection. Sean Carter went one better — or worse — completing a pair: stumped off Len Conway's bowling for his 2nd duck of the season, then bowled by the rampaging Ray Howard for his 3rd, taking his career tally to 3 from just 6 innings (100th all-time). Two ducks, one date, no complaints. Len Conway, run out for his trouble, moved to 6 career ducks (44th all-time, 73 innings) and his 2nd of the season, himself a Debutante Duck alumnus of some vintage. John Abnett's was his 2nd of the season and 16th career duck from a mere 42 innings — a startling 7th on the all-time list — and sits comfortably alongside his own "Ducks in a Row" board entry. Derek Pantony's was his 5th of the season, a genuine title charge, and 6th career duck (39th all-time), the old 1947 Duck of the Year proving he's lost none of his touch for the art. History rhymed all afternoon: no fewer than six of Sunday's fallen discovered that on this exact date back in 1955, Frank Brattle — Saturday's own man of the moment — was himself out for nought against Linton Park CC. Some ghosts never leave the crease. 📊 Week in Summary 8 ducks, 2 matches, one treble of duck-taking, one pair, and Ray Howard doing more damage with ball than bat ever could. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - Pat Hardwick — 6 ducks / 37 inns (16%) - Richard Harris — 5 ducks / 11 inns (45%) - Derek Pantony — 5 ducks / 12 inns (42%) - Bob Arnold — 5 ducks / 19 inns (26%) - Robert Wood — 5 ducks / 34 inns (15%) 🍩 The season presses on, and so does the hunt for glory — or its rather more common opposite. William already shares "Quacking Together" honours with John Thirkell from campaigns past. Alan Wilkes rounded things off, Spanswick's third victim, his 3rd of the season and 14th career duck, joining Frank Sutton (1925–1949) on the same mark. Alan's own trophy cabinet includes "Only Two Quacks" pairings with both Bob Arnold and John Ames. Tuesday 26 July — Mote A (Away) A solitary entry at Mote A: Roy Clarke, bowled by Ashurst for his 3rd duck of the season and 19th career — rank 5 of 736, and a former Duck of the Year himself back in 1959. On this very day in 1959, none other than Tony Snell also departed against Folkestone CC — Linton's own "Runaway Duck" of 1958, a season memorable for yielding no runs whatsoever. Roy's sibling H Clarke also flies the family flag with 3 career ducks of his own. Week 8 · 18 Jun 1960 – 19 Jun 1960
Rumwood CC provided the hunting ground this weekend, with the 1st XI's trip away yielding a full quartet of noughts. A quiet weekend elsewhere, but Rumwood more than made up for it. 🏏 1st XI at Rumwood CC Batting at four, T- May fell b J- Carter without troubling the scorers — and it's a debut to remember for all the wrong reasons. His maiden senior innings ends in a duck, earning immediate and simultaneous membership of three honours boards: Debutante Duck, One and Done, and the Retirement Duck club (the last two, naturally, presumptive — nobody's writing his farewell speech just yet). On this very day back in 1949, club legend John Thirkell was doing exactly the same thing against Bowaters CC, en route to a colossal 44 career ducks and the No.1 spot in the all-time rankings. Good company to keep, even from the bottom of the ladder. At five, H Clarke was run out for nought — the fielding side doing the bowler's work for him. It's Clarke's 3rd career duck from 18 innings, sitting him at 84th all-time, and a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club from his own first-baller some innings back. He's got form in the family too — sibling Roy Clarke carries a hearty 18 career ducks, so the nought clearly runs in the blood. Like May, Clarke shares this day in history with John Thirkell's 1949 vintage. Number seven Terry Whittaker was bowled by J- Carter, his 2nd of the season and 5th for his career — a tally that lands him at 48th all-time, level with the likes of Allan Peach (1903–1907) and Frank Wright, the latter a fellow member of the exclusive Quack-to-Quack club. Terry already shares Quacking Together honours with team-mate Brian Relf — and rather fittingly, Relf was next through the gate. Brian Relf, batting nine, was stumped off the same tireless J- Carter, his 1st duck of the season and 6th of his career, moving him to 34th on the all-time list. Brian's card is a crowded one — Debutante Duck, Quack-to-Quack, Quacking Together with Whittaker, and Retirement Duck all present and correct, a full house of dubious distinction. He now sits alongside D Sells (1943–1944), who also stopped the clock on six. Four wickets, one bowler, one stumping — J- Carter clearly fancied his chances against Linton Park this week, and the Duck Club is grateful for the service. 📊 Week in Summary Four ducks from two matches, all four falling in the same innings at Rumwood — a proper collective effort, and every single one of them credited to the same bowler. The art of not scoring was alive and well on the away trip, even if the rest of the fixture list stayed disappointingly fowl-free. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - Bob Arnold — 3 ducks in 8 innings (37.5%) - Alan Wilkes — 2 ducks in 3 innings (66.67%) - Eddie Lawrence — 2 ducks in 5 innings (40.0%) - Derek Pantony — 2 ducks in 6 innings (33.33%) - Terry Whittaker — 2 ducks in 8 innings (25.0%) Alan Wilkes lurking on a fearsome 66.67% strike rate should have the rest of the club nervous. Roll on next weekend — the ducks at Rumwood clearly enjoyed the company, so who's joining them next? 🍩

🦆 DUCK NEWS — 11-12 June 1960 🦆

4 ducks
Week 7 · 11 Jun 1960 – 12 Jun 1960
A quiet couple of days by Duck Club standards, but the exclusive zero club still found four new inductees at Headcorn and Halfway House. No pairs, no family affairs this time round — just honest, individual triumphs in the art of not scoring. 🏏 Saturday 11 June — Away Day at Headcorn CC The 1st XI travelled to Headcorn and left two names richer for the honours board. Robert Wood departed at number five for his 1st duck of the season, bowled by S Parnham, and now stands on 8 career ducks — 28th of 730 all time. A paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club from way back, though today's effort was a solo affair rather than a repeat performance. Poetically, on this very day in 1955, Bob Arnold also made a duck against Headcorn CC — Arnold went on to rack up 34 of the things (2nd of 730 all time), so Robert keeps distinguished company on the calendar if not yet on the leaderboard. Down at number ten, Tony Snell followed him back with a golden-tinged 1st duck of the season, caught Murrell bowled Ward. Tony now sits on a mighty 19 career ducks — 5th of 730 all time — a Duck of the Year winner in 1958 and holder of the "Runaway Duck" board for that same barren campaign. Fittingly, he shares his on-this-day company with the very same Bob Arnold, also felled by Headcorn on 11 June 1955. 🏏 Saturday/Sunday — Halfway House Away The 1st XI's trip to Halfway House on the 12th brought two more names to the party. John Abnett, in at nine, edged behind for his 1st duck of the season and moves to 15 career ducks — 9th of 730 all time. A quietly serious tally that puts him level on career ducks with John "--'s" Taylor, who racked up his 15 across 142 innings between 1949 and 1958. On this same date back in 1865, W Crittenden also made a duck, against 1st Innings Yalding United — the club's ducking traditions clearly run deep. But the standout of the weekend belongs to Derek Pantony, bowled by Roger Mills at number ten for his 2nd duck of the season, taking him to just 3 career ducks from a mere 7 innings — a frankly alarming 43% strike rate in the wrong direction. Derek is already a Duck of the Year alumnus from 1947, and tonight joins a long and distinguished queue on exactly 3 career ducks, including E Hayes (3 from just 3 innings — a perfect and terrible record) and Michael Fagg. Also on this day in 1865, W Crittenden made his duck against Yalding United — the calendar clearly has a taste for these things. 📊 Week in Summary Four ducks from two matches, all in the 1st XI, all away from home — Linton's top order clearly fancied giving the locals a show without troubling the scorers. No pairs, no golden family affairs, but Derek Pantony's second duck of the weekend deserves a nod for pure economy of effort. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. Bob Arnold — 7 innings, 3 ducks (42.9%) 2. Alan Wilkes — 3 innings, 2 ducks (66.7%) 3. Eddie Lawrence — 5 innings, 2 ducks (40.0%) 4. Derek Pantony — 6 innings, 2 ducks (33.3%) 5. Frank Brattle — 10 innings, 2 ducks (20.0%) Alan Wilkes leads on strike rate but Bob Arnold holds the volume crown for now. Plenty of season left for the standings to turn. 🦆 The next fixture awaits, and with it, no doubt, further contributions to the cause. Same duck time, same duck place — see you all out there (or rather, back in the pavilion) soon!

🦆 Duck Report — 4th to 9th June 1960

3 ducks

A tidy little harvest this week: three ducks from four matches, the whole lot served up courtesy of the 1st XI, who appear to have taken sole custody of the club's scorelessness this week. 🏏 1st XI Home to Canning Town Glassworks CC on Saturday 4th June, the top order held firm but the lower order did not escape so lightly. Bob is already a fully paid-up member of Ducks in a Row (four on the spin, no mean feat), and carries dual membership of Only Two Quacks (with Alan Wilkes) and Quacking Together (with John Thirkell) — the Duck Club's answer to a testimonial dinner. Fittingly, on this very date in 1898, C S Smith was doing precisely the same thing against Sutton Valence School, on his way to that year's Duck of the Year honours. Last man in, Richard Harris fared no better, bowled by the very same Gwyn Reynolds — his 1st duck of the season but a substantial 30th of his career, good enough for 3rd on the all-time chart from 162 innings. Richard, too, shares his date with C S Smith's 1898 vintage against Sutton Valence — the Duck Club evidently keeps its own anniversary diary. Away at Tovil on Monday 6th June, Pat Hardwick completed the week's card, lbw to the splendidly named Cradduck for his 1st duck of the season and 3rd of his career from just 39 innings. Pat currently holds the Duck of the Year 1960 title, one he'll be defending with some vigour as the summer wears on. And once again the calendar obliged — George Champion fell in exactly this fashion against Town Malling CC back in 1903. 📋 The Week in Brief Four matches, three ducks, and a tidy little pattern: two of the week's three victims fell to the same bowler in the same innings, and all three noughts landed on dates the Duck Club's own history had already claimed. Frank Brattle — 10 innings, 2 ducks (20.0%) 🍩 Bob Arnold sits proudly atop the pile as the 1960 season heads for home, while Pat Hardwick's reigning Duck of the Year form proves quantity and quality are entirely different games. The 1960 campaign is barely a fortnight old and already the exclusive zero club has its first inductee of the new season. It's the 9th of his LPCC career from 75 innings, a tally that plants him firmly at 24th in the all-time standings out of 726 names on the books — respectable company for a man who keeps finding fresh ways not to trouble the scorers. A chip off the old block too, it should be said — kin records show Percy Brattle carrying 4 career ducks of his own, so the surname is no stranger to the honours reel. And in a splendid quirk of the calendar, on this very day back in 1955 — five years to the very date — John --'s Taylor also made a duck against West Farleigh CC, one of 15 career noughts he'd amass across a playing career running 1949–1958, good enough for 8th of 726 all-time. Cricket's ducks, it seems, know their anniversaries. 🌱 Elsewhere Sunday's fixture passed without incident — a rare vegan affair for the Duck Club, entirely free from fowl. No shame in that, though the purists among us will insist a quiet weekend is merely a duck biding its time. 📋 Week in Summary One duck from two matches is a modest return by Linton standards, but early season is early season — the real hunting rarely begins before the wickets have dried out and the confidence has grown. 🦆 Duck News — Weekend of 26–27 September 1959 🦆

4 ducks
Week 22 · 26 Sep 1959 – 27 Sep 1959
Two fixtures, four ducks, and the archives creaking under the weight of history — a proper vintage weekend for the exclusive zero club. 🏏 Saturday 26th — 1st XI v A.Trembeths Robert Wood battled to the crease at seven, dug in gamely, and was eventually undone c P. Rye b C. Rye — the Rye family clearly operating a closed shop that afternoon. It's his 5th duck of the season and 7th of an illustrious career, good enough for 31st on the all-time list of 726. Robert is also a paid-up member of the Debutante Duck club from a duck-on-debut long since consigned to history — not this one, but the badge stands. He now joins the Victorian great A Startup on exactly 7 career ducks — a man who played 1868–1963... sorry, 1868–1882, took Duck of the Year honours three separate times, and once strung five ducks in a row. Illustrious company for a Saturday afternoon dismissal. 🌱 Sunday 27th — the "Unknown XI" v Linton Park CC Whoever they were, the archives have lost their name — but not, mercifully, their ducks. Three fell in this one innings alone, and two of them were old sparring partners reunited. Alan Wilkes opened and departed first ball region c John Abnett b Terry Whittaker — his 3rd of the season and 11th of a career now sitting a lofty 15th of 726 all time. Alan is a double Only Two Quacks honouree, paired separately with Bob Arnold and John Ames — both of whom, delightfully, ducked in this very same innings, reuniting all three on the honours board in the flesh. His dismissing bowler, Terry Whittaker, has previous form too — on this very day in 1958 he also walked for nought against A.Trembeths. Bob Arnold, at three, fell b Tony Tipples for his 5th of the season, moving to a barely believable 31 career ducks — 2nd of all 726 in club history, second only to the legendary Tim Thirkell-tier company. Bob owns Ducks in a Row (4 consecutive) and shares Only Two Quacks with Alan Wilkes, his batting partner in ignominy this very afternoon. His own executioner, Tony Tipples, has a habit of this fixture — he too made a duck against Linton Park CC on this day back in 1953. John Ames, two down, fell b Alan Wilkes for his 3rd of the season and 20th career — 4th of 726 all time, and a Homebody Duck top-tenner to boot. He shares Quacking Together honours with none other than Roy Clarke, who currently tops this season's leaderboard — proof that good company follows a man even into the zero column. 📊 Week in Summary Four ducks from two matches, three of them arriving in a single Sunday innings — a rare cluster that would have made fine viewing for the purists. Special mention to catcher John Abnett, who claimed Wilkes's wicket this week while quietly sitting 5th in the season charts himself — a man evidently more comfortable behind the stumps than in front of them. 🥇 Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. Roy Clarke — 9 ducks, 28 innings, 32.14% 2. Tony Snell — 5 ducks, 8 innings, 62.5% 3. Bob Arnold — 5 ducks, 22 innings, 22.73% 4. Robert Wood — 5 ducks, 30 innings, 16.67% 5. John Abnett — 4 ducks, 6 innings, 66.67% Roy Clarke holds firm at the summit, but with three names locked on five apiece the chase is tightening nicely. 🍩 As ever, the crease waits for nobody. 🦆 Duck Report — 12th–13th September 1959

5 ducks
Week 20 · 12 Sep 1959 – 13 Sep 1959
Two fixtures at Linton Park this weekend, and the zero club welcomed five new entries to its ledger, all from the 1st XI. A tidy reminder that late September shows no mercy to the specialist blocker. 🏏 Saturday 12th September — v Bowaters CC (home) S Lusher, in at seven, was stumped by John Woollett off Bernard Collins to open his LPCC duck account. It is duck number one of the season and number one of a career just five innings old, placing him 296th of 726 in the all-time table. He arrives alongside - Dampier, whose sole Linton duck came in 1952 and came, rather ominously, with a Debutante Duck, a One and Done, and a presumptive Retirement Duck all in the same afternoon. Lusher, we trust, has a rather longer stay in mind. 🏏 Sunday 13th September — v Tunbridge Wells CC (home) A grim afternoon in the middle order and beyond, as four Linton batsmen queued up for the walk back without troubling the scorers. John Ames was stumped by Don Glanvill off John Piper for his 2nd duck of the season and 19th of a long and distinguished career, good enough for 4th on the all-time list. A fully paid-up member of Ducks in a Row and the Homebody Duck top ten, Ames also extends his Quacking Together partnership with Roy Clarke, who joined him in the pavilion in this very innings. Robert Wood fell lbw to Mike Willard, his 4th of the season and 6th of a career that began, fittingly, with a Debutante Duck some years back. He draws level on career ducks with D Sells (1943-44), who reached six in just 14 innings and wore the Duck of the Year crown in 1943. Roy Clarke, caught and bowled by Mike Willard, brought up his 9th duck of the season, a tally already leading the current Duck Hunting Season table by some distance, and his 16th career duck, 6th on the all-time roll of dishonour. 1959 is officially Clarke's year: he holds the Duck of the Year 1959 title, and duly proved it by quacking together with John Ames for the second time in the innings. He is level on career ducks with the mighty Stan Wratten (1943-59, 172 innings), and joins a small dynasty of Clarkes, sibling H Clarke having chipped in two career ducks of his own. John Abnett completed the rout, bowled by Mike Willard for his 4th duck of the season and 14th of his career, good for 11th all-time. A charter member of Ducks in a Row, Abnett is now level with Frank Sutton (1925-49), twice Duck of the Year in the 1940s, who took 62 innings to reach the total Abnett has managed in 36. 📋 Week in Brief Five ducks from two matches, four of them arriving in a single Tunbridge Wells innings. Snell, meanwhile, is quietly building a formidable CV — his 4th duck of the season lifts him to 17 career ducks in just 50 innings, a startling 5th of 723 all-time, backed by a Duck of the Year gong from 1958, a "Ducks in a Row" honour, and the small matter of a Runaway Duck season with no runs at all to his name that year. Both tail-enders share the Leveson-Gower coincidence with Clarke — quite the reunion on Maidstone Road, forty-nine years apart. 🌱 Sunday — home to Newington CC Pat Hardwick was run out for nought at first drop, his opening entry to the Duck Club — 1st of the season, 1st of his career in 11 innings, 278th of 723 all-time. On this same day in 1944, one E- Humphreys was likewise dismissed without scoring, against the splendidly named National Fire Service Overseas Contingent. Some coincidences transcend the decades. 📋 Week in summary Four ducks, two matches, and J Lee can fairly claim to have run a one-man cull through the Aylesford innings. Brian Mills — 5 innings, 3 ducks (60.00%) — a startling rate for a man still finding his feet 3. R. Spillane — 2 innings, 2 ducks (100.00%) — perfect consistency, of a very particular kind 4. William Buck — 7 innings, 2 ducks (28.57%) 5. Bob Arnold — 8 innings, 2 ducks (25.00%) Brian Mills, incidentally, sits on exactly 3 career ducks — level company with Robert Wood himself, along with a small crowd of Linton names stretching back to 1881. The zero club has never been short of company. 🍩 Looking Ahead Slim pickings this week, but the season is young and Roy Clarke shows no signs of relinquishing top spot without a fight. Next weekend's fixtures await — bring your bats, gentlemen, and if you can't trouble the scorers, at least trouble the record books. The Duck Club will be watching. 0️⃣🦆

🦆 Duck Report — Weekend of 13–14 June 1959

3 ducks
Week 7 · 13 Jun 1959 – 14 Jun 1959
A quiet weekend for the fowl-hunters by recent standards, but the exclusive zero club never fully closes its doors, and the 1st XI kept the lights on across both days out. Saturday 13th — 1st XI away at Headcorn CC Number eleven Peter Hughes wasted no time announcing himself, bowled by W- Ward for nought on his very first senior appearance. A debut duck is one of cricket's purest ironies and Peter is now formally inducted onto the Debutante Duck board, taking up residence at 277th of 718 in the all-time ledger. Splendidly, on this exact date back in 1943 Herbert Sunley was doing much the same against the Home Guard's Maidstone 11th Battalion, en route to five career ducks of his own — so there's a precedent, Peter, for turning a rough start into a proper collection. Sunday 14th — 1st XI away at Halfway House Opener Stan Wratten fell early, bowled by Don Capeling, his first duck of the summer but his 16th for the club overall — enough to keep him parked at a mighty 5th of 718 all-time. Stan remains a proud member of the Quacking Together board alongside John Ames, proof that misery enjoys the best company. Neatly, on this very 14th of June back in 1882, C Gibbs was contributing his own nought against Boxley CC's 1st Innings — his career amounted to just the one duck against Stan's sixteen, so consistency of a very particular kind clearly runs deeper in some than others. He had company in the returning-hut. At number nine John Abnett also departed for nought, bowled by Peter Bedelle, his 11th career duck from a brisk 33 innings — good enough for 14th on the all-time list and a place on the Ducks in a Row board for four consecutive noughts, a genuine feat of sustained failure. Fittingly, John shares his on-this-day company with C Gibbs too, who was busy not scoring against Boxley on this same date in 1882. Two Linton men, 77 years apart, united in nought. Week in summary Three ducks from two matches, all shouldered by the 1st XI, and all three victims caught, bowled or otherwise dismissed without so much as troubling the scorer — a clean sweep for the bowlers, a triumph through adversity for the club's honours boards. 🦆 Duck Club Dispatch, 6th to 7th June 1959

2 ducks
Week 6 · 6 Jun 1959 – 7 Jun 1959
Two fixtures on the books this weekend, and the exclusive zero club held its ceremony at just one of them, Tilling Steven away, where the 1st XI queue formed early and often. 1st XI, away to Tilling Steven Brian Mills, promoted to first drop, made scarcely more of his innings than the walk out and back, bowled by F- Baker for his 3rd duck of the season and 3rd of a still-young senior career, 5 innings in and already 71st of 716 on the all-time list. A long-standing member of the Debutante Duck club too, his very first Linton innings some seasons back also brought nought, so today's effort felt almost like tradition reasserting itself. On this very date in 1903, George Champion (1886 to 1912, Duck of the Year 1897) was doing exactly the same thing against Town Malling CC, proof that some anniversaries keep themselves without any help. At number 8, Roy Clarke joined the returning-early queue moments later, also undone by F- Baker, also bowled, for his 4th duck of the season and 11th of an increasingly decorated career, good enough for 16th of 716 all time. Roy currently holds the reins of Duck of the Year 1959 and shows no urgency to relinquish them, and remains one half of "Quacking Together" alongside club stalwart John Ames, though Ames kept his boots dry this time round. A chip off the old block too, with sibling H Clarke a fellow member of the club on a career duck of his own. Roy shares his on-this-day company with Brian, the very same George Champion also walking back for nought on this exact date in 1903. Two batsmen, one bowler, one long walk back twice over. F- Baker will have enjoyed his afternoon considerably more than the top order did. Week in brief Two matches, two ducks, both from the same fixture. The second match of the weekend passed entirely without incident, a rare outbreak of competence from all concerned. Both victims fell to the same bowler in the same innings, which is either very good bowling or very bad luck depending which dressing room is asked. 4 ducks
