The Duck Club Gazette

2 ducks
Week 6 · 20 Jul 1881
A record of ciphers for the week ending the 20th of July, 1881 1st XI Two members of our eleven were sent back without troubling the scorers in the match at home to Boxley CC, and by a curious chance both bore the same surname, though we are given no cause to make more of that than the coincidence itself allows. J Sedgwick, in at number nine, was bowled by C Chambers, and thereby entered his second duck of the season and the second of his career in as many completed innings, a consistency that keeps him a comfortable 17th of 99 on the club's all-time roll of the dismissed. He remains, for the present, in possession of the Duck of the Year honour for 1881, a distinction he appears determined to defend rather than surrender. We note, not without a certain wonder at the calendar's sense of humour, that on this very day in 1869 one C Amies performed an identical service against Horsmonden CC. G Sedgwick, opening the innings, was run out, the identity of the fielder responsible having escaped the scorer's pencil, and so departed for his second duck of the season, his career figures now reading two ciphers from three innings, placing him 14th of 99 in the club's long and dishonourable memory. He too may draw whatever comfort is on offer from the fact that C Amies, on this same date in 1869, was likewise unable to trouble the scorers. Week in summary One match, one innings begun and ended in disappointment at both its head and its tail, and two ducks laid to the club's account. A modest week's work, but the ledger does not discriminate between the grand failure and the small one, and both Messrs Sedgwick have done their part to keep it filled. Duck Hunting Season leaderboard - C Fryer — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100% - J Sedgwick — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100% - G Sedgwick — 3 innings, 2 ducks, 66.67% - J Mallard — 4 innings, 2 ducks, 50% - F Danells — 6 innings, 2 ducks, 33.33% A closely fought table at its head, and no sign yet of any gentleman inclined to trouble it by scoring a run. Members are cordially reminded that the next fixture offers every prospect of fresh additions to this distinguished company, and the club awaits its candidates with its customary patience.

The LPCC Duck Club Gazette — a Chronicle of Ducks' Eggs, 6th July 1881

4 ducks
Week 4 · 6 Jul 1881
Our correspondent is pleased to report a lively afternoon's cricket against Collier Street CC, in the course of which the eleven contributed no fewer than four contributions to the exclusive zero club. A dubious distinction indeed, and one borne with the customary good grace. 1st XI Mr G Sedgwick opened proceedings in this unhappy line by falling to F Laurence's bowling, bowled, in what we are given to understand was his very first innings for the club — an arrival marked, alas, by a cipher rather than a run. He stands 22nd of 95 in the club's melancholy all-time list, and it may interest readers that on this very day in 1870, no fewer than seven of the old brigade — Messrs W Goad, T Goad, J C Crawford, A Startup, C Amies, H Freed and W White — were themselves sent back to the pavilion without troubling the scorer, against Sissinghurst CC. A fine anniversary for the art of not scoring. Mr F Danells followed, caught T B Jackson off the same F Laurence, his second duck of the season and his second of his career in six innings at the wicket — he now occupies 11th place of 95 in the honours board of failure, a position secured, one might say, through consistency of a very particular kind. Mr J Sedgwick, brother in arms if not in scorebook to Mr G Sedgwick, likewise made his bow for the club and was caught Jackson, bowled Laurence, without scoring — his maiden innings yielding a maiden duck, and with it immediate elevation to the season's Duck of the Year honours for 1881. A debut to remember, if not quite in the manner one would wish. Mr Ernest Cruttenden completed the quartet, caught F Laurence off H Cranham, his first duck of the season and, in six innings at the crease, his first career nought — placing him 19th of 95 on the club's roll of dubious distinction, level with a considerable company of gentlemen similarly acquainted with the art of departing empty-handed. The Week in Summary One match, one innings, four ducks — a full house for Mr F Laurence, who accounted for three of the four dismissals himself, and a testing afternoon all round for the home eleven. No golden ducks were recorded, each gentleman having troubled the bowler for at least a stroke before his dismissal, which the correspondent supposes counts as triumph through adversity of a modest kind. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - C Fryer — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100% - J Mallard — 4 innings, 2 ducks, 50% - F Danells — 6 innings, 2 ducks, 33.33% - W H Fryer — 6 innings, 2 ducks, 33.33% - J Sedgwick — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% The eleven take the field again shortly, and the correspondent has every confidence that the willow will continue to fail our men at the moment of truth. Members are cordially invited to attend and, should fortune desire it, to add their own names to the roll.

The Duck Club Chronicle — 22nd June, 1881

3 ducks
Week 2 · 22 Jun 1881
A single fixture engaged our attentions this week, our first eleven away to Boxley CC, and the willow proved a poor friend to three of our number, each returning to the pavilion with a duck's egg against his name. The First Eleven, away to Boxley CC - W H Fryer, at the fourth wicket, was caught by C W Battiscombe off the bowling of Kenneth McAlpine. This is his season's second cipher, and his third in a career of twelve innings, placing him seventh of ninety in the club's roll of dubious distinction — a respectable, if unenviable, standing. He now keeps company with A Startup, of the 1868 to 1870 vintage, who sits on the identical figure of three, though that gentleman additionally holds the Duck of the Year honour in both 1868 and 1870, and a string of five ducks in a row besides — company enough to be modest about. - X Carter, sent in at number eight, was bowled by C Chambers, and does so on his arrival among the club's ranks — a debut of the most particular sort, the timbers disturbed before any real acquaintance with the bowling could be made. It is his first duck for the club, and he joins E M Owens, who played between 1869 and 1875, on a single career duck apiece, Owens presently occupying the sixteenth position of ninety. Mr Carter must hope his second visit to the crease proves a longer one. - J Mallard, last man but one at number ten, was caught by C W Battiscombe off C Chambers, the same bowler who accounted for Mr Carter — Chambers may fairly claim to have enjoyed the better of the afternoon. This is Mallard's second duck of the season and his second in a career of four innings, the fourteenth of ninety on the club's honours board. He draws level with C French Snr, of 1860 to 1864, who holds two career ducks and the Duck of the Year distinction for 1864. In summary, three of our batsmen failed to trouble the scorer in the one match played, and it may be observed that Mr C Chambers's bowling accounted for two of the three, while Mr Battiscombe's safe hands at the wicket were twice called upon. A modest but instructive afternoon for the art of not scoring. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - C Fryer — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100 per cent - J Mallard — 4 innings, 2 ducks, 50 per cent - W H Fryer — 4 innings, 2 ducks, 50 per cent - W White — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100 per cent - W Eggar — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50 per cent The club awaits its next fixture with due anticipation, confident that further additions to this ledger of ciphers will not long be wanting.

The LPCC Duck Club Gazette — a Chronicle of the Willow's Sterner Disappointments, 15th June 1881

8 ducks
Week 1 · 15 Jun 1881
Our correspondent is pleased, in the peculiar way one is pleased by such things, to report a thoroughly productive afternoon against Collier Street CC — eight ciphers were recorded, an innings return that will not soon be forgotten by those who suffered it. The First Eleven F Danells opened proceedings at number four, bowled by C Martin without registering a run — a first appearance for the club and, by the same stroke, a first entry in the ledger of nought. He sits now level upon a single career duck with a goodly company of former members, E M Owens among them. C Fryer, coming in at five, was likewise bowled by C Martin for a debut cipher — and, the eleven having a second innings to offer, returned again to be bowled once more by the same hand for nought. A pair, then, on debut no less, which the correspondent is bound to record as a distinction of the most unenviable sort. Mr Fryer's two ducks now draw him level with W H Fryer's career tally of two, the latter himself among the fallen this day. W Wilson, at number seven, went the way of Danells and Fryer, bowled by C Martin, his maiden failure of the season and first career duck in three innings at the wicket. W Eggar, opening at number two, was also accounted for by C Martin without scoring, his first innings' acquaintance with the game concluding at once in a duck — a debut he will doubtless prefer not to dwell upon, and he too joins the same populous company at one career cipher. J Mallard, batting nine, was caught by E Pettett off the bowling of H Cranham for nought, another debutant undone, and finds himself in the identical fraternity of single-duck men. W H Fryer, at ten, fell to H Cranham without scoring, his second career duck from ten innings, and joins C Fryer, C French Snr and sundry other names of seasons past upon that particular rung of the table. W White, closing the innings at number eleven, was likewise bowled by H Cranham for nought — his fourth career duck, placing him fourth of all who have ever failed to trouble the scorer for this club, and a paid-up member of the honours board for Duck of the Year 1869. He now stands level with C Amies on four apiece. The correspondent notes with some solemnity the case of Mr C Fryer, whose two failures this day at the same fixture constitute what the club's records term simply a pair — a debut and its unhappy sequel, achieved within the compass of a single afternoon. A Summary of the Day's Proceedings Eight batsmen back to the pavilion without score, from a single fixture against Collier Street CC — a display of collective restraint from the willow that the bowling of Messrs Martin and Cranham did much to encourage, the former accounting for four of our number and the latter three, with one further victim to the safe hands of the field. Whether this be misfortune, difficult wickets, or simply a day when the runs declined to come, the correspondent leaves to wiser judges. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - C Fryer — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100 per cent - W White — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100 per cent - F Danells — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50 per cent - J Mallard — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50 per cent - W Eggar — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50 per cent The correspondent commends these gentlemen to the attention of the membership, and looks forward, with the customary mixture of dread and anticipation, to the next fixture's inevitable additions to the roll.

1875 Season 1 report

The Duck Club Gazette — for the week ending the 30th of June, 1875

1 duck
Week 1 · 30 Jun 1875
A quiet week for the willow, correspondents will note, with but a single fixture played and a single name added to the club's roll of honour. Yet where the eleven is concerned, quality has ever mattered more than quantity, and this week's entrant is worthy of note. The First Eleven - M A Atkins, opening the batting against Marden CC of Kent at home on the 30th instant, was undone by the bowling of A Foreman and returned to the pavilion for a cipher. It is his first blemish of the current season, and but the second occasion in five visits to the crease upon which he has failed to trouble the scorer, leaving him placed 24th of the 79 gentlemen who make up the club's honours board. It may be observed that Mr Atkins stands presently a contender for the season's Duck of the Year, this being but his opening entry toward that distinction for 1875, and one imagines he shall not welcome further additions to the tally before the season is out. A curious point of history attends the date, for on this very day in 1868 one J Amies likewise walked back for nought, upon that occasion against Frittenden CC, the third-placed name upon the club's all-time roll with four such disappointments to his credit. Whether the coincidence of date shall prove an omen, the correspondent leaves to wiser heads than his own. The Week in Summary One fixture, one wicket surrendered without score, and thus a week that shall trouble the club's chroniclers but lightly. Still, a single duck's egg is not to be dismissed, and Mr Atkins may take some comfort that he keeps distinguished company on this particular anniversary. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - M A Atkins — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100 per cent The correspondent shall await with interest the next fixture, in the sincere hope, or perhaps the sincere doubt, that further gentlemen of the eleven shall be moved to add their names to the club's ever-growing roll of dubious distinction.

1873 Season 1 report

The Duck Report — 23rd July 1873

4 ducks
Week 1 · 23 Jul 1873
🏏 A single fixture upon the fields this week, and Cranbrook CC's bowling proved altogether too searching for four of our number, who file into the Ledger of the Nought in varying states of ceremony. 1st XI — v Cranbrook CC (home) - F Warde opened proceedings in the most inauspicious fashion imaginable, dismissed lbw to X Marshall for his first duck of a debut innings, then, called upon again in the same fixture, was stumped by X Dyke off X Dunk for a second — a full pair on debut, no less, the sternest possible welcome to the crease, and enrolment straightway upon the Duck of the Year 1873 honours. He stands 10th of 73 in the club's all-time ledger of ducks, level now upon two with a small fraternity that includes C French Snr, E Skinner and F Daniels. - H Freed, batting at seven, was bowled by X Marshall without scoring — his second career duck in but three innings, and 11th of 73 upon the all-time list. He now sits level upon two career ducks with the aforementioned company, Mr Warde among them. - J T Amies, opening the innings, was likewise bowled by X Marshall for nought — his first duck in eight innings of trying, placing him 20th of 73. He joins a considerable gathering level on a single career duck, among them E M Owens, E Price and the estimable J Woollett, the latter himself a Duck of the Year laureate of 1865. Curiously, upon this very date in 1867, both R J Bennett and W Goad were each sent back for nought against Staplehurst CC — a pleasing coincidence of the calendar, six years apart almost to the day, and the pattern each of this week's duckers shares. Week in summary: four ducks from a single match, all falling to the bowling of X Marshall save Mr Warde's second, and all in the home eleven's showing against Cranbrook. Mr Warde's full pair is the week's chief curiosity — a gentleman twice walked to the wicket and twice walked straight back, a feat of consistency few would care to repeat. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - F Warde — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100% - H Freed — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - J T Amies — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% The willow awaits its next victims at the coming fixture, and the club's exclusive zero club stands ever ready to receive fresh membership. Until then, gentlemen — mind the timbers.

1872 Season 1 report

THE LINTON PARK DUCK CLUB GAZETTE

6 ducks
Week 1 · 26 Jun 1872
A record of the willow's failures, the match of the 26th of June, 1872, against Sutton Valence Cricket Club The First Eleven Six of our men were sent back to the pavilion without troubling the scorer this day, and the exclusive zero club welcomes its newest and most industrious members. Mr E Skinner opened proceedings in the most modest fashion imaginable, lbw to the bowling of T Jordan for a nought upon his very first appearance for the Club — a debut few gentlemen would choose to remember, yet one for which the honours board shall now forever answer. Not content with a single cipher, he returned to the crease later in the day only to be run out for nought once more, thereby completing what we style, in the decorous language of this Club, a pair — two ducks laid in the one match, a feat of consistency his correspondent hesitates to call triumphant. He stands eighth of our sixty-nine upon the all-time roll, and holds the season's own Duck of the Year honour for 1872, a distinction he has this day done a great deal to secure. On his first blemish he kept company with Mr E M Owens, similarly becalmed at one; on his second he drew level with Mr C French Snr, whose own brace of ciphers earned that same honour as long ago as 1864. Mr W Goad, caught and bowled by the same Mr Jordan, added a fifth duck to a career already sixteen innings long, and sits, not without a certain grim distinction, at the very head of the Club's all-time list. His brother Mr T Goad is himself a member of good standing, with one cipher to his name, so the failing may fairly be said to run in the family, if not on this particular afternoon. Mr X Bowles was bowled by Mr Jordan for nought, the first blemish of a three-innings career, and joins Mr Owens upon a single such duck, thirty-second of sixty-nine. Mr L Barker, caught by F Edmed off Mr Jordan's bowling, recorded a duck upon his own debut for the Club, and finds himself twenty-first of sixty-nine, in the same modest company as Mr Owens. Mr S Woollett completed the collapse, bowled by J Thurston, for the first blemish of a five-innings career, and he too joins Mr Owens at a single cipher, twenty-fourth of sixty-nine. The Week in Brief Six ciphers from a single match is industry indeed, and the greater share of the credit, if credit is the word, belongs to Mr T Jordan of Sutton Valence, who accounted for four of our six by his own hand, Mr Thurston and a run out dividing the remainder between them. Mr Skinner's pair upon his first outing must stand as the day's chief curiosity, a debut that will be spoken of, one suspects, rather longer than he would wish. Duck Hunting Season — the Standings - E Skinner — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100 per cent - L Barker — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50 per cent - S Woollett — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50 per cent - W Goad — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50 per cent - X Bowles — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50 per cent The Club looks forward, with its customary mixture of dread and anticipation, to the next fixture, at which further candidates for the honours board may confidently be expected to present themselves.

1870 Season 1 report

The Duck Gazette — Wednesday, the 6th of July, 1870

7 ducks
Week 1 · 6 Jul 1870
Our correspondent is obliged to report a determined showing for the exclusive zero club this week, no fewer than seven of the eleven's men submitting themselves for enrolment in a single afternoon against Sissinghurst CC. The First Eleven, at Sissinghurst J C Crawford, opening the innings, was bowled by W Winch without troubling the scorer — his first career cipher in three innings, joining the estimable E M Owens, tenth upon the club's roll of sixty-three. A Startup followed at first wicket down, likewise done by Winch, for his third duck in a career of seven innings. A gentleman twice already decorated Duck of the Year, in 1868 and again this present season, and no stranger to a run of five such episodes in succession upon the honours board, he now stands level with T Tomson at three apiece. C Amies, at four, was smartly taken by X Goldsmith off Winch's bowling for his fourth career duck in nine innings — a return placing him first of the whole sixty-three, a distinction not lightly won. He keeps company with J Amies, second upon that same list, at four apiece. W Goad, at five, fell to W Piper for his fourth career duck in fourteen innings, third of sixty-three and close upon the summit — a family affair, as our next item will relate. H Freed, at seven, was likewise accounted for by Piper, a cipher to mark his very arrival at the wicket, and he joins Mr Owens upon a single career duck. W White, at nine, went the same way for his third career duck in four innings, sixth of sixty-three and himself a Duck of the Year for 1869 — he now stands level with Mr Startup at three. T Goad, last man in, was bowled by Winch without scoring, a cipher on only his second appearance for the eleven, joining Mr Owens on a single career duck — the second Goad to fall this same afternoon, as follows. Two of a Quack The rarest ceremony of the day fell to the Goad household, W and T both walking back without a run against Sissinghurst CC, a shared misfortune the honours board records under that particular heading. The elder's was his fourth such episode, the younger's his very first — a duck to begin a career, and a fourth to continue one. The Week in Brief Seven ciphers from a single afternoon is a determined showing indeed, with no golden ducks among them and the Goad family alone accounting for two of the seven. Sissinghurst's bowling was shared between Winch, four wickets for nought, and Piper, three for the same. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - A Startup — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% - C Amies — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% - H Freed — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% - J C Crawford — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% - T Goad — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% The eleven take the field again shortly, and our correspondent has every confidence the honours board will not want for fresh entries.

1869 Season 3 reports

The Duck Report — 4th August 1869

4 ducks
Week 4 · 4 Aug 1869
A single fixture graced the calendar this week, and Horsmonden CC proved unkind hosts, our eleven leaving no fewer than four gentlemen to make the long walk back for a cipher. 1st XI W H Fryer, at the wicket in the number five position, was taken by A Napean off the bowling of Sir F S Marriott, and returns to the pavilion with his season's account opened at one, and his career log reading a first duck's egg in seven completed innings — a modest total that places him twenty-fifth of the sixty-one gentlemen who share this dubious distinction. He may take some comfort, if comfort be wanted, in the knowledge that he stands level on a single career cipher with a full company of members, among them Mr J Woollett, himself a bearer of the Duck of the Year honour for 1865. W Goad, sent in at six, fell to a smart catch by T Lambert, again off Sir F S Marriott's bowling, and thereby notches his third career duck in a dozen innings, and his first of the present season — a showing that carries him to fourth upon the all-time roll of honour, level in tally with Mr C Amies, second upon that same list, a fellow traveller in the art of not scoring. Following him to the crease and swiftly following him back was X Plomley, whose very first innings for the club ended leg-before to the bowling of G Sawyer without so much as a run to his name. A debut duck is a peculiar christening, but a christening nonetheless, and Mr Plomley now shares his solitary career cipher with a considerable fraternity, Mr Fryer among them. Last of the day's unfortunates was J Amies, bowled by A Napean at number nine, his second duck of the current season and his fourth for the career in nine innings — a record that stands, remarkably, at the very head of the club's all-time table, first of sixty-one. No comparison was drawn for Mr Amies this week, his eminence in this particular field being, it seems, beyond parallel. In summary Four gentlemen dismissed without troubling the scorer in the one match of the period, Horsmonden's bowlers Sir F S Marriott and A Napean each claiming two victims apiece, and G Sawyer accounting for a third. A tidy afternoon's work for the visitors' attack, and a chastening one for our lower order. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - W White — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100% - C Amies — 3 innings, 2 ducks, 66.67% - J Amies — 4 innings, 2 ducks, 50% - E M Owens — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - X Plomley — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% The club awaits the next fixture with its customary mixture of dread and delight, confident that further candidates for the exclusive zero club shall not be long in presenting themselves.

The LPCC Duck Club Gazette — an Account of the Twentieth of July, 1869

3 ducks
Week 2 · 20 Jul 1869
A single fixture against Horsmonden CC furnished the Club with three additions to its roll of honour this week, the eleven's order finding the art of not scoring far from beyond its powers. The First Eleven - Mr C Amies, promoted to the crease at number two, was caught by W Sawyer off the bowling of R Wilson without troubling the scorer — his second cipher of the season and his third in a career of seven innings. This places him, with a certain grim distinction, at the very head of the Club's all-time table of ducks, first of seven-and-fifty names now inscribed there. He is joined, and not displaced, by Mr J Amies, whose own three ducks between 1867 and 1869 hold him steady in second place — two tallies alike, and neither gentleman about to yield the honour to the other. - Mr E M Owens, at first drop and at the very first asking of his career, was run out for nought. A debut of the most economical kind, it stands as his maiden innings and his maiden duck in the same stroke, and installs him tenth of seven-and-fifty in the Club's ledger. He finds companionship in Mr E Price, another single-duck man of the years 1860 to 1864, presently eleventh upon the same list. - Mr G Hodsoll, sent in at number ten, was caught by H Ford off the bowling of H Burr — his first duck of the season, and the first of his career in three innings attempted thus far, earning him thirteenth place of seven-and-fifty. He shares his solitary tally, curiously enough, with the very Mr Owens named above — two gentlemen, one duck apiece, standing tenth and thirteenth together upon the same roll this very afternoon. A Word on the Week Three ducks from a single match is no mean haul, and the innings ran the full width of the batting order, from number two to number ten, sparing nobody's blushes. No pair of ducks was recorded this week, and no family party presented itself for joint ignominy — a quieter week than some, but a productive one nonetheless. The Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - W White — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100 per cent - C Amies — 3 innings, 2 ducks, 66.67 per cent - E M Owens — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100 per cent - G Hodsoll — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100 per cent - H Kemp — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50 per cent Mr White retains his commanding, if unenviable, lead at the head of the season's table, having yet to trouble the scorer in either innings offered him this year. The Club looks forward, as ever, to the next fixture, confident that further names shall present themselves for inclusion in due course.

The LPCC Duck Club Gazette — a Chronicle of Ciphers, 10th July 1869

9 ducks
Week 1 · 10 Jul 1869
Our correspondent is pleased, in a manner appropriate to the sad business at hand, to report upon the eleven's visit to Hayle Place, where no fewer than nine of our men returned to the pavilion without so much as troubling the scorer. A rare and thorough afternoon's work for the opposing bowlers. 1st XI - J Amies, at number four, was caught by H Freed off the bowling of F Swift, and thereby notches his first duck's egg of the season, the third of a career now numbering seven innings. He joins T Tomson, of the years 1864 to 1868, upon an identical career tally of three — a fellowship separated by half a decade but united in the art of not scoring. - A Startup fell bowled by F Swift, his season's first, his career's second in a mere three innings, and a name already inscribed upon the honours board for the Duck of the Year 1868 and for Ducks in a Row, five consecutive. He draws level upon two career ciphers with C Amies, of whom more directly below. - H Kemp, at number eight, was bowled by F Swift and thereby opens his account with the club in the most inauspicious manner conceivable — his maiden first-class duck, the first of his career, in only his second innings. He stands presently level upon one career duck with E Price of the 1860s. - W White, first innings, was caught by L Barker off H Freed — his maiden duck, taken in only his second innings for the club, and inscribed already upon the honours roll for Duck of the Year 1869. Level for the moment upon one career cipher with E Price. - X Griffin, last man in, was run out without troubling the scorer — his maiden duck, his second innings, and level upon one career duck with E Price and companions. - C Amies was bowled by H Freed at the top of the order, his season's first, his career's second in six innings, level with A Startup upon that same tally of two. - M Barker, batting seventh, fell caught H Freed bowled A Tyrell, his maiden duck in his second innings, level upon one with the aforementioned E Price. - T Bonny, at nine, was likewise caught H Freed bowled A Tyrell, his maiden duck in his second innings, level upon one with E Price and the growing company thereabouts. - And W White again — stumped, this time, by George Marsham off A Tyrell in the same fixture, a second dismissal without score that completes what the club records term simply a pair. Two ducks in one afternoon's cricket is a distinction few young careers achieve so promptly, and W White has managed it in only his second innings, taking his season's tally to two and his career tally to two at a stroke. A remarkable beginning, if not quite the one a batsman hopes to relate to his grandchildren. The Week in Summary One match, nine ducks — a positively epidemic afternoon at Hayle Place, and the visiting eleven may reflect that Messrs Swift, Freed and Tyrell bowled with rather more success than our batting order cared to acknowledge. Four of our number recorded their maiden career ducks in this single fixture, a debut season already showing considerable early promise in the wrong direction entirely. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. W White — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100% 2. A Startup — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% 3. C Amies — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% 4. H Kemp — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% 5. J Amies — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% The season is yet young, and the club looks forward with its customary mixture of dread and delight to the next fixture, when further candidates shall no doubt present themselves for the honours board. Our men are cordially reminded that the willow is intended for striking the leather, not merely admiring it.

1868 Season 1 report

The Duck Club Gazette — the Match of the 30th of June, 1868

4 ducks
Week 1 · 30 Jun 1868
Frittenden CC paid a visit to Linton Park on Saturday last and made unusually free with our batting order, escorting no fewer than four of our number back to the pavilion without troubling the scorer. He now sits level with the venerable C French Snr, whose own pair of career ducks between 1860 and 1864 earned him the Duck of the Year honour for 1864 — respectable company in which to find oneself. - C Amies followed not long after, undone by F Still for his maiden nought of the campaign, the first blemish upon a young record of four innings and good enough for eighth place on the all-time list. He arrives upon the Club's books already carrying the Duck of the Year 1868 board and a place among the Ducks in a Row (five consecutive), honours his solitary innings to date has been sufficient to secure. His tally of one duck stands level with that of C Amies. - T Tomson, last man in at number ten, was caught and bowled by A Levett for his third career duck in five innings — a return sufficient to place him first of all eight-and-forty names on the Club's all-time roll, a position he holds at present without rival. In summary Four ducks fell to a single fixture, three of the four to the persistent A Levett, who might fairly be said to have done the honours-board keeper's work for him this week. A patient afternoon for the scorers and a busy one at the pavilion gate. The Club awaits the next fixture with quiet confidence that Frittenden, or whichever eleven follows, will furnish further ciphers for the ledger.

1867 Season 3 reports

The LPCC Duck Club Gazette

1 duck
Week 5 · 12 Aug 1867
A Chronicle of Ciphers — the 12th of August, 1867 1st XI A single name is entered upon the roll this week, and let it be recorded with all due ceremony. Mr G A K Simpson, sent in at number ten against the First Innings of Leeds Park CC upon home ground, was undone by the combination of J C Crawford's bowling and W Roper's safe hands in the field, departing caught for nought. That this was his very first innings for the club renders the achievement the more remarkable — few gentlemen manage to inaugurate a career with quite such economy of effort, and the Duck Club is pleased to welcome him to its exclusive and ever-lengthening roll, in which his single cipher already secures him eighth place among forty-three names so honoured. In this distinction he is not alone in history. One E Price, who turned out for the eleven between 1860 and 1864, likewise retired upon a single duck across three innings, and rests to this day sixth upon the very same roll. Mr Simpson may take what comfort he can in such distinguished, if scoreless, company. The Week in Brief One match, one innings of note, one gentleman sent back to the pavilion without troubling the scorer. A quiet week for the timbers, all told, though the season's ledger continues to swell by modest increments, as these things do. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - J Simpson — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100% - T Tomson — 3 innings, 2 ducks, 66.7% - G A K Simpson — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% - R J Bennett — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% - T Philpott — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% The correspondent notes with interest that Mr J Simpson stands at a perfect record of failure this season, a feat of consistency that must surely be admired even as it is regretted. The eleven take the field again presently, and the Gazette has every confidence that fresh material for these columns will not be long in arriving. The LPCC Duck Club Gazette — Tuesday, 23rd July 1867

2 ducks
Week 2 · 23 Jul 1867
🏏 A modest fixture against Staplehurst CC this week, but the exclusive zero club is never long without new correspondence, and two of our number have duly written themselves in. 1st XI - R J Bennett, sent in at number seven, was bowled by J Orpin without registering a run, and thereby opens his account with the club — his maiden innings, and a maiden duck to mark it, which is one way of making an entrance. It is his 1st duck of the season and the 1st of his career from 2 innings, placing him 11th of 39 on the all-time roll of dubious distinction. He now sits level with a whole company of gentlemen on a single career cipher, among them J Woollett, himself Duck of the Year in 1865 — modest company, but company all the same. - W Goad, at number five, was bowled by S H Burden for nought, his 1st duck of this season but his 2nd for the career, from 5 innings all told, and he rises to 5th of 39 on the club's melancholy ledger. In this he draws level with C French Snr, who claimed the Duck of the Year honour in 1864 on the very same tally — proof, if proof were needed, that two ducks in a career is no bar to distinguished company. The Week in Summary A brief but productive afternoon for the timbers: two of our batsmen dismissed without scoring, both at Staplehurst, both bowled rather than caught or run out — a clean sweep for the bowlers, and a fresh entry apiece in the honours book. No pairs, no golden ducks, and no family affairs to report this week, the ignominy being confined to individual endeavour. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard 1. J Simpson — 2 ducks in 2 innings (100%) 2. T Tomson — 2 ducks in 2 innings (100%) 3. R J Bennett — 1 duck in 2 innings (50%) 4. T Philpott — 1 duck in 2 innings (50%) 5. J Amies — 1 duck in 4 innings (25%) The season standings remain keenly contested at the summit, with Messrs Simpson and Tomson yet to trouble the scorer on a single occasion this year — a perfect record, of its kind. We look ahead with quiet confidence to the next fixture, at which the club's honours board may well be further enriched. Members are reminded that the art of not scoring requires no practice whatsoever, and the timbers stand ready to receive all comers.

The Duck Club Gazette — a Report of the Willow's Failures, 17th July 1867

7 ducks
Week 1 · 17 Jul 1867
Our correspondent takes up his pen to record a melancholy but instructive afternoon against Leeds Park CC, in which the eleven contributed no fewer than seven ducks' eggs to the ledger from a single innings — a showing that will not soon be forgotten by those concerned. 1st XI T Gandy opened proceedings by being bowled by J C Crawford, his first duck of the season and the first of his career in four completed innings, placing him tenth of the four-and-thirty gentlemen who maintain residence in the club's rolls of dubious distinction. He joins E Price, whose own solitary duck was recorded some seasons past, on a tally of one apiece. J Amies, appearing in only his second innings for the club, was run out without troubling the scorer — a debut duck in the fullest sense, and a sobering welcome to the exclusive zero club. He too sits level with Mr Price on a single career cipher. T Tomson was twice dismissed by F F Crawford's bowling in the course of the day's play, first for a plain nought and then, later in the same fixture, for a second — a grim pair, and his second and now his career-defining feature, standing at two ducks from three innings. In this unhappy symmetry he draws level with C French Snr, whose two ducks earned him the Duck of the Year honour in 1864, and with F Daniels, similarly garlanded in 1860. J Simpson, likewise in only his second innings for the club, contrived the same feat as Mr Tomson — run out twice in the one match, for his first and second ducks of the season and of his career alike. Mr Simpson carries the singular distinction of Duck of the Year 1867 already inscribed to his name, a laurel earned in short order indeed, and now finds himself level with Mr Tomson, Mr French and Mr Daniels on two apiece. T Philpott, run out for his solitary contribution, brings his career tally to one duck in four innings, twelfth upon the honours list, and joins the same gathering of single-duck gentlemen as Mr Gandy and Mr Amies. A Summary of the Day's Misfortunes Seven ducks were recorded in the one fixture against Leeds Park CC — a showing of consistency, if nothing else, and proof once again that the art of not scoring remains alive and well at Linton Park. Two of our number, Messrs Tomson and Simpson, achieved the rare distinction of a pair apiece, each managing to be dismissed twice without the inconvenience of scoring, though neither quite achieved the golden ignominy of a king pair — some small mercy was shown them by the bowling, if not by fortune. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - J Simpson — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100% - T Tomson — 2 innings, 2 ducks, 100% - J Amies — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% - T Gandy — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% - T Philpott — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50% The season stands but young, yet already a keen contest for the wooden spoon is under way. Members are respectfully reminded that the next fixture offers every opportunity for further additions to this distinguished roll, and the correspondent awaits the outcome with his customary mixture of dread and delight.

1865 Season 1 report

The Duck Club Gazette — Report for the 12th of June, 1865

2 ducks
Week 1 · 12 Jun 1865
A single fixture at Yalding brought the eleven no great fortune with the willow, and the timbers were troubled twice for a cipher apiece. Let us proceed to the melancholy particulars. 1st XI In the first innings against Yalding United, our men found the going hard at the tail. W Crittenden, sent in at number ten, was bowled by R Lipscombe without registering a run — his first duck of the season, and the third of his short career across three innings. He now stands eighth of eight-and-twenty in the club's roll of dubious distinction, a modest but earnest contribution to the art of not scoring. He joins a small fraternity — E Price, F May, J Tompson, T M Dann and W Goad among them — all presently level with him on a single career duck apiece, kindred spirits in nought. Following hard upon his heels, J Woollett came in at number eleven and suffered precisely the same fate, bowled by the same R Lipscombe, for the same solitary blob. This is his first duck of the current season and his first in a career of three innings, placing him sixth of eight-and-twenty on the all-time list — no mean feat of consistency, and one that earns him standing as a paid-up holder of the Duck of the Year 1865 honour, a distinction his club colleagues will no doubt raise a glass to, whatever the state of his batting average. He too finds himself, for the moment, level on career ducks with the aforementioned gentlemen of the zero club. Two wickets, one bowler, one unhappy pattern — R Lipscombe may fairly claim to have found our tail end rather to his liking this particular afternoon. The Week in Summary A single match, a pair of ducks, and both credited to the same visiting bowler — Yalding United's R Lipscombe leaves Linton Park having accounted for our last two batsmen without either troubling the scorer. A tidy piece of work on his part, and a sobering one on ours. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard - J Woollett — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50.0% - W Crittenden — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50.0% A Closing Word The season stands young, and the leaderboard shows our two contributors locked at fifty per cent apiece — honours even, for now. The club looks forward with quiet confidence, or perhaps quiet dread, to the next fixture, when the timbers shall doubtless be rattled again and fresh names added to this most exclusive of registers. Until then, the eleven remain, as ever, your obedient servants of the duck's egg.

1864 Season 1 report

The Duck Club Gazette

5 ducks
Week 1 · 9 Jun 1864
A Chronicle of the Fixture of the 9th of June, 1864 Our First Eleven met Collier Street Cricket Club on the 9th instant, and in the course of a single innings contrived to send no fewer than five of its number to the pavilion for a cipher — a showing of most uncommon consistency, which the Recording Secretary sets down below with the solemnity it deserves. The First Eleven - Mr E Price, opening the innings, was adjudged leg-before to the bowling of Mr T Startup. It is his first duck's egg in three innings at the wicket, placing him third of nineteen upon the club's roll of the dismissed — level with Mr F May, his fellow traveller on a tally of one. - Mr W Goad, at first wicket down, was bowled by Mr G Hodges. As this was his maiden appearance for the club, his very first innings has ended without score — a debut duck, and a sombre christening indeed. He stands seventh of nineteen, drawing level with Mr E Price on career noughts. - Mr C French Snr fell to Mr T Startup for his second career duck in three innings, and by this the paper's records confirm him first of nineteen upon the all-time table, presently holding the honour of Duck of the Year for 1864 — a distinction he may wear, this season, with some ceremony. He sits level with a Mr F Daniels of an earlier generation, who himself claimed the same honour in 1860. - Mr F May likewise fell to Mr T Startup, his first duck in three innings, ranking him fourth of nineteen and, as with Mr Price above, keeping close company on a career tally of one. - Mr T M Dann, last man in, was bowled by Mr T Startup for nought upon his very first innings for the club — another debut duck, and sixth of nineteen upon the roll, level once more with Mr E Price. A Word on the Afternoon Five ducks from a single innings is no small return, and the bowling of Mr T Startup deserves particular mention, having accounted for four of the five himself — a spell of quite remarkable persistence against our order top to tail. Messrs Goad and Dann may take what comfort they can in having begun their careers as they mean to go on, while Mr French Snr now leads the club's roll of dishonour outright. Duck Hunting Season Leaderboard The season being but freshly begun, our five afflicted gentlemen stand shoulder to shoulder atop the table, each having faced one innings and returned one duck, a perfect century of failure: 1. C French Snr — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% 2. E Price — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% 3. F May — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% 4. T M Dann — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% 5. W Goad — 1 innings, 1 duck, 100% The Club awaits the next fixture with due anticipation, confident that further candidates shall present themselves for the exclusive zero club before the season is much older.

1860 Season 1 report

The Duck Gazette — the Match of the 31st of July, 1860

4 ducks
Week 1 · 31 Jul 1860
A single fixture occupied the eleven this week, the visit of Loose Cricket Club, and it yielded four ducks' eggs to the Club's ledger — no great multitude, but a notable one, for these are the very first entries upon our roll of dubious distinction. Friendly XI v Loose CC, played at home - J Tompson, at number six, was bowled by C Amies and returned to the pavilion without troubling the scorer. It is his first appearance in these pages, and he takes up the third position of the all-time table with a single egg to his name, keeping company there with C French Snr, who sits upon precisely the same tally. - F Daniels, at number seven, was bowled by Joseph Amies and thereby opened his account both for the season and for all time, claiming outright the leading position upon the club's roll. In the same stroke he is inaugurated into the Duck of the Year 1860 honours, a distinction that stands current for this very season. He is joined upon his tally of one by C French Snr, another gentleman new to the ledger. - C French Snr, first wicket down, fell to Joseph Amies without score, his debut innings for the Club securing him the second position of the all-time table, level in every particular with J Tompson. - F Daniels, called to the wicket a second time in the same fixture, was this occasion taken by C Childs off a bowler whose name the scorer did not think to preserve. He thereby completes a pair, two ducks in the one match, a grim if not unheard-of feat, and his figures advance to two for the season and two for his short career, his position at the head of the table undisturbed and his place among the Duck of the Year 1860 honours now doubly confirmed. The Week in Summary Four ducks from a single fixture is no mean return, and the distinction of contributing two of them belongs to Mr Daniels alone, whose pair rather sets the tone for a season only just begun. The eleven may reflect that three of its number departed without score inside a single afternoon, a circumstance the scorebook recorded with more regularity than enthusiasm. The Duck Hunting Season Table 1. F Daniels — 2 innings, 2 ducks, a full 100 per cent 2. C French Snr — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50 per cent 3. J Tompson — 2 innings, 1 duck, 50 per cent In Closing The Club's roll of honour, opened this very week, stands ready to receive whatever further entries the next fixture may furnish. Members are cordially invited to attend, and, should fortune so decree, to add their own names to the ledger of the willow's more modest triumphs.
